excerpt: Sobre el rolBuscamos un Backend Engineer hands-on responsable de diseñar, construir y operar servicios backend en producción dentro de un entorno AWS corporativo.
description:
Sobre el rol

Buscamos un Backend Engineer hands-on responsable de diseñar, construir y operar servicios backend en producción dentro de un entorno AWS corporativo. El eje del rol es el desarrollo backend sólido: APIs bien estructuradas, patrones de diseño aplicados, código seguro y auditable.

El candidato no será responsable del desarrollo frontend, pero sí debe asegurar que los servicios que construya estén correctamente diseñados para ser consumidos por aplicaciones en React/Next: estructuras de respuesta claras, validaciones, contratos de integración y manejo de errores.

La empresa opera bajo lineamientos corporativos estrictos: casa matriz audita el código, existen herramientas automáticas de verificación de calidad y seguridad antes de cada promoción entre ambientes. Se espera que el candidato llegue con buenas prácticas ya internalizadas no como algo a aprender en el trabajo.

Requirements


— Perfil profesional y soft skills —

PERFIL PROFESIONAL

Buscamos a alguien que:

  • Ha tenido responsabilidad directa sobre lo que construye
  • Puede explicar con claridad qué desarrolló, cómo funciona y por qué se diseñó así
  • Ha trabajado en contextos reales (producción, incidentes, presión, ambigüedad)
  • Puede tomar decisiones y avanzar sin depender constantemente de otros
  • Se comunica de forma clara, directa y estructurada

En entrevista, esperamos ver:

  • Explicaciones concretas, no teóricas
  • Forma de pensar estructurada
  • Capacidad de proponer soluciones reales


    — Perfil técnico — MAPA DE SKILLS
  • Indispensable (sin esto no avanza)
    • Backend hands-on en producción
    • APIs REST + seguridad
    • AWS aplicado en producción
    • Patrones de diseño
    • Código limpio y mantenible
    • IaC: conocimiento funcional (entender cómo funciona y cómo impacta el despliegue)
  • Flexible (puede compensar con potencial claro)
    • React / Next (nivel integración, no desarrollo profundo)
    • IaC: desarrollo directo (escribir desde cero)
    • Servicios avanzados de AWS
    • Experiencia en entornos altamente regulados
  • Nice to have
    • Certificación AWS
    • Experiencia en sector financiero
    • Experiencia en entornos corporativos auditados
    • Conocimiento de CI/CD (no ownership completo)


Primer Frente: — BACKEND—

No se requiere que hayas diseñado arquitecturas de empresa completas, pero sí que puedas construir componentes de forma autónoma, tomar decisiones técnicas fundamentadas y entender el impacto de tu código en el sistema completo. No se busca un arquitecto que delega, se busca alguien que ejecuta con criterio.

(Hands-on real)

  • Experiencia desarrollando APIs en producción (Node, Python, C#, Java)
  • Diseño de APIs REST (endpoints, validaciones, manejo de errores)
  • Implementación de autenticación/autorización (JWT, OAuth2 o similar)
  • Manejo de base de datos (SQL y/o NoSQL)
  • Experiencia real ejecutando (no solo diseñando o liderando)

Stack backend

  • C# (.Net) o Node.js o Python como lenguaje principal. No importa cuál, lo que importa es la profundidad.
  • Desarrollo de APIs REST: diseño de recursos, versionamiento, autenticación (JWT, OAuth2), autorización por roles.
  • Manejo de bases de datos relacionales (SQL) e idealmente alguna NoSQL. Queries optimizadas, transacciones, índices.
  • Manejo de errores robusto: respuestas consistentes, logging estructurado, trazabilidad.
  • Pruebas unitarias e integración: no solo saber que existen también saber escribirlas y mantenerlas.

Esperamos identificar en ti:

  • Facilidad para hablar de tus APIs con propiedad de producto: conoces el input, el output, los casos de error, quién lo consume y por qué se diseñó así.
  • Claridad para explicar paso a paso cómo construiste o modificarías un servicio real: desde la definición del endpoint hasta su despliegue en producción.
  • Agilidad cuando se te presenta un escenario técnico: daR una solución concreta sin evadir o desviar el caso.
  • Capacidad para reconoces trade-offs: saber cuándo usar una Lambda vs un contenedor, una BD relacional vs una NoSQL, y poder justificarlo.
  • Transparencia para compartir cuándo has tenido incidentes en producción y poder describir cómo los identificaste, atendiste y previenes.

Buenas prácticas — 'CÓDIGO LIMPIO'

Este punto es crítico. El código es evaluado automáticamente en cada promoción entre ambientes, por lo que es importante contar con buenas prácticas bien consolidadas desde el inicio.

Patrones de diseño — deberás conocer y saber aplicar al menos uno

  • Clean Architecture (también llamada Arquitectura Limpia): separación de capas, dependencias apuntando hacia adentro, dominio independiente de infraestructura.
  • Arquitectura en Capas (Layered / N-tier): presentación, negocio, datos — claramente separados.
  • Arquitectura de Cebolla (Onion Architecture): núcleo de dominio rodeado por capas concéntricas de adaptadores.

Clean code — lo que esperamos ver en tu forma de trabajar
Se espera que puedas explicar cómo estructuras tu código, cómo separas responsabilidades y cómo manejas errores en servicios reales, con ejemplos claros de lo que has construido.

  • Separación clara de responsabilidades: cada clase, función o módulo cumple un propósito específico.
  • Uso de nombres descriptivos que hagan el código fácil de entender sin necesidad de explicaciones adicionales.
  • Lógica de negocio ubicada en las capas correctas (servicios o dominio), no en controladores.
  • Código limpio y mantenible, evitando redundancias o elementos innecesarios.
  • Manejo explícito de errores, con control y trazabilidad adecuados.

Seguridad en código — requerida, no opcional

  • Validación de inputs en backend (no confiar en el frontend para validar).
  • Protección de endpoints: autenticación + autorización correctamente implementada.
  • No hardcodear credenciales, API keys ni secrets en el código — uso de variables de entorno o servicios como AWS Secrets Manager.
  • Conocimiento básico de OWASP Top 10: SQL injection, XSS, broken auth, etc.
  • Logging sin exponer datos sensibles (PII, tokens, passwords).


Segundo Frente: — CLOUD AWS —

AWS es un componente clave del rol.

Se espera experiencia real en producción y entendimiento de cómo el backend vive dentro de un entorno cloud, pero el enfoque principal sigue siendo backend.

Se espera capacidad de explicar cómo ha desplegado servicios, cómo se conectan entre sí y cómo su código impacta el entorno.

Importante que el candidato:

  • Haya trabajado con AWS en producción (no solo teoría)
  • Entienda cómo se despliegan servicios y se promueve código entre ambientes
  • Comprenda cómo su código impacta seguridad, despliegue y operación

Servicios con los que se espera experiencia práctica

  • Lambda: creación, configuración de triggers, conexión con otros servicios, manejo de timeouts y errores.
  • API Gateway: creación de APIs, integración con Lambda, manejo de stages y autorizadores.
  • S3: gestión de objetos, permisos, políticas de acceso, lifecycle rules.
  • DynamoDB o RDS: operaciones CRUD, índices, conexión desde servicios backend.
  • IAM: roles, políticas, principio de menor privilegio — sabe por qué importa y cómo aplicarlo.


    Infraestructura como Código (IaC) — conocimiento funcional obligatorio:
  • Entiende qué es y para qué sirve: no se crean recursos manualmente en consola.
  • Puede leer y entender una plantilla de CloudFormation o un módulo de CDK/Terraform aunque no sea su especialidad.
  • Sabe cómo se declara una Lambda, un API Gateway o un rol IAM en código.
  • Entiende el ciclo: escribir IaC → plan/preview → deploy controlado.


    Seguridad en nube — nivel esperado
    • Entiende buenas prácticas básicas de seguridad al trabajar en AWS

Sommaire du poste

Le gestionnaire de comptes (GC) est un poste au sein de l'équipe de l'expérience client, relevant du directeur des comptes stratégiques de son segment de marché. Le GC est le principal point de collaboration pour apporter de la valeur aux clients assignés. Le portefeuille de clients présente une complexité faible à moyenne. Le GC est la personne responsable de développer des relations solides, de fournir un soutien quotidien et d'apporter des perspectives techniques afin d'exécuter une stratégie de compte maximisant le rendement pour le client et pour Steritech.

Une partie essentielle de ce poste consiste à orchestrer la mise en œuvre des services, à assurer la qualité et la calibration des spécialistes évaluant les sites, à respecter les ententes sur les niveaux de service, ainsi qu’à communiquer et acheminer les problèmes aux instances supérieures lorsque nécessaire.

De plus, le gestionnaire de comptes doit posséder une compréhension approfondie du secteur des normes de marque (Brand Standards), des protocoles et procédures de Steritech, ainsi que des exigences spécifiques des marques clientes afin d'assurer un service de haut niveau et de faciliter une excellente communication entre Steritech et tous les paliers de l'organisation cliente.

Requirements

  • Planification : Exécuter les plans stratégiques incluant les cibles financières et les étapes critiques.
  • Analyse des besoins : Valider proactivement les besoins des clients pour ajouter de la valeur à leurs programmes.
  • Rapports : Soumettre les rapports hebdomadaires, mensuels et annuels requis.

Expérience et qualifications requises

excerpt: At Montera, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure.
description:
At Montera, we’re building the future of digital infrastructure. Founder-led with $1.5B backed by Stonepeak, Montera is driven by a future-focused vision: to develop and operate hyperscale data centers essential for tomorrow's technology. Our mission is to deliver strategically located, hyperscale data centers designed for speed, reliability, and scalability. Backed by decades of experience in design, construction, and operations, we don’t just build—we execute with purpose.

Our Values

  • Client First Alignment: We align every solution to our clients’ goals.
  • Speed with Certainty: Velocity matters. We deliver with urgency and precision.
  • Operational Excellence: Decades of experience drive our high standards.
  • Safety & Integrity: Safety is non-negotiable. We lead with integrity and transparency.
  • Ownership Mentality: We think like owners, because we are.

The Opportunity

Montera is seeking a Vice President Data Center Design leads the delivery of Montera’s facility designs across the portfolio. Reporting to the CTO, the VP owns design execution end to end — from reference architecture through IFC and construction support — and is the senior leader of Montera’s Principal Engineering & Architecture Leadership family and its external design and construction partners.

This is a people-leadership and delivery-accountability role, distinct from the CTO’s external technical and customer-facing mandate. The CTO owns customer requirements capture and is the technical external face of Montera; the VP converts those requirements into buildable, coordinated, on-schedule designs and drives them through the design and construction partner ecosystem (CSA, MEP, design-assist trades, GC/CM, and specialty consultants) to a predictable, commissioned outcome.

The VP manages the five Principal ICs — Architect & Master Planning, Electrical, Mechanical, Controls, and Network — aligning their reference architectures into a single coherent facility design, resolving cross-discipline conflicts, and holding the integrated design schedule and budget. The role is accountable for design quality, constructability, multi-discipline coordination, and the design inputs to cost, schedule, and availability targets across active projects (currently Eagle and Goldeneye) and the broader pipeline.

Requirements

What You'll Do

Design Delivery & Program Execution

  • Own end-to-end design delivery across the portfolio — concept, SD, DD, IFP/IFC, and construction-phase support — against committed schedule milestones (e.g., schematic design and IFC dates) and yield-on-cost targets.
  • Hold the integrated, multi-discipline design schedule and budget; drive the critical path across architectural, electrical, mechanical, controls, and network scopes.
  • Govern design change control, trade studies, and value-engineering decisions, protecting design intent, reliability targets (five-nines availability), and operability.
  • Own the design basis of design (BOD) and its consistent application across projects, and the design deliverables that feed permitting, procurement, and construction.

Leadership of the Principal Engineering & Architecture Family

  • Directly lead and develop the five Principal ICs (Architect/Master Planning, Electrical, Mechanical, Controls, Network); set objectives, review performance, and build the discipline centers of excellence.
  • Integrate discipline reference architectures into one coherent, coordinated facility design; arbitrate cross-discipline trade-offs (e.g., power vs. cooling vs. space, controls data model vs. network segmentation).
  • Ensure the Controls–Network interlock on customer data exposure is delivered jointly and coherently, consistent with the single-tenant model and the requirements the CTO captures.
  • Enforce portfolio-wide design standards, playbooks, and prototypical modules that enable rapid, repeatable deployment.

Design Contracts & Partner Governance

  • Define, review, negotiate, and manage design contracts with design partners (CSA and MEP engineers of record, design-assist trades, and specialty consultants) — owning scopes of work, deliverable schedules, standard of care, fee structures, and design responsibility matrices.
  • Establish consistent contracting standards and templates for design engagements across the portfolio; align scope boundaries and interface agreements so multi-discipline coverage is complete with no gaps or overlaps.
  • Manage contract performance through delivery: track deliverables against milestones, administer change and additional-services requests, review and approve design invoicing against progress, and resolve scope and performance issues.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, and Procurement on design-contract terms, risk allocation, and commercial approvals, engaging qualified counsel on high-stakes terms.

Design & Construction Partner Leadership

  • Serve as Montera’s senior owner-side leader to external design and construction partners: CSA and MEP engineers of record, design-assist trade partners (e.g., mechanical and electrical), GC/CM, and specialty consultants.
  • Own the design-assist and delivery-model strategy (e.g., design-bid-build vs. design-assist) and the associated partner scopes, deliverables, and interface agreements.
  • Lead design reviews, coordination summits, and constructability reviews; drive partner accountability to quality, schedule, and cost.
  • Support AHJ permitting and entitlement outcomes through the Architect/Master Planning Principal and partner teams.

Design Oversight Through Construction

  • Own owner-side design oversight through construction with GCs and subcontractors — protecting design intent from IFC through commissioning and turnover.
  • Govern the construction-phase design workflow: RFIs, submittals and shop-drawing review, and coordination/BIM clash resolution across trades, driving timely engineer-of-record responses.
  • Review and disposition field changes, design-related change orders, and value-engineering proposals from GCs and subs; safeguard reliability (five-nines availability), operability, and standards conformance.
  • Lead design representation at OAC meetings and site design reviews; track design-related construction risk and drive resolution with the GC, subs, and design partners.
  • Ensure as-built and design close-out documentation from GCs and subs is complete and fed back into Montera reference designs and standards.

Constructability, Commissioning & Handover

  • Ensure designs are constructable, coordinated (clash-free), and aligned to procurement lead times and site logistics.
  • Own the design-side inputs to commissioning and integrated systems testing (IST); ensure acceptance criteria and turnover readiness are designed in, not retrofitted.
  • Drive lessons-learned from construction and operations back into reference designs and standards for continuous fleet improvement.

Cross-Functional & Executive Alignment

  • Translate the CTO-captured customer requirements into a governed design program and report design status, risks, and decisions to the CTO and leadership.
  • Partner with Development, Delivery, Operations, GRC, and Finance on schedule, cost, constructability, and interconnection-driven design constraints (e.g., FRT / utility obligations).
  • Provide design content and technical substantiation to support the CTO’s customer engagements and executive/board materials, without owning the customer-facing relationship.

Who You Are:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Architecture or Engineering (Electrical, Mechanical, or related); professional licensure (PE/RA) preferred.
  • 15+ years of experience in data center or mission-critical design and delivery, including senior leadership of multi-discipline design programs for hyperscale or AI-focused facilities.
  • Proven track record leading design across full delivery lifecycle (concept to IFC to commissioning) with accountability for schedule, cost, and quality.
  • Demonstrated leadership of principal/expert individual contributors and of external design and construction partners (CSA, MEP, design-assist, GC/CM).
  • Proven experience defining, negotiating, and managing design contracts (scope, deliverables, standard of care, fees, change control) and administering owner-side design oversight through construction with GCs and subcontractors (RFIs, submittals, change orders, field changes).
  • Strong command of how architectural, electrical, mechanical, controls, and network scopes integrate, and of delivery models (design-bid-build, design-assist, EPC).
  • Excellent judgment on constructability, value engineering, and design risk; strong commercial and schedule discipline.
  • Exceptional communication; able to represent design internally to the CTO, leadership, and board, and to lead partners externally.

Why Join Montera?

At Montera, you’ll shape the next generation of digital infrastructure while being supported by a team that values integrity, collaboration, and long-term partnership. We’re a remote-first company that empowers our people with flexibility, ownership, and meaningful rewards.

Compensation:

At Montera, we believe great work starts with investing in great people. That is why we offer a competitive and thoughtful total compensation package designed to recognize the value each team member brings.

Our compensation ranges are informed by market data and aligned to job level and role. When making hiring and compensation decisions, we consider a variety of factors, including skills, experience, education, training, competencies, and overall business needs.

Our Benefits at a Glance:

  • Comprehensive Health Coverage: We pay 90% of health premiums for employees and their dependents.

  • Parental Leave: Up to 8 weeks of paid time off after 6 months of employment.
  • Financial Security: 401(k) plan with immediate eligibility, no vesting requirement, and employer match contributions up to 6%.
  • Learning & Development Reimbursement: Up to $3,500 reimbursed annually for approved courses, certifications, conferences and professional development opportunities.
  • Extra Support: Remote work stipend to help you stay connected.

At Montera, you’ll have the autonomy to do great work and the benefits to thrive personally and professionally.

description:
ChampionAI is QAD | Redzone agentic platform, purpose-built for manufacturing and utilized by the various business units within QAD | Redzone. This engineer joins the core platform team with three main areas of focus: building new capabilities into the platform, helping Applied AI teams at partner business units build and ship Champions correctly, and directly building Champion agents for business-unit use cases when needed.
You will work in the same codebase as the Applied AI engineers you support, which keeps the enablement work
practical and the platform work focused on real problems.

Key Responsibilities
Platform Development

  • Build and ship features across the Champion platform repositories
  • Improve developer experience: tooling, scaffolding, internal documentation, and onboarding paths for Applied AI engineers.
  • Maintain and evolve the MCP tool server and agent infrastructure that BU teams depend on.
  • Identify and address friction points that slow down Champion development or deployment

Applied AI Enablement

  • Support BU Applied AI engineers in building, deploying, and operating Champions correctly
  • Review agent implementations for prompt quality, scope enforcement, auth configuration, and deployment setup
  • Contribute to internal engineering guides and skill documentation
  • Pair with BU engineers on first K8S manifest creation, database registration, and LaunchDarkly prompt rollout

Agent Development

  • Design and build Champion agents for BU use-cases when the platform team is directly engaged
  • Write and iterate on system prompts, tool bindings, and context injection for production agents
  • Register agents in Champion Server and configure LaunchDarkly-gated prompt rollout across environments

Engineering Practices
We follow trunk-based development with PR-gated merges to main. Engineers are expected to:

  • Write tests before implementing. TDD is the expectation, not a nice-to-have.
  • Keep PRs small and focused; use feature flags to ship partial work incrementally
  • Follow conventional commit format (feat:, fix:, etc.)
  • Be mindful of API and schema backward-compatibility; prefer additive changes over breaking ones
  • Review your own diff before requesting review

Core Requirements

  • Python: Proficient in async Python, Pydantic, type hints, and FastAPI. Experience with the Strands agent SDK or a comparable agentic framework. Testing is non-optional: candidates should be comfortable with pytest, pytest- asyncio, and DeepEval for agent-specific evaluation. We test agent behavior, not just unit logic.
  • Prompt Engineering: Able to write and iterate on production system prompts: XML-structured, scope-enforced, with tool descriptions that guide LLM delegation reliably.
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP): Solid understanding of MCP and hands-on experience building or consuming MCP servers. Familiarity with Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is a strong plus.
  • Agent Patterns: Familiar with multi-agent architectures and orchestration patterns beyond basic ReAct: supervisor/subagent delegation, parallel tool use, handoffs, and context management across agent boundaries.
  • Agent Evals: Able to design and run evaluation suites for agent behavior: correctness checks, scope enforcement tests, regression coverage, and systematic prompt iteration based on eval results.
  • Docker: Comfortable authoring Dockerfiles, multi-stage builds, and local dev environments via docker-compose / make.
  • PostgreSQL: Comfortable with templated INSERT/SELECT, foreign key relationships, and reading an ER diagram.
  • Git / Semantic Versioning: Follows conventional commit format (feat:, fix:) and a PR-based trunk workflow.

Nice to Have

  • Kubernetes: Working knowledge of Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and ServiceAccounts. Able to read and adapt K8s manifests and use kubectl for basic troubleshooting.
  • AWS: Working knowledge of ECR, EKS, IAM, and Bedrock (inference layer).
  • OAuth2 / OIDC: Conceptual understanding of Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, token exchange, and agent auth delegation.
  • Terraform: Beginner-level familiarity; able to make targeted changes to existing modules and interpret a plan diff.
  • LaunchDarkly: Experience managing feature flags or AI config overrides for environment-gated rollout.
  • Document Intelligence / OCR: AWS Textract or comparable pipeline experience for use cases involving structured document extraction.

AI-Native Development

  • We run an AI-native SDLC. AI-assisted tools (Claude Code, Cursor) are part of the standard engineering workflow at every stage: planning, implementation, review, and documentation. This is not optional or supplemental; it is how we work. Candidates should be comfortable with AI-assisted development and willing to invest in getting good at it.
  • Use Claude Code and Cursor actively across planning, implementation, and code review
  • Know when AI output is wrong and push back on it.
  • Help drive adoption across the team by sharing what works

What This Role Is Not
This is not an ML research or data science role. The platform team owns cluster networking, observability pipelines, auth configuration, and LLM routing, so deep expertise in those areas is not required. The job is building reliable
software on top of that infrastructure and helping others do the same.

At Foodsmart, our mission is to make nutritious food accessible and affordable for everyone, regardless of economic status. We are committed to a set of core values that shape our culture and work environment:

👥 Customer First - You start with the member and work backwards.
🚀 Make It Happen - You act with urgency, use data, and hold high standards.
🤝 One Team - You collaborate with respect and commit as a group.

Whether you're a dietitian, a commercial leader, or a technologist, working at Foodsmart means being part of a team that is passionate, supportive, and driven by a shared purpose. Join us in transforming the way people access and enjoy healthy food.

About the Role:

Foodsmart’s value proposition rests on a claim: we improve outcomes for the members who need it most, and we save payers real money doing it. We’re looking for a Senior Director of Health Economics & Actuarial Analytics who can make that claim airtight, rigorous enough to hold up when a payer’s own actuarial team pressure tests it.

This role owns the full chain from clinical improvement to economic value. It starts with measuring what actually changed for a client’s members: weight loss, A1c improvement, blood pressure control, HEDIS performance. It ends with quantifying what that improvement is worth and defending that number in front of the people writing the check.

You’ll also help shape our value-based care strategy, including which populations we should be targeting and what performance we can credibly commit to.

Health economists and actuaries approach these problems differently, and either can be excellent here. What matters is the standard you hold yourself to. Our numbers get validated by payers’ own actuarial teams, which means the work has to be built the way they would build it, with their assumptions about trend, credibility, and risk adjustment.

This is our most senior data science leadership role, reporting directly to the VP of Analytics & Data Science. You’ll lead a small team while staying deeply hands-on with the methodology yourself, and you’ll be expected to use AI as a genuine force multiplier, to move faster, go deeper, and extend your reach well beyond what the headcount alone would suggest. You’ll also be a partner on our peer-reviewed research work, which we pursue with academic collaborators and our founder and Chief Science Officer.

The strongest candidates will have done this inside a telehealth or digital health company, or will have built their foundation on the payer or consulting side and then moved into digital health. What matters most is that you have proven value to payers before, repeatedly, and know what it takes for those numbers to be believed.

You will:

  • Own how we measure clinical outcomes across client member populations: weight loss, A1c, blood pressure, food insecurity, HEDIS measures, and the quality metrics our clients hold us to.
  • Own Foodsmart’s ROI methodology: translating those clinical outcomes into economic value, and identifying which member populations we help the most.
  • Represent that methodology directly to payers and external actuarial and consulting firms, defending our approach under real technical scrutiny rather than just presenting a final number.
  • Own the analytical substance of the value story we tell individual clients, grounded in their own members’ outcomes rather than generic benchmarks.
  • Help shape our value-based care strategy, including which member populations to target and what performance we can credibly stand behind.
  • Build our outcomes and ROI methodology as a scalable system, one that extends to new populations and new client conversations without being rebuilt from scratch each time.
  • Partner on peer-reviewed research with academic collaborators
  • Work with our clinical team to translate findings and best practices into how care is actually delivered.
  • Lead and develop a small team while staying hands-on, and lean on AI and other tooling to extend how much ground you and your team can cover.

You are:

  • Rigorous in the way a payer’s actuarial team is rigorous. You reason about cost, utilization, risk, and credibility with real discipline, and you know where a methodology is most likely to be attacked.
  • Fluent in both clinical quality measurement and economic value, and comfortable moving between the two. You can look at a change in A1c across a population and know how to turn it into a number a payer will accept.
  • Comfortable being the technical counterpart to a payer’s own actuaries and consultants: unintimidated by scrutiny, and able to defend methodology choices in real time.
  • Seasoned. You have proven value to payers repeatedly, and you are not learning ROI methodology on the job.
  • A systems builder who thinks in terms of scale: a repeatable methodology, not a one-off analysis redone for every new client or payer.
  • Able to translate technical findings into how care actually gets delivered, working alongside clinical and care delivery teams.
  • Someone who treats AI as a genuine lever on your own impact. You actively look for ways to use it to work faster and go deeper, and you have a point of view on where it helps and where rigor still demands a human.
  • Comfortable leading a small team while staying personally hands-on with the hardest analytical work yourself.

You have:

  • A background in health economics, actuarial science, or a closely related quantitative field, with a track record of applying it to healthcare cost and value questions. An advanced degree or actuarial credentials (ASA, FSA, MAAA) are a plus but not required if you have equivalent hands-on depth.
  • Experience proving ROI and value inside a telehealth or digital health company, or a foundation on the payer or consulting side followed by time in digital health.
  • Hands-on experience measuring clinical outcomes and quality across populations, including familiarity with HEDIS and common chronic condition measures.
  • Deep, hands-on experience with healthcare claims data, both medical and pharmacy (Rx), including the practical realities of using it for cost and utilization analysis.
  • Deep expertise in causal inference as applied to healthcare cost and outcomes: matched cohort design, risk adjustment, and quasi-experimental methods.
  • Direct experience presenting and defending ROI methodology with payers, actuaries, or similarly technical external audiences.
  • Experience with value-based care arrangements and a point of view on what a provider or vendor can credibly commit to.

  • Comfort working directly with data (SQL, R, or Python) to conduct your own analysis.
  • Familiarity with AI-native tooling (Claude Code, or equivalent) as a way to accelerate analysis.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write for external, technical, and non-technical audiences alike.

  • Гнучкі методології розробки, знання та застосування SDLC, Scrum, Kanban, XP, WF.

Буде плюсом

  • Інструменти інкрементальних змін у БД (Liquibase).

Ми пропонуємо

description:

What You'll Be Doing

    PROSPECT AND BUILD A QUALIFIED LIFE SCIENCES PIPELINE

  • Proactively build pipeline in a green-field or assigned Life Sciences territory using conference presence, publication monitoring, thought leadership networks, hunting via warm and cold outreach, leveraging of BDR Team, and CRO or consultancy partnerships

  • Opportunity qualification

  • Pricing and commercial structuring

  • Partner closely with legal, finance, and leadership to finalize terms efficiently

  • Orchestrate internal resources without over-committing them, and manage a clean handoff to delivery and customer success to protect revenue
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date CRM records and deliver reliable forecasts, distinguishing clearly between commit, best case, and pipeline
  • Contribute market and competitive feedback that informs product roadmap, packaging, and pricing decisions

  • 5+ years of experience selling into pharmaceutical and/or biotechnology companies, ideally in a quota-carrying, individual contributor role
  • Demonstrated success selling data-, analytics-, or evidence-driven solutions (RWD, RWE/HEOR, clinical analytics, or adjacent offerings)

What You'll Get

  • For more than a decade, Arcadia has been the trusted data and analytics partner to health systems, physician groups, and payers nationwide. That core business provides deep, longitudinal clinical and claims data, embedded clinical workflows, and durable relationships across the healthcare ecosystem

  • Life Sciences is a strategic pillar built on this foundation. Arcadia has made a deliberate, multi-year investment in:
  • Purpose-built real-world data assets
  • Clinically connected solutions that link insight back into provider workflows
  • A growing research and collaboration ecosystem to expand data use rights
  • Dedicated leadership, product, data, and operational resources
  • The opportunity is to sell—and help shape—solutions that connect data, analytics, and real-world clinical activation across the pharma development lifecycle, backed by enterprise credibility and executive commitment
  • This role is a founding, hands-on commercial leadership role, accountable for building the direct Life Sciences revenue engine, and deeply involved in shaping deals, messaging, and market positioning
  • This role is not a channel-only or account maintenance role, a narrowly scoped quota-carrying role with a fixed playbook, and insulated from product, delivery, or execution realities

About Arcadia

Arcadia.io helps innovative providers and payers across the country transform healthcare to reduce cost while improving patient health. We do this by aggregating large amounts of disparate data, applying algorithms to identify opportunities to provide better patient care, and making those opportunities actionable by physicians at the point of care in near-real time. We are passionate about helping our customers drive meaningful outcomes. We are growing fast and have emerged as a market leader in the highly competitive population health management software market and have been recognized by industry analysts KLAS, IDC, Forrester, and Chilmark for our leadership. Osmind is a public benefit corporation advancing psychiatry through technology, services, and real-world evidence to bring innovative mental health treatments to patients in need. Simultaneously, Osmind's clinic network, point-of-care software, and real-world data support life sciences companies in developing and scaling access to cutting-edge treatments. Osmind is a 50-person, Series B-stage company and has raised funding from top investors such as DFJ Growth, Y Combinator, and General Catalyst.

The Opportunity

We're hiring a second mid-market Account Executive to close deals that give psychiatry practices offering innovative treatments the technology and services to treat more patients in need. These practices are growing, and the operational and financial side of running these programs is where they most often get stuck. You'll work with a physician owner, a practice administrator, and usually someone who runs the business side and will ask hard questions. These are substantial relationships, often six figures. You'll report to our Director of Sales.

Pipeline comes to you, from inbound demand and from two Founding BDRs who join at the same time to build our outbound motion. Your job is to run the deal from the first meeting through signature.

These practices rarely buy on features. They buy because their current setup isn't built for the new era of psychiatry, and that limits how many patients they can treat. Getting it right for a clinic has a direct effect on access to care.

What You'll Do

  • Run mid-market deals from the first meeting through signature, aligning clinical, operational, and business stakeholders along the way.
  • Diagnose which of our offerings fits a practice early in the conversation. Selling the wrong one is the most common way these deals are lost.
  • Build the financial and ROI case. These practices buy on what they collect, so you'll need to be fluent enough in accounts receivable, denials, and net collection rate to hold your own with whoever runs their billing.
  • Displace incumbents on how they're actually performing rather than on a feature comparison.
  • Qualify with discipline, and verify what a practice tells you before investing a full cycle in it.
  • Partner closely with the Founding BDRs: give fast, specific feedback on what you accept and why, and coach by example.

  • Represent Osmind at industry conferences and events (quarterly travel).
  • Use AI to increase selling effectiveness: leverage Gong, Claude, and other tools to cut manual admin so more of your week goes to selling.

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years closing deals end to end at six-figure contract values, with multi-stakeholder buying committees and 5+ years of closing experience overall
  • Experience selling into independent medical practices — you understand how clinicians and clinic owners make purchasing decisions
  • Genuine comfort with the numbers: you can talk through practice P&L yourself rather than handing it off
  • Experience selling services, or services alongside software, rather than seats alone
  • Disciplined qualification — you'd rather disqualify in week one than carry a weak deal for a quarter
  • AI-first instincts, with a point of view on where it helps in a sales cycle
  • Startup experience at Series A through C companies, demonstrating an ability to run autonomously and embrace ambiguity

Bonus points

  • Experience with/understanding of interventional psychiatry treatments, including the REMS requirements attached to some of them
  • Familiarity with prior authorization, verification of benefits, or payer contracting
  • Experience selling EHR, RCM, or practice management software

EnableComp provides Specialty Revenue Cycle Management solutions for healthcare organizations, leveraging over 24 years of industry-leading expertise and its unified E360 RCM™ intelligent automation platform to improve financial sustainability for hospitals, health systems, and ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) nationwide. excerpt: About the TeamOur engineering team builds next-generation, cloud-native bare-metal orchestration platforms for AI neo-cloud environments.
description:
About the Team

Our engineering team builds next-generation, cloud-native bare-metal orchestration platforms for AI neo-cloud environments. We operate on a T-shaped engineering model: while each engineer brings deep expertise in a primary domain, every team member maintains practical fluency across neighboring systems. This shared foundation enables rigorous design reviews, effective cross-domain code reviews, and dependable on-call coverage. Our development is fundamentally based on open-source projects, and contributing to them is a major part of our work.

We develop primary control plane software in Rust and Go, leverage Kubernetes operators, and foster an OpenTelemetry-first operational culture.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer who combines strong software architecture principles with deep technical domain expertise in Datacenter Networking and DPU architectures. Fitting into our T-shaped engineering model, you will drive the development of control planes powering high-density, high-throughput infrastructure for AI training and inference workloads. Familiarity with automated bare-metal provisioning and lifecycle management is a strong asset.

Core Responsibilities

  • Control Plane Development: Design, build, and maintain production-grade control plane microservices, custom Kubernetes operators, and robust reconciliation engines in Rust and Go.

  • Architecture & API Design: Author clear Functional (FR) and Non-Functional Requirements (NFR), architectural specs, system sequence diagrams, and clean gRPC/Protobuf and REST API schemas.

  • Network Integration: Develop custom integration modules and integrations for modern network operating systems (SONiC, NVUE, Cumulus) and DPU hardware platforms.

  • Observability & Diagnostics: Instrument services end-to-end using OpenTelemetry (OTel) traces and metrics, performing systematic root-cause analysis across polyglot distributed systems.

  • Quality & Engineering Excellence: Participate in rigorous, review-gated pull request workflows across Rust, Go, and SQL codebases while ensuring high test coverage via mock-driven testing.

  • Language Proficiency: Primary mastery of Rust (Tokio async runtime, Tonic, Axum, sqlx) and strong proficiency in Go.

  • Data & APIs: Advanced SQL / PostgreSQL fluency, gRPC/Protobuf contract design, and schema evolution.

  • Concurrency & Reliability: Strong background in async concurrency models, lock-free patterns, distributed state handling, and mock-driven testing discipline.

  • Datacenter Protocols & OS: Expertise in BGP, MP-BGP, EVPN, VXLAN, L3VNI, route targets, and route server design. Hands-on experience with SONiC, Cumulus Linux, and NVUE (featuring a first-class NVUE client).

  • DPU & Fabric Ecosystem: Deep knowledge of NVIDIA DOCA, Host-Based Networking (HBN), BlueField DPU architectures, and the DPF (DOCA Platform Framework) operator model (BFB, DPUSet, DPUNode CRDs).

  • High-Performance Interconnects: Understanding of InfiniBand fabrics, NVLink / NMX-M partitioning, and RoCEv2.

  • Linux Kernel Networking: Advanced grasp of Linux netlink, network namespaces, routing tables, and internal DHCP/DNS service implementations (the project ships its own services).

  • Cloud & Kubernetes Networking: Familiarity with CNI plugins (Calico, Cilium). OVS and DPDK experience is a plus.

  • Provisioning & Boot Infrastructure: Expertise in PXE/iPXE, UEFI, Secure Boot, measured boot, and TPM attestation.

  • Hardware Management: Proficiency in Redfish, IPMI, and BMC abstractions across heterogeneous hardware platforms (Dell, Lenovo, NVIDIA reference hardware).

  • Linux Systems Internals: In-depth knowledge of boot chains, systemd, initramfs, BIOS configuration matrices.

  • Identity & Security: Practical experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, TLS, SPIFFE/SVID, Vault, KMS, Keycloak (OAuth2/JWT), and RBAC.

  • Virtualization: Experience with KubeVirt / KVM.

  • Kubernetes Control Planes: Experience writing custom controllers/operators using kube-rs or controller-runtime with CRD-driven reconciliation loop patterns.

Universal Requirements

  • Testing Discipline: Commitment to test-driven design, writing highly testable code with mock interfaces for external hardware and network dependencies.

  • Collaborative Architecture: Proven track record of writing crisp architectural specs and engaging in constructive, cross-functional design reviews.

Educational & Experience Baseline

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience in cloud-native platforms, systems programming, networking, or infrastructure automation.

  • Demonstrated participation or maintainership in open-source systems projects is a plus.

What does Mirantis offer you?

- Work with an established Silicon Valley leader in the cloud infrastructure industry;

excerpt: Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm.
description:
Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. Most modernization work doesn't ship, it stalls in pilots, slips a year, or lands at three times the budget. We exist to ship it: production systems running, legacy retired, outcomes measured. Our delivery is built on Aedeon, the agent platform built by Mactores' founders' sister company, which absorbs the repetitive 60–70% of engagement work, discovery, dependency mapping, validation, test generation, that traditional consulting bills human hours against. Forward-deployed engineers own the rest: architecture, judgment, and cutover, on dates we commit to in the contract.

We put delivery dates in contracts and carry the overage risk ourselves. That only works if someone owns the delivery-scope, timeline, budget, and sprint execution and treats a slipping date as their problem, not a status-report line item. That someone is you.

As our Project Manager, you'll run distributed engineering teams across India and three US time zones on customer engagements where the date is committed. You'll run the daily, sprint, and client cadences, translate fluently between engineering and business stakeholders, and push back on scope creep with data. Agents compress the repetitive engineering work, which makes delivery faster and makes your job sharper: shorter timelines leave no room for blockers that sit in a log for days. We're looking for the PM who gets things done who personally removes blockers, drives escalations to closure, and makes sure no risk reaches the client as a surprise.

This role is not for you if:

  • Your default is to forward messages between the client and engineering.
  • Your role has primarily been reporting and coordination without delivery ownership.
  • You've only facilitated agile ceremonies without driving delivery outcomes.
  • Sprint ownership and execution were largely driven by a Business Analyst or Product Owner in your previous roles.

What you will do?

  • Build the project plan in Smartsheet from the Solutions Architect's scope of work, real dependencies, a defensible critical path, sprint boundaries overlaid on the timeline.
  • Track scope, hours, and budget in real time. Flag burn-rate risk early and push back on scope creep with numbers, not gut feel.
  • Maintain a live risk register. Spot risks before they become issues, surface the right ones to the client at the right time, and drive mitigation actively.
  • Maintain a live RAID log (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, Dependencies) and an action tracker with clear ownership, accountability, and timely closure.
  • Run crisp daily stand-ups, sprint planning, and retrospectives that produce decisions, not discussions.
  • Remove sprint blockers personally. Chase the client-side data dependency, escalate the stuck cloud permission, redirect pulled resources don't let "waiting on" sit in a log for days.
  • Handle sprint-level risks in real time: reprioritize, descope, swap stories, or escalate before commitments slip.
  • Keep trackers honest. Action items have owners and dates; delays are visible and followed up on time.
  • Translate technical progress into business language for the customer, and business priorities into clear, estimable requirements for engineers.
  • Facilitate internal and external architecture reviews across India and three US time zones; document decisions and circulate them the same day.
  • Produce weekly customer status updates a senior business leader can absorb in 90 seconds — RAG colors backed by evidence, not sentiment.
  • Own customer escalations and drive them to resolution. Communicate status, risks, and decisions needed — proactively, not reactively.
  • Onboard engineers on customer systems, scope, process, deliverables, and documentation standards.
  • Create kick-off presentations, project charters, and tracking mechanisms in collaboration with the customer.
  • Maintain meeting notes, recorded calls, and a clean project documentation library.
  • Review and approve timesheets and leaves; keep capacity planning and team calendar management accurate.
  • Negotiate scope changes with data. Produce formal change requests with impact analysis hours, timeline, trade-offs, options before anyone commits the team to additional work.
  • Drive sprint predictability with velocity planning and burndown tracking; commitments are realistic and consistently met.
  • Run backlog refinement with Principal Consultants or Technical Leads so stories are clear, prioritized, and estimable.

What are we looking for

  • 3+ years of delivery experience on cloud engineering or data engineering projects.
  • Hands-on fluency with Smartsheet, Jira / Confluence, and Clockify — you can stand up the tooling on day one.
  • Excellent written and spoken communication, facilitation, negotiation, and coaching skills — you can hold your ground with a skeptical client engineering director and coach a junior engineer in the same afternoon.
  • Strong prioritization and problem-solving instincts. You make trade-offs explicit rather than quietly absorbing them.
  • A demonstrable track record of driving outcomes, not just reporting on them.
  • Demonstrated experience managing at least one fixed-bid project from kickoff through closure, including scope change negotiation with clients.
  • A strong grasp of Agile delivery metrics — velocity, burndown, sprint predictability — and the ability to use them to drive execution.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments where requirements evolve; you bring structure proactively.

You will be preferred if you posses

  • Experience managing Data Lake projects on AWS.
  • Professional Scrum Master™ (PSM) certification.
  • Managing Jira Projects certification.
  • Smartsheet certification.

How we work?

    Aedeon absorbs scale. Engineers absorb judgment. The contract absorbs risk fixed-date delivery, with Mactores covering overage cost for delays inside our control. You're the person who keeps those three honest on a live engagement: the plan defensible, the burn visible, the risks surfaced before they cost anything. Our engineers embed with the customer's team and carry the delivery commitment personally. You carry the date.

The Path to Joining the Mactores Team

At Mactores, our recruitment process is structured around three distinct stages:

VGS is the world's leader in payment tokenization. Large banks, aspiring fintechs, and growing merchants embed our universal token vault into their technology stack to manage the complexities of payment data tokenization across processors and networks, open banking, card issuance, omnichannel loyalty, PCI compliance, payment orchestration, and more. Some of the use cases we enable include multi-processor Network Tokenization, Account Updater, payment orchestration, secure settlement file processing, 3DS, and Risk provider connectivity.

The majority of this role is hands-on technical work: debugging, troubleshooting network and integration issues, onboarding new customers, and resolving tickets.

The remainder is operational ownership and cross-team coordination. The support team plays a vital role in translating between our Engineering and Go-To-Market teams (including account management and sales). During incidents, outages, escalations, and planned maintenance, you are the primary on-shift decision-maker for PT business hours: you decide whether an incident goes on the public status page, approve the wording of customer notifications, set maintenance timing, and coordinate as needed with the GTM teams so that they are aware of any impacts to their clients. These decisions sit with leadership today, and we want them to be owned within Support.

They come up infrequently but are time-sensitive and customer-visible. You'll have a written scope of what you can approve independently and what requires the manager, expanding as you establish a track record.

What you will be doing at VGS (Responsibilities)...

  • Serve as the senior decision-maker for the Support team during PT business hours. Escalations, judgment calls, and approvals land with you. You're the person on shift with the standing to decide, not to route.

  • Own incident and maintenance communications. Assess severity and customer impact, decide when to post to the public status page, write or approve the wording, including team drafts, and keep it up to date through resolution.

  • Set and coordinate maintenance timing. Choose windows based on real customer traffic patterns and regional load, negotiate them with engineering, inform internal client-facing teams about and make sure the notice goes out with enough lead time for customers to plan.

  • Coordinate multi-team projects where Support is a stakeholder: migrations, deprecations, launches, and customer-specific rollouts. Track dependencies and keep the parties honest about status.

  • Debug deeply. Reproduce issues with cURL and Postman, read logs, and trace requests across VGS infrastructure, customer systems, and downstream gateways. Diagnose network problems independently: DNS, TCP/IP, routing, timeouts, connection resets, and TLS/SSL handshake failures.

  • Resolve an issue, find a workaround, or escalate with a bug report good enough for engineering to act on immediately.

  • Drive mid-tier and long tail customer integrations from kickoff to go-live, coordinating between customer engineers and internal teams.

  • Write up nontrivial investigations as internal runbooks or public documentation.

  • Prepare and deliver customer training, building the material where it doesn't exist.

  • Meet SLA and quality targets, and help the team meet theirs.

  • Participate in the weekend on-call rotation (every 3rd weekend, Saturday and Sunday, 8:00–20:00 PT). On-call is monitoring coverage, not a full working day — you respond to urgent incidents and time-sensitive requests, while routine tickets wait for the next business day.

  • Experience owning customer-facing incident or maintenance communication. You will be writing status page updates, incident notices, and escalation emails. You understand the difference between transparency and alarm.

  • Strong internal communication skills. You will be the translation layer between customers, VGS account management, and VGS product and engineering. You should be able to operate in different contexts and understand how to translate between the technical, operations, and business contexts of conversations to ensure context is not lost between stakeholders.

  • Autonomy. You are comfortable deciding and then reporting, rather than checking first. You'll have a few hours of overlap with your manager each day and spend the rest of your shift as the main decision-maker.

  • Strong command of HTTP, REST APIs, and proxies.

  • Independent network debugging — DNS, TCP/IP, routing, connectivity, TLS/SSL handshakes. Be ready to describe a specific problem you diagnosed and how you narrowed it down.

InStride Health’s mission is to deliver specialty anxiety and OCD care that works for every kid, teen, young adult, and family who needs it. Through this mission, we are expanding access to insurance-based care, increasing engagement in treatment, and improving treatment outcomes.   • Give Heart: We lead with heart, treating patients and their families the way we want our loved ones to be treated.
  • Work Smart: We find smarter ways to solve hard problems and fix the broken mental health system by leveraging technology, diversity of thought, and innovation.
  • Have Humility: We leave our egos at the door, empowering our team to collaborate, celebrate diversity, and adopt a growth mindset.
  • Embrace Community: We all belong. We are in this together, and we never worry alone. We believe in each other and recognize that every voice matters.

About the Role

We are looking for a Manager of IT to bring technical depth, delivery structure, and systems health to the technology department that keeps InStride running. Reporting to the Senior Director of IT, this role owns the operating rhythm of our core workplace systems, including sprint planning, ticket hygiene, resolution SLAs, and project delivery, while directly managing and developing a team of IT support specialists. Sitting between leadership and support specialists, this role acts as a force multiplier: converting recurring manual work into automation, establishing clear reporting layers, and serving as the senior technical escalation point. This role is focused on technical leadership, operational rhythms, and managing the support team through company growth. This is a fully remote position.

Responsibilities:

  • Run the IT Team operating rhythm, establishing sprint planning, standups, retrospectives, ticket hygiene, and clear SLA tracking aligned with the broader technology organization.
  • Directly supervise and develop the IT support team, providing clear direction, performance oversight, and professional growth support.
  • Serve as the senior technical escalation point above support specialists, guiding the team through complex troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and IT operational standards.
  • Own enterprise identity and access management (IAM) platforms (specifically Okta), including RBAC design, group architecture, SSO and SCIM integrations, and lifecycle provisioning automation.
  • Administer systems and policies within cloud collaboration platforms alongside direct mobile device management (MDM) to ensure device compliance, zero-touch deployment pipelines, and OS update strategy across macOS endpoints.
  • Manage the cloud telephony and collaboration portfolio, including but not limited to Zoom, Zoom Phone (call queues and IVR routing), Slack, and Jira Service Management queue routing logic and configuration.
  • Convert recurring manual IT onboarding and access requests into automated self-service workflows.
  • Build IT operational reporting dashboards, structuring data to help manage and streamline day-to-day IT operations.
  • Reconcile software licenses against active headcount on a set cadence to identify cost variances before they compound across SaaS applications.
  • Partner with Security to run access reviews, enforce least-privilege principles, support endpoint/email security tooling, and collect IT audit evidence for compliance cycles.
  • Strategically implement and administer AI capabilities within IT operations to improve overall IT throughput, efficiency, and SLAs while adhering to rigorous compliance standards.
  • Partner cross-functionally with HR, Clinical, Commercial, and Engineering stakeholders to manage cohort onboarding/offboarding, run decision-oriented meetings, and maintain clear internal technical runbooks and end-user FAQs.

  • 5+ years of progressive experience in IT operations and systems administration, including direct people-management experience supervising, developing, and mentoring technical or support staff.
  • Deep technical mastery of enterprise identity administration, including RBAC design, SSO/SCIM integrations, and provisioning workflow automation.
  • Strong hands-on experience managing macOS fleets (~400 endpoints) using MDM and cloud collaboration platforms. Direct experience with Iru (Kandji) and Google Workspace is a plus.
  • Proven track record of building operational reporting dashboards and structuring data into actionable metrics for leadership across ticket execution, SLA tracking, and license utilization.
  • Capable of operating within regulated healthcare or compliance environments (HIPAA, SOC 2), including running access reviews and audit evidence gathering.
  • Highly developed cross-functional communication and project delivery skills, with the ability to run decision-oriented meetings and write clear runbooks for technical and non-technical staff.
  • Experience or familiarity administering cloud telephony (Zoom Phone IVR/queues), Jira Service Management, or CRM tools (Zoho) is preferred.
  • Practical experience applying AI tools to operational workflows within a secure, compliant environment.

Salary

The expected annual salary for this role is between $124,000 and $138,000. Actual starting salary will be determined on an individualized basis and will be based on several factors including but not limited to specific skill set, work experience, etc.

Why Join Our Team

  • Generous benefits package (401k with match, Flexible PTO, paid holidays, paid service days, 4 week paid sabbatical, 12 week paid parental leave, health benefits starting on your first day, and more)
  • Opportunity to join a mission-driven company that is changing the landscape of pediatric mental health treatment
  • Chance to make a far-reaching impact by helping children and families access desperately-needed, evidence-based care
  • Opportunity to work with talented and experienced team members who have devoted their lives to solving this problem
  • Fully virtual: work from the comfort of your home with periodic in-person retreats

Commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Belonging (DEIB)

We want to make our clinical services available for everyone, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or how you identify. To achieve this, we recognize we must continually make progress in building a more diverse, equitable, and inclusive team. Through these efforts, we support two primary objectives at InStride Health:

  1. Providing high quality patient care to families. We are in a privileged position to support families during a vulnerable time in their lives. We approach all families and each other with compassion and are most effective as a diverse team where all individuals feel valued, respected, and accepted.
  2. Building a mission-driven business that lasts. Specifically, we believe our commitment to a supportive culture improves innovation, decision-making, and efficiency.

At the heart of that platform is a Python data API built on a layered router → service → repository architecture, containerized with Docker and deployed entirely through infrastructure-as-code.

The role is primarily focused on the data API, but it is a team role rather than a single-service one — you will work across the data platform as it grows. This is backend- and data-centric work: you will spend more time on data correctness, performance, and the movement and reconciliation of large datasets across heterogeneous sources than on any single framework or UI library. Strong proficiency in Python (3.12+) backend development — FastAPI, Pydantic v2, async/await — and T-SQL, with deep comfort in the data and service layers of an enterprise application. (Breadth and fundamentals matter more than any specific library or framework.)

Your Success; Our Blueprint

Nothing influences your success more than a solid roadmap to your growth. Your onboarding will be an immersive and engaging experience. About Thrivent
Thrivent is a diversified financial services organization that, with its subsidiary and affiliate companies, serves more than 2.4 million clients, offering advice, insurance, investments, banking and generosity products and programs. Location: This is a fully remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team

The External Data Analytics team builds and operates the data platform that powers trusted, timely analytics across College Board's exam and AP Classwork programs, including AP Classwork's continuous, year-round data needs. We're a small, closely knit, cross-functional team (~7 engineers today, and growing) with a mix of data engineering and full-stack backgrounds. We value ownership, thoughtful automation, clear documentation, pragmatic architecture, and keeping students top of mind in everything we build.

About the Opportunity

As the technical lead for the platform, you'll own architecture end-to-end and serve as the final technical authority on the team's hardest problems, operating a level above a senior IC. You'll stay hands-on yourself, writing production infrastructure-as-code and setting the coding standards the team follows, while leading design and implementation across streaming and batch ingestion, curated analytical data products, and reliable data-consumption patterns. Because our immediate priority is AP Classwork analytics, you'll be designing for continuous, steady-state, year-round throughput and long-running data quality, often working through ambiguity as requirements and priorities evolve; not just a single test-day spike.

You will work with contributing domain teams to establish data contracts and ensure data is accurate, governed, secure, and ready for analysis, making and communicating tradeoffs involving scale, performance, reliability, cost, and operational complexity along the way. You'll also set the standard for how the team uses AI-assisted coding responsibly, establishing review practices and guardrails for AI-generated code, and, as a technical anchor for the team, mentor engineers and raise engineering standards across the platform.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the technical direction, architecture, evolution, and reliability of a shared enterprise data and analytics platform, serving as the team's final technical authority and escalation point.
  • Lead the hands-on design and implementation of streaming and batch data pipelines supporting real-time and historical analysis, independently writing production infrastructure-as-code (CDK/TypeScript).
  • Design curated, governed analytical data products that provide consistent and trusted information for reporting and decision-making, including for a continuous, year-round data load rather than single-event spikes.
  • Ensure the platform can scale efficiently while meeting expectations for performance, availability, reliability, and cost, including safe recovery from retries and failures.
  • Establish data contracts with contributing teams, including expectations for schemas, data quality, service levels, and change management.
  • Embed security, access controls, lineage, classification, auditability, monitoring, and operational readiness into the platform.
  • Partner with domain, product, operations, security, and governance stakeholders to translate business and reporting needs into sustainable technical solutions.
  • Lead code and design reviews, set and enforce coding standards, mentor engineers across varying experience levels, and promote strong practices in data engineering, automation, observability, and platform reliability.
  • Establish and enforce responsible AI-assisted coding practices for the team, including reviewing AI-generated code and setting guardrails so AI-assisted development doesn't compromise shared infrastructure.
  • Respond to incidents and drive platform reliability across the team's services.
  • Evaluate emerging tools and architectural patterns and recommend changes when they improve outcomes, simplify operations, or reduce risk.

About You:

You bring experience across the capabilities below. We do not expect candidates to have worked with our exact tool stack for everything; comparable tools and the judgment to map your experience onto ours quickly matter.

  • Strong, current, hands-on coding experience in TypeScript and/or JavaScript with AWS CDK is required. You'll be writing production infrastructure-as-code yourself and setting the coding standards the rest of the team follows from Day 1, not just reviewing architecture from a distance.
  • Demonstrated experience owning, not just contributing to, the technical direction and architecture of a scalable cloud data platform in production; you can point to a specific system you were accountable for end-to-end, built on technologies such as Kinesis, Data Firehose, Flink, Lambda, EventBridge, SNS/SQS, Redshift, Athena, Glue, EMR, S3, DynamoDB, or comparable.
  • Strong experience with analytical data modeling and curated, layered data architectures (e.g., medallion-style), plus monitoring/observability (CloudWatch, Grafana, InfluxDB, or similar) as a core part of platform design.
  • A track record of designing for scalability, performance, cost efficiency, data integrity, and safe recovery from retries or failures; you've personally debugged issues like out-of-order processing, duplicate delivery, or hot partitions in production.
  • Experience establishing data contracts and implementing schema evolution, data quality, access control, classification, lineage, and auditability practices.
  • A strong point of view on how to use AI coding tools responsibly at the team level, able to set guardrails and review standards, not just use the tools personally.
  • Demonstrated success of mentoring engineers, leading code and design reviews, being the escalation point on hard problems, and communicating across technical and nontechnical teams.
  • Helpful but not required: SaaS/multi-tenant or cell-based architecture, DuckDB, ML/AI-enabled analytics tools (e.g., SageMaker), a regulated/high-governance data environment, experience hiring or growing a data team, presenting technical roadmaps to non-technical stakeholders, multi-account AWS at org scale, or familiarity with the education technology domain.

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $185,000–$200,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

Sr. Director Analyst – AI Integration & API Management
Gartner for Technical Professionals Practice

  • This is an individual contributor role, based remotely in North America.

About this Role:
Gartner is seeking a Sr. Director Analyst to join our Technical Professionals practice, focusing on AI integration, API management, and orchestration. This role is designed for a hands-on expert who can bridge the gap between technical implementation and market realities, delivering actionable insights to clients on establishing robust interfaces for AI integration. The ideal candidate will possess deep technical knowledge, practical experience, and a relentless curiosity about emerging AI technologies and their impact on enterprise architecture.

What You Will Do:

  • Conduct in-depth research and analysis on AI integration strategies, API management, and AI orchestration, with a focus on practical implementation and operational excellence.
  • Author research notes, market guides, and best practices that help clients navigate the complexities of integrating AI into existing ecosystems, including API-driven architectures and hybrid/multi-cloud environments.
  • Advise clients (including architects and integration leaders) on vendor selection, technology adoption, and implementation challenges, leveraging hands-on experience and market familiarity.
  • Deliver presentations, webinars, and client engagements that cut through industry hype, providing objective, evidence-based recommendations and actionable insights.
  • Monitor and analyze market trends, vendor offerings, and emerging technologies related to AI integration, API management, and AI, ensuring Gartner clients remain ahead of the curve.
  • Collaborate with fellow analysts and research teams to develop cross-domain perspectives on AI integration, security, scalability, and governance.
  • Maintain a pulse on the rapid evolution of AI, APIs, and integration platforms, adapting research and recommendations to reflect new developments and client needs.

What You Will Need:

  • 10+ years of hands-on experience in integration, API management, and AI orchestration, ideally within enterprise environments.
  • Demonstrated expertise in designing, implementing, and managing API-driven architectures, integration platforms, and AI interfaces.
  • Deep familiarity with market-leading vendors, open-source solutions, and emerging players in the API, integration, and AI space.
  • Proven ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and concisely, both in written research and verbal client interactions.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to synthesize market data, client feedback, and technical trends into actionable guidance.
  • Insatiable curiosity and adaptability, with a track record of continuous learning and engagement with new technologies.
  • Ability to critically evaluate vendor claims, industry hype, and evolving standards, providing clients with objective, practical recommendations.
  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or related field; advanced degree preferred.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with AI-native integration platforms, API gateways, and orchestration tools.
  • Background in designing interfaces for AI/ML pipelines, including considerations for security, scalability, and compliance.
  • Familiarity with cloud-native architectures, microservices, and event-driven systems.
  • Published research, blogs, or thought leadership in the integration/API/AI domain.

Who are we?

At Gartner, Inc. (NYSE:IT), we guide the leaders who shape the world.

Our mission relies on expert analysis and bold ideas to deliver actionable, objective business and technology insights, helping enterprise leaders and their teams succeed with their mission-critical priorities.

Since our founding in 1979, we’ve grown to 20,000 associates globally who support over 13,000 client enterprises in ~90 countries and territories. We do important, interesting and substantive work that matters. That’s why we hire associates with the intellectual curiosity, energy and drive to want to make a difference. The bar is unapologetically high. So is the impact you can have here.

What makes Gartner a great place to work?

Our vast, virtually untapped market potential offers limitless opportunities – opportunities that may not even exist right now – for you to grow professionally and flourish personally. How far you go is driven by your passion and performance.

We hire remarkable people who collaborate and win as a team. Together, our singular, unifying goal is to deliver results for our clients.

Our teams are inclusive and composed of individuals from different geographies, cultures, religions, ethnicities, races, genders, sexual orientations, abilities and generations.

We invest in great leaders who bring out the best in you and the company, enabling us to multiply our impact and results. This is why, year after year, we are recognized worldwide as a great place to work.

Gartner is the world authority on AI

At Gartner, you’ll join a company at the very center of the AI revolution. Gartner has proactive, objective guidance throughout clients’ AI journeys. We set the standard for how organizations leverage artificial intelligence to drive meaningful impact. You’ll have access to unmatched resources, expertise, and technology, and play a key role in helping Gartner and our clients innovate and grow as we leverage AI to transform business and technology landscapes.

It’s an exciting time to be at Gartner, with limitless opportunities to make a real impact, grow your skills, and build a lasting, meaningful career in a field that’s reshaping the way we operate. If you’re passionate about AI and want to be part of a team that’s guiding the leaders who shape the world, Gartner is the place for you.

What do we offer?

Gartner offers world-class benefits, highly competitive compensation and disproportionate rewards for top performers.

In our hybrid work environment, we provide the flexibility and support for you to thrive — working virtually when it's productive to do so and getting together with colleagues in a vibrant community that is purposeful, engaging and inspiring.

Ready to grow your career with Gartner? Join us.

Gartner believes in fair and equitable pay. A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is 172,000 USD - 202,500 USD. Please note that actual salaries may vary within the range, or be above or below the range, based on factors including, but not limited to, education, training, experience, professional achievement, business need, and location.
