External Supply Operations (ESO) is responsible for the global purchase and delivery of more than 200 million packs of medicine each year. Working with supply partners across Europe, Asia, MEA and South America. It contains 100 highly skilled and dedicated people, located in Europe and India, committed to the delivery of high quality, reliable, low-cost medication for patients in over 30 countries in Europe and to B2B customers globally. As part of this team, you will gain international experience in a high growth area of Zentiva’s business, working with a vast set of pharmaceutical manufacturers and formulations and will be part of the Industrial community consisting of internal manufacturing sites and global functions.

MISSION STATEMENT

As a valued member in the External Operations Supply Chain team, you will have overall responsibility for Supply Planning Operations for assigned suppliers & region and will report directly to the Supply Chain Head.

You will lead a supply planning team and play a crucial role in ensuring Zentiva's customers’ and patients’ needs are met, offering the highest service at competitive cost. You will be responsible for maximizing customer as well as supplier service, minimizing out of stock situations, creating and executing strategies to improve the quality of the planning processes, increasing business profitability and customer satisfaction while optimizing the Customer Service, Cash Flow (E.g. optimal Inventory) Cost and Capabilities. You will responsible for the team’s management and performance.

Working collaboratively with External Suppliers/CMO, Quality, Supplier Relationship Management, Internal Markets and Zentiva Global Functions (Regulatory ,Artwork and Portfolio Management), this position is responsible for managing and coordinating the supply planning activities for all external suppliers from assigned portfolio to ensure reliable product supply to market consistent with Zentiva objectives, customer service level and inventory management targets.

MAIN ACCOUNTABILITIES AND DUTIES

  • Lead a supply planning team setting tasks, supporting escalations, performance evaluation and development
  • Create transparency on available supply, identify, coordinate and addresses short- and long-term bottlenecks, closely collaborating with Suppliers and Zentiva Commercial Directors to mitigate shortage risks
  • Coordinate all stakeholders during crisis, and responsible for applying rules of allocation for Local/Global crisis; create scenarios to support decision making process
  • Identify drivers of longer term performance improvement; Define the direction and implement action plan to guide supply planning team.
  • Support target setting and monitoring of key metrics to drive continuous cost and service improvement
  • Run, maintain and as required upgrade, planning tools
  • Support supply introduction of new product portfolios
  • Identify and drive value improvements together with team such as order grouping, transport lane and mode optimisation, Minimum Order Quantity adjustments
  • Lead, manage and drive a culture of continuous improvement, contribution to the sider ESO supply chain team across locations, building capabilities and facilitating Zentiva-wide knowledge and best-practice sharing across all facets of the operations (safety, quality, cost, service) to support the Zentiva strategy
  • The employee will perform other tasks under the direction of the Head of Supply Chain within the agreed type of work.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

  • Experience in all Supply Chain areas: demand & stock management, reporting, planning, requirement planning or MRP advanced knowledge
  • Five (5) or more years of experience excelling in supply chain and business/industry (previous experience in pharmaceutical company is a plus)
  • Preferred Bachelor degree in economics/ engineering/ logistics/ management.
  • Proven management skills and a competence in people management with strong communication skills and positive energy giver
  • Strategic and analytical mind, attention to detail and creative problem solver
  • Customer orientated mindset
  • Advanced English

Pacific Oaks College and Children’s School is recruiting an Adjunct Professor for our campus in Pasadena, California.

About Pacific Oaks College and Children's School

Pacific Oaks College and Children's School, located in Pasadena, California, is a nonprofit institution rooted in Quaker values and a strong social justice heritage. The College offers bachelor’s, master’s, a doctorate, and certificate programs in education, human development, counseling, and related fields, while the Children’s School is internationally recognized for its pioneering work in anti-bias education, emergent curriculum, and peaceful conflict resolution. Together, they foster inclusive, culturally responsive learning environments that honor the unique potential of every individual. Employees join a mission-driven community committed to respect, diversity, social justice, and lifelong learning.

About the Position

The Pacific Oaks College Master’s in Social Work (MSW) Program invites applicants to apply for the online adjunct professors pool for the Spring, Summer and Fall semesters. Pacific Oaks College MSW students represent a wide range and diverse cross-section of the national population. Our non-traditional students work full-time, have families, and possess a variety of employment and life experiences. The program, having received full accreditation in 2024, is experiencing rapid enrollment growth and is seeking well-qualified, highly motivated, well-organized individuals with online teaching experience to teach courses in the online, asynchronous program.

MSW courses are fully built, and our adjuncts are not responsible for creating syllabi or curriculum.

Responsibilities

  • Teach and facilitate interactive, high-quality online courses within the Master’s in Social Work (MSW) Program using the Canvas Learning Management System.

  • Provide timely, constructive feedback on assignments and submit grades in accordance with established deadlines.
  • Engage students through meaningful dialogue, reflective practices, and collaborative learning approaches that support academic success.
  • Identify students who may be at risk academically and refer them to appropriate institutional support services.
  • Collaborate with faculty colleagues to review, refine, and enhance course content in alignment with program goals and academic standards.
  • Complete required faculty onboarding, adjunct training modules, and participate in scheduled adjunct and all-faculty meetings.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Master’s Degree in Social Work from a CSWE-accredited institution is required.
  • A minimum of 3 years of clinical experience in social work practice is required, showcasing exemplary professional expertise.
  • Demonstrated ability to teach undergraduate courses in an online format using a Learning Management System (e.g., Canvas).
  • Strong communication skills and commitment to cultural responsiveness.
  • Experience working with diverse student populations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in Social Work or a closely related field and/or Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) credential is preferred.
  • Prior graduate-level teaching experience, particularly in online or hybrid environments.
  • Familiarity with Pacific Oaks pedagogy and integration of social responsibility in business education.
  • Proficiency in Canvas LMS, Microsoft Office Suite, and online teaching tools.
  • Proven track record of professional excellence in social work, with a commitment to ongoing professional development and learning.

About This Role:

The Associate Director Clinical Development, Immunology, based within Biogen’s West Coast Hub (WCH), will contribute to the clinical trial design and execution of one or more Immunology programs, focus on early-phase (I-II) studies in autoantibody-driven disease such as myasthenia gravis and chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP). Reporting to Sr Director Clinical Development Lead Immunology and Indications Expansion (WCH).

The Associate Director, Clinical Development is a pivotal role requiring strong blend of scientific acumen, tactical trial execution, and collaborative leadership. Your primary responsibilities will include contributing to clinical development frameworks for new indications, designing robust protocols, and interpreting study data in clos partnership with internal research and development teams. As a key member of the clinical development team, you will execute key trials that drive the trajectory of our WCH immunology pipeline. You will also support the company’s broader mission by providing clinical insights to early-stage research assets, external partnerships, and due diligence activities.

What You’ll Do:

  • Partner with cross-functional teams including clinical operations, biostatistics, data management, regulatory, and safety to advance early-phase development programs.

  • Contribute to clinical trial protocol design, development and execution for early phase neuroimmunology studies.

  • Provide medical monitoring, clinical execution, and oversight of clinical studies to ensure patient safety

  • Serve as a contact for CRO and investigators to provide responses for protocol related questions.

  • Provide scientific therapeutic expertise to internal and external stakeholders.

  • Support data interpretation and clinical reporting for early phase clinical studies.

  • Support preparation for health authority interaction and contribute to responses for regulatory questions related to clinical development activities.

  • Contribute scientific contents for clinical protocols and other clinical development documents.

  • Support risk mitigation strategies and provide clinical input for safety management plans

  • Assist in providing scientific content for clinical study documents such as protocols, amendments, investigator brochure, clinical study reports, and briefing materials.

  • Champion patient-centered development approaches by incorporating disease burden, feasibility and patient experience considerations into study design.

  • Monitor the external landscape in neuroimmunology and autoimmune disease, including competitive intelligence, evolving standards of care, and relevant scientific advances.

Who You Are:

You are passionate about advancing clinical development in immunology and improving the lives of patients with immune-mediated or autoimmune diseases. You thrive in ambiguity and continuously seek to learn and improve. Your expertise in neuroimmunology and autoimmune disorders helps provide input for complex scientific and clinical information into actionable development strategies. You will have the ability to influence without authority and partner effectively across disciplines. Experienced in framing trade-offs and decision points for senior leadership, you are adaptable, able to flex between program-level strategy and disease area depth as needed.

Required Skills:

  • MD/DO (or international equivalent) or PharmD with relevant experience required. Subspecialty experience in neurology or neuromuscular medicine, or prior drug development experience in neuromuscular or neuroimmunology diseases, is strongly preferred.

  • 0-2 + years’ experience in the biotech/pharmaceutical industry with additional experience in academic or clinical research.

  • Prior experience in medical monitoring or investigator/sub-investigator role

  • Experience contributing to clinical study execution and/or oversight and working cross-functionally with R&D partners.

  • Strong communication skills (written and verbal)

  • Deep scientific and clinical understanding of neuroimmunology/ autoimmune disorders

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in fast paced environment

  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally, as required for business needs.

Preferred Skills:

  • Relevant disease area experience (e.g., Myasthenia Gravis, CIDP, neuroimmunology, or other immune-mediated conditions)

  • Understanding of regulatory requirements for drug development.

  • Established network of global Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs)

Open to remote U.S.-based talent, with a preference for candidates located near our West Coast site in California.

Job Level: Management

Additional Information

The base compensation range for this role is: $184,000.00-$253,000.00

Base salary offered is determined through an analytical approach utilizing a combination of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills & experience, job location, and internal equity.


Regular employees are eligible to receive both short term and long-term incentives, including cash bonus and equity incentive opportunities, designed to reward recent achievements and recognize your future potential based on individual, business unit and company performance.

Why Biogen?

We are a global team with a commitment to excellence, and a pioneering spirit. As a mid-sized biotechnology company, we provide the stability and resources of a well-established business while fostering an environment where individual contributions make a significant impact. Our team encompasses some of the most talented and passionate achievers who have unparalleled opportunities for learning, growth, and expanding their skills. description:
Who is Forcepoint?

Forcepoint simplifies security for global businesses and governments. Forcepoint’s all-in-one, truly cloud-native platform makes it easy to adopt Zero Trust and prevent the theft or loss of sensitive data and intellectual property no matter where people are working. 20+ years in business. 2.7k employees. 150 countries. 11k+ customers. 300+ patents. If our mission excites you, you’re in the right place; we want you to bring your own energy to help us create a safer world. All we’re missing is you!

Forcepoint has a fantastic opportunity to join our team in Vietnam.

This is a pre-sales engineering position where you will be working extremely closely with sales. You are expected to work as team to create and execute a territory / account plan. This includes building relationships with partners and ensuring they can position and implement our solutions.

From a technology perspective we are looking for someone ideally with a Web, CASB, ZTNA and data protection security background, with experience on positioning security products on large customers. You will be joining a great, successful team of SEs in the APAC who will be happy to bring you up to speed. While we are responsible and accountable for our patch – we support and help each other, and only good team players will succeed.

Like the industry and our customers, we are transitioning from network and data security products to a “Data-First” SASE architecture. Not all companies are moving at the same speed and many continue with our really good NGFW, DLP, Web Security and other products. You should feel at home in both worlds.

What you will be doing:

  • Lead discussions with customers to drive understanding and documentation of the customer’s environment and needs, specifically their cross domain, network security, DLP/Intellectual property protection needs and recommend appropriate products/services that meet these needs.

  • Deliver product, technology and/or customized solution presentations to technical and business decision makers which may include system demonstrations, white-boarding and technical Q&A sessions to the client.

  • Provide pre-sales technical support, security engineering and technical guidance for the development and implementation of Forcepoint cybersecurity technologies for customer.

  • Work with customer, strategic partners, resellers and Forcepoint team members to architect, design, build, and deploy cyber security solutions for customers and partners in support of pilot and proof of concept demonstrations.

  • Unite your passion for audio innovation with high-tech product development

  • Create pitch-perfect, cutting-edge technology that elevates the listening experience

About the Role

At Roon, we are at the forefront of revolutionizing the way people experience music. Since our inception, we have dedicated ourselves to developing software that transforms music streaming into an immersive journey, tailored specifically to the listener's preferences and unique tastes.

Under the umbrella of Harman International, Roon continues to operate with the spirit of a nimble startup, backed by the resources and reach of a global powerhouse. Our team comprises passionate individuals who believe in the power of music to connect and inspire. We are developers, designers, engineers, and audiophiles united by a common goal — to make listening to music more engaging, personal, and connected.

This is the most senior product role on Roon, and it is a hands-on one. You will set the direction the product takes, and then do the work that gets it there: the research, the strategy, the feature definition, the prototypes. You will have engineers and a designer to build with, and no support function to hand the thinking to.

What You Will Do

  • Own product strategy: Define who Roon is for and what we do better than anyone else for them.

  • Grow the audience: Determine who the serious listener of the next decade is, how they discover and consume music, and what Roon has to become to belong in their setup. Do this without losing the listeners who pay for Roon today.

  • Represent the listener: Maintain an accurate picture of who our users are and what they need, drawing on direct conversations, community forums, support tickets, reviews, and product data.

  • Define the feature set: Translate strategy into a specific set of features with a clear rationale for each, and decide what gets built, what gets cut, and what we will not take on.

  • Own the roadmap: Sequence the work across multiple quarters, keep it current, and build the implementation plan with engineering, in specifications clear enough for the team to start work.

  • Build the measurement practice: Instrument what matters, define the metrics that decide whether a feature worked, and move Roon from gut to evidence.

  • Prototype your own ideas: Build working, interactive prototypes yourself with AI tooling, close to our design language, and bring them to the team as the starting point for an idea.

  • Hold the quality bar: Have and defend opinions on interaction, information density, defaults, naming, and how the product feels to use, working with design as a peer.

  • Investigate our codebase: Use AI coding tools to establish how Roon behaves today, including business rules, constraints, and edge cases, before specifying changes.

  • Build your own tooling: Create the research pipelines, internal tools, automations, and evaluation harnesses you need to work effectively.

What You Need to Be Successful

  • Experience: 10+ years in product management, including having owned the strategy for a whole product or business rather than a feature area. You have done your own research rather than commissioning it, launched something new, and stayed with a mature product long enough to live with your earlier decisions. Founders and early-stage operators who have worked at this altitude without the title are welcome to apply.

  • A personal connection to music: A serious, long-standing involvement with music, as a collector, musician, producer, DJ, critic, or simply someone who has spent years listening closely. Roon is built for people who care which recording, which pressing, and who played on it, and we have found that people without that connection struggle to judge what this product should be. You do not need to be an audiophile or a current Roon user.

  • Product taste and direction: A clear sense of what good looks like, the ability to say where the product should go, and the judgment to choose between competing versions of something and explain the reasoning.

  • Building with AI: AI is already part of your daily work, from research synthesis through to prototyping and the tooling you build for yourself. You have taken ideas to working prototypes with tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Lovable, or v0, and can show the work. You validate what these tools produce and know when not to use them.

  • Ownership: Comfortable committing to a position with incomplete information and defending it to engineering, design, and senior leadership. Works with limited guidance in a small, remote, self-managing team.

  • Communication skills: You can write for a public community of expert users who will scrutinize everything we say, and for senior leadership, and be persuasive to both.

  • Measurement: You have built this practice somewhere it did not exist, not only operated one that did. You decide what success looks like before anything gets built, and you can get to the answer yourself by querying product data in SQL or equivalent, running an experiment, and reading the result honestly. Familiar with subscription metrics such as trial-to-paid conversion, retention, churn, and lifetime value.

  • Technical fluency: Enough technical grounding to pick up how our systems work and why the constraints exist, so you can judge what a decision makes easy, expensive, or impossible. Engineers will explain the details; you need to absorb them and design accordingly. A deeper engineering background is a plus, not a requirement.

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Something you built and shipped on your own, outside of a team — a side project, a tool, a small product — that people other than you actually used.

  • Experience in music, audio, media, or another category serving enthusiast users across both hardware and software.

  • Experience with subscription businesses, or with hardware and software sold together.

  • Experience with a product that has a vocal, publicly organized user community.

  • You have built something on the Roon API, or you are a Roon user with opinions.

What Makes You Eligible

  • Willingness to travel up to 5%, domestically and internationally.

  • Able to work virtually in any US time zone.

  • Successfully complete a background investigation and drug screen as a condition of employment.

What We Offer

  • Flexible work environment, allowing for full-time remote work globally for positions that can be performed outside a HARMAN or customer location.

  • Access to employee discounts on world-class Harman and Samsung products (JBL, HARMAN Kardon, AKG, and more).

  • Extensive training opportunities through our own HARMAN University.

  • "Be Brilliant" employee recognition and rewards program.

  • An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.

This position evaluates medical records, provides clinical and surgical abstraction for full range of complex and/or multispecialty surgical, procedural and E&M professional services in accordance with nationally recognized coding guidelines. Utilize coding knowledge and expertise to support department projects, validation edits and/or revisions.

CORE FUNCTIONS

1. Analyzes medical information from medical records. Accurately codes diagnostic and procedural information in accordance with national coding guidelines and appropriate reimbursement requirements. Consults with medical providers to clarify missing or inadequate record information and to determine appropriate diagnostic and procedure codes. Provides thorough, timely and accurate coding in accordance to department specific productivity and quality standards. Codes ICD CM and CPT4 for accurate APC assignment. Addresses National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) edits as appropriate. Reconciliation of charges as required.

2. Abstracts clinical diagnoses, procedure codes and documents other pertinent information obtained from the medical record into the electronic medical records. Seeks out missing information and creates complete records, including items such as disease and procedure codes, discharge disposition, date of surgery, attending physician, consulting physicians, surgeons and anesthesiologists, and appropriate signatures/authorizations. Refers inconsistent patient treatment information/documentation to coding quality analysts, supervisor or individual department for clarification/additional information for accurate code assignment.

3. Provides quality assurance for medical records. For all assigned records and/or areas assures compliance with coding rules and regulations according to regulatory agencies for state Medicaid plans, Center for Medicare Services (CMS), Office of the Inspector General (OIG) and the Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA), as well as company and applicable professional standards.

4. As assigned, compiles daily and monthly reports; tabulates data from medical records for research or analysis purposes.

5. Able to identify validation edits and revision issues to ensure compliant coding.

6. Recognizes and distinguishes complex diagnoses and procedures and has attention to detail to make needed corrections and ensure accurate coding, reimbursement, and compliance.

7. Works independently under regular supervision. Uses specialized knowledge for accurate assignment of ICD/CPT codes according to national guidelines. May seek guidance for correct interpretation of coding guidelines and LCDs (Local Coverage Determinations).

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

High school diploma/GED or equivalent working knowledge and specialized formal training equivalent to the two year certification course in medical record keeping principles and practices, anatomy, physiology, pathology, medical terminology, standard nomenclature, and classification of diagnoses and operations, or an Associate’s degree in a related health care field.

Requires at least one of the following: Certified Professional Coder (CPC), Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), Certified Coding Specialist – Physician (CCS-P), Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA), or Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT), in an active status with the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) or American Academy of Professional Coders (AAPC). Certification may also include a general area of specialty.

Requires three or more years of complex professional coding experience within specialty.

Must demonstrate a level of knowledge and understanding of ICD and CPT coding principles as recommended by the American Health Information Management Association coding competencies, and as normally demonstrated by certification by the American Academy of Professional Coders.

Must be able to work effectively and efficiently in a remote setting, utilizing common office programs, coding software and abstracting systems.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Specialty Certification. Radiology Certified Coder (RCC) if employed in the Imaging space.
Experience in a large, multi-system physician practice preferred.

Additional related education and/or experience preferred.

  • Implement the organization’s rare disease data partnership strategy, including the identification of critical data needs across US Commercial rare disease brands, functions, and priority use cases.
  • Establish, manage, and strengthen strategic rare disease data partnerships with external data providers, platforms, and vendors to maximize the value of external rare disease data assets.

description:
Job Description

McCarthy Tétrault is a leading Canadian law firm offering a full suite of legal and business solutions to clients in Canada and around the world. With offices in Toronto, Montréal, Québec City, Calgary and Vancouver, we provide challenging and rewarding career opportunities across the country. Recognized as one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers for eleven consecutive years and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers for fourteen consecutive years, our culture is guided by The McCarthy Way—our shared approach to working with clients and with each other.

The McCarthy Way is built on four core elements: Excellence, through attracting and developing top talent committed to delivering on our Client Commitment; Collaboration, through seamless, integrated teamwork; Inclusion, through eliminating barriers to belonging and success; and Innovation, through delivering maximum value by embracing leading-edge technologies and approaches. Together, these principles shape how we work, lead, and grow—every day.

The employee in this position will be part of a national team in which they will work with lawyers and professionals in all of our offices across Canada, where English is the predominant language. An employee in this position will be expected to work on documents in English or French for clients, lawyers or professionals who understand and communicate only in English or French. This national document services team operates 24/7 and it is necessary for the proper functioning of the operations to have bilingual staff available at all times to respond to requests. Bilingualism (French and English) is therefore a requirement for this position.

We are recruiting for a Bilingual Document Specialist to join our team in our Montreal, Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary or Quebec City offices. The successful candidate must have a minimum of 2 years of experience in document management and will be responsible for providing firm-wide document support, such as creating and formatting documents, as well as correcting spelling and grammar errors.

Weekday Evening Shift (Bilingual EN/FR Required)

  • Monday to Friday: 6:00 p.m. – 2:00 a.m. ET

Weekday Evening Shift (Unilingual)

  • Monday to Friday : 5:00 pm - 1:00 am ET

Weekday Afternoon Shift (Unilingual)

  • Monday to Friday: 12:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m. ET

Weekend Overnight Shift (Bilingual EN/FR Required)

  • Friday to Sunday: 8:00 p.m. – 6:00 a.m. ET

All shifts are fully remote.

As a Bilingual Document Specialist, you will be:

  • Creating various legal and other documents through copy typing, transcription, scanning or other methods. Document work includes converting styles, performing mail merges, inserting media into presentations, cross-referencing, indexing, creating tables (including financial tables), working with graphs and objects, using graphics applications etc.
  • Proofreading and checking documents for appropriate formatting, spelling, grammar, and sense/clarity. Includes document version comparisons, checking for accurate revisions, and correcting document corruption.
  • Developing understanding and working knowledge of the Firm’s procedures for the production of documents from the Firm’s precedents.
  • Responding promptly to requests, meeting deadlines, and working cooperatively with other departments and individuals within the Firm.
  • Applying word processing expertise to be able to work on complex legal and other documents.
  • Proactively managing workload fluctuations while working with minimal supervision and direction.
  • Performing quality control of own work, seeking clarification when necessary, and reviewing work of others as required.
  • Offering assistance to other members of the team, including mentorship when required.
  • As required, managing the intake process of all document production requests and document support requests which includes prioritizing and coordinating work for completion.
  • Providing Firm-wide support for document production using Microsoft applications (e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio etc.).
  • Documenting, logging, tracking and responding to calls, emails, voicemail and drop-bys for document support in a timely manner.
  • Managing escalation and retaining problem ownership of document production and document production support (track call, research and update knowledgebase).
  • Reviewing support issues/procedures and recommending solutions with respect to document production and document production support when applicable.
  • Other duties as assigned.

As our ideal candidate, you will distinguish yourself by the following profile:

  • College certificate (office administration, legal specialization, or related).
  • Three years of experience in a professional work environment. Experience in a document production role will be an asset.
  • Knowledge of legal terminology, documents and procedures an asset.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Knowledge of legal terminology, documents and procedures an asset.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and telephone manners; ability to correspond effectively and respectfully with DSG clients.
  • Ability to transfer knowledge in an efficient, pleasant and effective way using a variety of techniques and software applications.
  • Patience, flexibility and an ability to effectively manage difficult situations.
  • Well organized with meticulous attention to detail and strong proof-reading skills.
  • Personable, approachable disposition, with an ability to handle pressure/stress.
  • Well-developed analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to visualize and deliver creative solutions.
  • Capability to adapt to different work schedules (week, weekends and statutory holidays where applicable).
  • Confident in working independently, prioritizing and making day-to-day decisions, with the judgment to seek supervisory assistance when appropriate.
  • Ability to type with a speed of 80-100 words per minute.
  • Bilinguism (French and English) is required.

As a member of the McCarthy team, you will have access to:

  • Outstanding benefits from day one, including insurance premiums paid by the Firm and wellness and technology reimbursements.
  • Competitive compensation, paid overtime and generous time off, including a day off to volunteer and a day off for your birthday.
  • A commitment to professional development and growth opportunities for our people at all levels, supported by a culture that fully embraces and encourages two-way feedback.
  • Strong community involvement and a commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion.
  • A collaborative, cohesive culture that connects lawyers and business teams through collective purpose.

How to Apply:

We encourage external candidates to apply online and internal applicants must apply directly through our internal careers portal on Espresso. We look forward to receiving your application.

We thank all applicants for their interest in McCarthy Tétrault; however, only chosen applicants will be contacted. We regret that we are unable to respond to individual inquiries about application status. McCarthy Tétrault is an equal opportunity employer that fosters an inclusive, equitable, and accessible environment. Please notify us if you require accommodation at any time during the recruitment process.

COMPANY OVERVIEW:

WellRight is a corporate wellness leader delivering customizable and complete wellness programs, used by organizations to improve the health and well-being of their employees and clients. Our mission is to help people live their best lives with industry-leading technology through personalized, holistic well-being. What sets us apart is our dedication to tailoring solutions to the unique needs of each customer we serve.

At WellRight, we embrace and celebrate diversity in all its forms. We are united by a common purpose: to create a meaningful impact through well-being programs that engage and inspire participants while delivering tangible results. Our goal is to foster well-being in the workplace with a versatile and empowering solution, allowing each individual to embark on their own well-being journey. We invite you to explore how you might contribute to our mission.

JOB SUMMARY:

The Senior Director, Consultant Relations is responsible for developing, executing, and evolving WellRight's strategic plan to expand and increase business from the broker and benefit consultant ("Consultant") community. In close partnership with WellRight's Sales and Marketing teams, they organize, manage, and lead business development activities focused on Consultants. They conduct direct outreach to that community to educate and promote WellRight's value proposition and competitive differentiation, and to build the WellRight brand to drive more opportunities offered to WellRight and greater conversion of those opportunities.

The Senior Director, Consultant Relations leads, promotes, strategizes, and implements. They have a deep understanding of Consultants and their clients, and stay current on evolving benefit and wellbeing trends through multiple sources and contacts. They translate complex ideas into relevant, actionable market insights, connecting patterns across different data sets and settings to inform winning communication, engagement, and growth strategies. They bring an existing network of Consultant contacts who would welcome a call day one. They see projects through to completion, use metrics to measure success, and evolve strategies over time based on results.

This individual communicates clearly and organizes effectively across multiple concurrent priorities. They read stakeholder needs accurately and adapt their approach accordingly, setting strategic priorities and scope and leading execution across those priorities. They work independently, stay organized, and collaborate well with others. They write and speak clearly, act with high integrity, and bring resourcefulness to solving problems under ambiguity.

The ideal candidate is a proven relationship-builder who develops trust with stakeholders across organizations to get things done. They are credible and persuasive when presenting to senior executives and clients, and comfortable leading high-stakes meetings and driving decisions in the room. They are proactive, versatile, and intellectually curious, with strong problem-solving skills and a focus on the highest-impact priorities. They combine strong execution, strategic insight, and organizational savvy with tactical experience to drive action and results.

Responsibilities:

Serve as WellRight’s expert resource for trends in benefit consulting and wellbeing:

  • Track current Consultant thinking on wellbeing and regularly communicate relevant information to WellRight sales, marketing, customer success, and product teams.
  • Develop a clear understanding of Consultants’ needs and challenges and how WellRight can provide solutions through existing strategies, new strategies or custom solutions.
  • Solicit product and market feedback from Consultants and communicate this feedback to sales, marketing, customer success, and product teams (e.g., feature requests, market trends, competition intelligence, new opportunities).
  • Serve as “the voice” of the Consultant community within WellRight in strategy discussions with sales, marketing, product, customer success, and management.
  • Connect and make Regional Sales Manager introductions to new territory broker relationships.
  • Develop strategies based on this feedback that can be executed to drive great penetration and market presence.

Build relationships between WellRight and the Consultant community:

  • Identify key broker/consulting firms and local offices for wellbeing engagements and identify key healthcare/benefits/wellbeing leaders and producers within those offices.
  • Manage day-to-day interactions with office/regional/national leadership at key consulting firms by owning existing relationships with those firms.
  • Serve as the WellRight “evangelist” with key firms and consultants– confidently, accurately, and compellingly conveying information on WellRight and its value proposition.
  • Build relationships between the WellRight sales team and key Consultants at the corporate and local office level.
  • Lead, partner, and collaborate with sales and marketing on outreach initiatives targeting the Consultant community to increase brand awareness, create interest in WellRight's value proposition, and generate leads.
  • Identify/develop opportunities to present WellRight to the Consultant community via events such as office meetings, conferences, etc.
  • Develop and implement measures of success for outreach initiatives for each targeted firm.

Enhance WellRight sales in consultant-driven opportunities:

  • Analyze CRM data and the consultant contact database to support the development of an outreach strategy to target specific consulting firms nationally and by territory.
  • Develop a pipeline of Consultants likely to produce leads and sales in alignment with annually established objectives.
  • Create processes with sales and business development teams to document all Consultant contacts and activities in WellRight sales tools and systems, resulting in a territory “heat map”.
  • Coordinate WellRight organizational resources and activities to support broker/consultant relationship-building activities.
  • Review WellRight sales and marketing materials (e.g., proposals, RFP responses, collateral, etc) targeted toward Consultants to ensure consistent and impactful messaging.
  • Support finalist meetings to win new business by serving as a subject matter expert for WellRight strategy to the participating Consultants.
  • Develop and provide key metrics to show progress and results and to drive ongoing program evolution.

Requirements:

  • 10+ years in strategy, sales, benefit consulting, or other relevant experience. Deep knowledge of wellbeing and benefit consulting.
  • Established network of relationships within the Consultant community, with a track record of selling into that community.
  • Track record of setting strategic direction and translating it into operational execution, including in ambiguous or fast-changing situations.
  • Proven project management skills, with experience managing multiple complex, concurrent projects and defining metrics to track results.
  • Strong written and verbal communicator, able to explain complex ideas clearly and build consensus while raising dissenting views constructively.
  • Skilled relationship-builder who asks the right questions to understand stakeholder needs and establishes trust quickly.
  • Analytical mindset — comfortable using data to measure outcomes, drive decisions, and challenge assumptions with evidence.
  • Demonstrated ownership: takes initiative, follows through on commitments, and collaborates effectively across functions (e.g., sales, marketing, product, customer success) to drive shared outcomes.

WellRight is based in Chicago with a remote team distributed across the country.

We are dedicated to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. People of all backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives are welcome here. We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

Project Job Title: Drone Pilot / Surveyor
Location: Remote
Job Type: Full-Time
Reports To: Director of Engineering
Travel: Extensive travel to active project sites required

Position Summary
The Drone Pilot / Surveyor is responsible for performing aerial data collection, mapping, surveying support, and construction documentation across utility-scale solar EPC projects. This position utilizes Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), survey equipment, and specialized mapping software to collect accurate field data used to support engineering, estimating, construction, project controls, and site management.
Working within a fast-paced, self-perform EPC construction environment, the Drone Pilot / Surveyor will support projects throughout the construction lifecycle—from existing-condition and preconstruction surveys through earthwork, pile installation, electrical construction, progress tracking, quantity verification, and final project documentation.
The ideal candidate combines strong UAS flight capabilities with practical surveying and construction knowledge and understands how accurate, timely field data directly impacts the successful execution of large-scale solar projects.
Key Responsibilities
  • Plan and conduct UAS/drone flight operations across large utility-scale solar construction sites in accordance with FAA regulations, company procedures, and project requirements.
  • Collect high-resolution aerial imagery and survey data for mapping, topographic surveys, construction progress, inspections, and project documentation.
  • Perform photogrammetry and aerial mapping to produce Ortho mosaics, digital terrain models (DTMs), digital surface models (DSMs), point clouds, and other project deliverables.
  • Support site surveying activities utilizing GPS/GNSS, RTK, robotic total stations, and other survey equipment as required.
  • Establish, verify, and maintain survey control throughout the duration of construction.
  • Support construction layout and verification activities for roads, grading, drainage, equipment pads, pile locations, electrical infrastructure, substations, and other project components.
  • Perform existing-condition and preconstruction aerial surveys to document site conditions prior to mobilization and construction.
  • Conduct routine progress flights to document construction status and provide project teams with current aerial imagery.
  • Assist with earthwork quantity calculations, stockpile measurements, cut/fill analysis, and verification of completed work.
  • Support grading operations by providing accurate surface data and comparing existing conditions against design surfaces.
  • Provide survey and aerial data to support pile installation, tracker/racking construction, module installation, underground electrical systems, inverter/transformer locations, and other solar construction activities.
  • Compare collected field data against IFC drawings, design models, and project specifications to identify potential discrepancies.
  • Support quality control activities by documenting installed conditions and assisting with verification of completed construction.
  • Process and manage drone imagery and survey data using applicable photogrammetry, CAD, GIS, and mapping software.
  • Coordinate with Project Managers, Superintendents, Survey Managers, Engineers, Project Controls, and field personnel to determine survey and aerial data requirements.
  • Maintain accurate flight logs, survey records, field notes, control documentation, and project files.
  • Organize and maintain aerial imagery and survey data so information is readily accessible to project teams.
  • Identify potential site, design, or construction issues through review of aerial and survey data and communicate findings to project leadership.
  • Maintain UAS equipment, batteries, survey instruments, and associated technology in proper working condition.
  • Perform pre-flight inspections and evaluate weather, airspace, site conditions, and potential hazards prior to flight operations.
  • Ensure all UAS operations comply with FAA Part 107 requirements and applicable federal, state, local, client, and company requirements.
  • Coordinate flight activities with project safety and field leadership to ensure drone operations do not interfere with cranes, equipment, electrical work, or other construction activities.
  • Support multiple projects and travel between active construction sites based on project needs.
Required Qualifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, GIS, or related technical discipline preferred.
  • Current FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate required.
  • Previous experience operating drones/UAS for surveying, mapping, engineering, or construction applications.
  • Working knowledge of surveying principles, coordinate systems, elevations, benchmarks, and construction layout.
  • Experience collecting and processing aerial imagery for photogrammetry and mapping applications.
  • Experience with GPS/GNSS and RTK survey equipment.
  • Ability to read and interpret civil plans, grading plans, site layouts, construction drawings, and specifications.
  • Understanding of survey control and the importance of horizontal and vertical accuracy in construction applications.
  • Strong computer and data-management skills.
  • Ability to work independently in large, active construction environments while coordinating effectively with field personnel.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments and priorities across multiple projects.
  • Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
  • Ability and willingness to travel extensively based on project requirements.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Previous experience supporting utility-scale solar, renewable energy, heavy civil, power generation, or large-scale EPC construction projects.
  • Experience working for a self-perform EPC or heavy civil contractor.
  • Experience with DJI Enterprise, Trimble, Leica, Topcon, or similar professional UAS and survey equipment.
  • Experience with photogrammetry and mapping platforms such as Pix4D, DroneDeploy, Propeller, Trimble Business Center, or similar applications.
  • Working knowledge of AutoCAD, Civil 3D, GIS, or comparable design/mapping software.
  • Experience creating Ortho mosaics, point clouds, surface models, contour maps, and volumetric reports.
  • Experience performing cut/fill analysis and earthwork quantity verification.
  • Experience with Ground Control Points (GCPs), checkpoints, RTK/PPK workflows, and survey-grade drone mapping.
  • Familiarity with solar site grading, pile installation, tracker systems, access roads, drainage systems, underground electrical collection systems, substations, and related utility-scale solar construction.
  • Surveyor-in-Training (SIT/LSIT) certification or related surveying credentials are a plus but not required.
Physical & Travel Requirements
  • Ability to travel extensively and potentially remain near project sites for extended periods based on construction schedules.
  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather and environmental conditions.
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods while performing field operations.
  • Ability to carry and set up drone, survey, GPS, and related field equipment.
  • Ability to work around heavy construction equipment while maintaining appropriate situational awareness.
  • Ability to wear all required personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Must be able to travel by vehicle and air as required

description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

As a Staff Software Engineer on the Nest Applications team, you will lead the evolution of the systems behind reliable healthcare delivery operations. You will own major technical decisions across interconnected operational workflows and help build software that remains simple, resilient, and adaptable as the network grows.

This is a hands-on, product-oriented full-stack role with deep backend ownership. We are looking for an engineer who brings exceptional Go expertise and can raise the technical bar across APIs, integrations, distributed systems, and engineering practices.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end software for fulfillment, maintenance, inventory, and flight workflows.
  • Lead architecture across multiple teams, from data models and API contracts through implementation, rollout, and ongoing operation.
  • Design robust APIs, backend services, and integration patterns that connect field operations, internal teams, and customer-facing products.
  • Build modular, event-driven systems that can evolve with operational and business needs.
  • Improve reliability, observability, automated testing, and operational decision-making for critical workflows.
  • Establish strong engineering standards through design reviews, code review, mentoring, and technical leadership.
  • Partner directly with operations, supply chain, finance, and customer-facing teams to resolve high-impact problems.

What You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of production software engineering experience, including staff-level technical scope.
  • Experience in both a high-engineering-bar organization where you worked at scale AND a startup or scale-up environment where you built from the ground up, with limited devops support and handled fast pace and ambiguity.
  • Deep production expertise in Go; you should be able to set technical direction for our backend services and develop other engineers’ Go capability.
  • Experience designing and operating distributed, event-driven systems; Kafka or comparable technologies are strongly relevant.
  • Strong database design and performance experience, including Postgres.
  • A record of owning architecture across teams, leading significant migrations, mentoring engineers, and working directly with customers or external stakeholders.
  • Clear, effective communication in English.
  • Ability to work from the US East Coast or London, UK, and travel to Africa approximately three times per year.

Additional Valuable Experience

  • Integrating with external partner APIs or partner systems.
  • Designing reliable integrations points and API contracts, authentication, error handling, observability, and integration workflows.
  • Healthcare, fulfillment, logistics, warehouse-management, or e-commerce systems.

What Else You Need To Know

For US-based candidates, the starting cash range for this role is $180,000 - $220,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; overtime pay; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply!

Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

description:
Keeper Security is hiring a Senior Software Architect to provide technical leadership for our Browser Extension team and help shape the architecture of one of Keeper’s most widely used client experiences. This is a 100% remote position, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the Chicago, IL or El Dorado Hills, CA metro areas.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help define the technical foundation for secure, high-performance browser experiences used by customers around the world.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.

About the Job

As a Senior Software Architect for Keeper’s Browser Extension team, you will define and guide the architecture of secure browser-based experiences across Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and other supported platforms.

This is a highly hands-on technical leadership role focused on application architecture, browser extension frameworks, security, performance and cross-platform reliability. You will work closely with Engineering, Product, Security, QA and UX teams to solve complex technical challenges, establish scalable design patterns and guide the long-term evolution of Keeper’s browser platform. You will remain close to the code while providing architectural direction across the team, ensuring that new capabilities are secure, maintainable and aligned with Keeper’s zero-knowledge security model.

Responsibilities:

  • Define and drive the technical architecture and long-term direction of Keeper’s browser extension platform
  • Lead architectural design for complex browser-based features, shared services and cross-platform capabilities
  • Design scalable solutions using JavaScript, TypeScript and modern web application technologies
  • Guide architecture across Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and other supported browser environments
  • Establish patterns for secure communication between browser extension components, web applications, backend services and native integrations
  • Lead technical decisions involving extension lifecycle, background services, content scripts, messaging, storage and browser APIs
  • Ensure architectural decisions align with Keeper’s zero-knowledge and zero-trust security principles
  • Identify and address performance, memory, reliability and scalability challenges across browser environments
  • Guide migration and modernization initiatives as browser extension standards and platform capabilities evolve
  • Partner with Product and UX teams to translate complex product requirements into scalable technical designs
  • Collaborate with Security teams on threat modeling, secure design and remediation of security-sensitive browser functionality
  • Lead architecture reviews, design reviews and technical standards across the Browser Extension engineering team
  • Mentor senior engineers and help raise engineering quality, architecture discipline and technical decision-making across the team
  • Work closely with adjacent Vault, Desktop, Mobile and backend teams where functionality or architecture overlaps
  • Use AI-assisted development tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or similar platforms to improve architecture research, prototyping, debugging, code analysis, documentation and engineering efficiency

Requirements

  • 10+ years of professional software engineering experience with true full-stack development expertise spanning databases, backend services, APIs, infrastructure and modern user interfaces
  • Demonstrated 0-to-1 architecture experience designing and delivering complex software systems from initial concept through production
  • Strong knowledge of software architecture and object-oriented design patterns, including common Gang of Four design patterns
  • Deep understanding of performance engineering, including profiling, load testing, bottleneck analysis and real-time debugging across the full application stack
  • Experience designing highly available, scalable systems and evaluating tradeoffs between centralized and decentralized architectures
  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, microservices, serverless architectures and event-driven application design
  • Experience with cloud-native technologies and platforms, including AWS, Lambda, Docker and Kubernetes
  • Strong understanding of database architecture and data modeling across transactional systems, sharded or horizontally scaled databases and analytical or warehouse platforms
  • Experience designing secure authentication, authorization and identity architectures, including IAM, CIEM and least-privilege access concepts
  • Strong knowledge of web and application security concepts, including CORS, OWASP guidance and secure software development practices
  • Experience with static analysis, code quality or application security tooling such as SonarQube, Checkmarx or similar platforms
  • Strong understanding of modern software development methodologies, CI/CD practices, automated testing and release engineering
  • Demonstrated ability to make sound architectural tradeoffs across performance, security, scalability, reliability, maintainability and delivery speed
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex issues across database, backend, infrastructure, network and UI layers
  • Proven ability to lead architecture discussions, influence technical direction and mentor senior engineers without relying on formal people-management authority
  • Ability and willingness to use AI-assisted tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or similar platforms to support architecture research, prototyping, debugging, code analysis and technical documentation
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep experience with modern browser applications, browser extensions or client-side platform architecture
  • Experience building or integrating enterprise security platforms in areas such as IAM, CIEM, privileged access management or endpoint security
  • Familiarity with enterprise product categories such as GRC, Integrated Risk Management (IRM), SCADA or other specialized security and operational platforms
  • Familiarity with high-scale SaaS, security-sensitive or zero-trust application architectures
  • Experience with compliance and security frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2 and GDPR
  • Familiarity with accessibility standards such as WCAG
  • Experience with product analytics platforms such as Google Analytics 4 or similar technologies
  • Familiarity with modern data and analytics platforms such as Databricks
  • Experience with machine learning, AI-enabled products, computer vision or reinforcement learning workflows
  • Experience integrating native applications, desktop software or endpoint components with browser or web platforms

  • Medical, Dental & Vision (inclusive of domestic partnerships)
  • Employer Paid Life Insurance & Employee/Spouse/Child Supplemental life
  • Voluntary Short/Long Term Disability Insurance

description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refueling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

Electromagnetic and Cyber Group (EM&C) is responsible for developing flexible and survivable advanced electronic warfare and secure communications equipment while providing the industry’s leading signals intelligence, electronic warfare, and cyber experts.  Metrea specializes in signal classification, direction finding, advanced geolocation techniques, and waveform development including waveforms for MANET and LPI/LPD applications. Metrea also develops special purpose radios for government customers and licenses DF and geolocation solutions to multiple OEMs. 

Position Summary

This role is responsible for providing technical operations expertise, mission support, research and development, and solution design in support real world ISR mission efforts.

What You'll Do

  • Serve as a subject matter expert dedicated to identifying, developing, and delivering technical solutions in support of real world ISR mission efforts
  • Serve as a command and control liaison between the customer and mission platforms

In the coming decades, our world needs substantially more critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt, to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. The mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago, because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.

KoBold is a leading scientific mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to make discoveries faster—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. We made our first discovery—Mingomba, one of the world’s largest undeveloped high-grade copper deposits—after spending materially less than the industry average. This asset is expected to operate for decades, and be a leading global copper supplier. KoBold is actively running exploration programs in 8 countries worldwide, all with the potential for another high-quality discovery.

We are developing Mingomba by applying the same technical rigor to resource development and mine planning as we do to exploration. Mingomba is also a scientific laboratory where we prototype new technology and workflows, combined with the expertise of veteran engineers. Our multidisciplinary team consists of mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. We want to develop world-class mining projects that are safer and have more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the role

This is a senior Engineering leadership role for the development of a significant Copper mining complex in Zambia. The Mingomba deposit contains over 10 million tonnes of copper more than half of which exceeds 6% grade. This role will help turn that world class deposit into a world class mine.

The Commercial Director establishes the commercial strategy, contracting approach, procurement and market engagement plan, and contractor management disciplines required to deliver the Mingomba project safely, competitively, and predictably. The role owns the commercial pathway from PFS and engineering delivery through package strategy, tendering, negotiation, award, contract administration, contractor performance, transition to operations and commercial close out. The Mingomba project is expected to require capital expenditure of more than US$2 billion, so the role requires a commercial leader who has built and run major-project commercial functions before.

What this role is accountable for delivering

This role provides the strategic commercial leadership for a significant greenfield project by setting the commercial direction, developing and implementing the strategies that flow from it and building and directing the team that delivers them. The successful candidate will be measured on:

  • A commercial strategy — delivery model, contracting approach, market engagement, and packaging — approved through project governance, delivered on schedule, and updated as conditions change.
  • A capable, high performing contracting, procurement and supply chain team built, developed and directed to deliver the targets with clear accountabilities and growing local capability
  • Major packages tendered and awarded to the baseline schedule with no critical path slippage attributable to procurement or contract formulation
  • Final contract outlays within the agreed band of the approved estimate, with commitments, cost exposure and forecasts visible to the project and finance at all times.
  • Claims and variation exposure quantified, contained and actively managed with no material unresolved disputes at handover to operations
  • Local content targets met with auditable evidence of local supplier participation and capability development
  • A procurement and contracting function that passes independent commercial audits and stage gate review without material qualification
  • A clean integrity record with no sanctions, bribery or conflict of interest findings in the supply chain and contracting workflows.

Responsibilities

  • Commercial governance and routines: Establish the commercial policies, approval thresholds, procurement gates, contract governance, tender review cadence, award recommendations, change controls, claims controls, and vendor management routines needed to support safe, competitive, and predictable project delivery.
  • Project delivery model and contracting options: Develop the project delivery model and contracting strategy (EPC, EPCM, design-and-build, owner-managed, or hybrid), assessing each option against risk, cost, schedule, market capacity, local content, and value for money
  • Commercial leadership and decision support: Lead commercial inputs into the project, executive forums and technical committees ensuring that contracting and procurement status, market intelligence and feedback, contractor risks, cost exposure, and package readiness are visible and early enough for management action.
  • Interface with engineering: Partner with the Senior Engineering & Integration Manager under a defined split of authority (engineering responsible for design authority and technical bid evaluation). The Commercial Director is responsible for commercial evaluation, contract formation and administration, with a single joint change control process spanning technical and commercial impacts.
  • Commercial roadmap and readiness: Develop the commercial plan for engineering, construction, and transition to operations. Lead contractor intelligence and prequalification activities, establish commercial and procurement delivery plans, and identify long-lead commitments and critical award milestones to support efficient project delivery.
  • Procurement, sourcing and contracting: Lead market engagement and package strategy implementation inclusive of tendering, negotiation, award, and contract formation for major packages, including engineering, construction management and delivery services, long-lead equipment, logistics, and site services.
  • Supply chain and logistics: Oversee supply chain execution and logistics strategy, including cross-border movement into Zambia, customs interfaces, freight forwarding, expediting, critical-path equipment delivery, logistics contractor performance, and contingency planning for high-risk routes and packages.
  • Local contractor engagement and local content: Own the local contractor engagement and local content strategy, including supplier mapping, capability assessment, package design, tender access, mentoring, joint-venture pathways, performance expectations, and reporting.
  • Cost control & forecasting: Partner with Finance on budgeting, forecasting, commitments, and cost discipline.
  • Risk & performance management: Provide systematic oversight of contractor performance management and commercial risk (market, forex movement, geopolitical, contractor claims, variations, and disputes), including the implementation of integrated, cross-functional frameworks alongside project management and controls to provide comprehensive oversight and ability proactively flag and mitigate any deviation to plans.
  • Insurance and risk transfer: Shape and place the project insurance program (construction all risks, marine cargo, delay in start up) in accordance with corporate insurance and align contractual risk allocation with insurance coverage.
  • Team & partner management: Lead the contracting, procurement and supply chain team and build ethical, values aligned supplier partnerships.

Qualifications

  • 15+ years of commercial leadership experience on multi-billion dollar mining, oil and gas, infrastructure, or large industrial projects, including direct accountability for commercial strategy, market engagement, procurement, contracting, contractor management, and project outcomes.
  • Demonstrated success forming and implementing high-value EPC, EPCM, design-and-build, engineering services, drilling, construction, logistics, and long-lead equipment contracts on major capital projects, including experience in Africa and direct involvement from package strategy through negotiation, award, administration, claims, variations, and close-out.
  • Deep working knowledge of major construction contract structures (including FIDIC and NEC forms), contracting models, risk allocation, payment mechanisms, incentives, securities, warranties, limits of liability, change management, claims, dispute resolution, and contractor performance remedies.
  • Track record developing local supplier and contractor capability in Africa, Asia, or Latin America, with evidence of measurable outcomes such as increased local participation, improved contractor performance, stronger compliance, safer execution, or reduced delivery risk.
  • Experience working with Chinese suppliers, contractors, and equipment manufacturers will be advantageous, including market engagement, tendering, negotiation, contract formation, technical-commercial alignment, expediting, performance management, and executive-level issue resolution.
  • Proven ability to design and implement commercial systems, governance, and reporting for major projects.
  • Strong business judgement, ethical leadership, and a commitment to transparency.
  • Experience building and leading multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Recognized qualifications in Quantity Surveying, Construction Law, Business, engineering, supply chain, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
  • Ability and willingness to travel internationally to Zambia, with anticipated travel of 90+ days per year.

Trusted Engineering That Matters

Engineering at VGS

Our vision is clear: VGS is building the platform powering agentic commerce and global payments infrastructure. VGS Engineering is the pillar that supports that vision. We create a platform that is an indispensable, ubiquitous component of our partners' payments and security infrastructure. To achieve this, we build and operate high-scale, reliable, and resilient systems that manage mission-critical payment data across the globe. We don't just participate in the payments ecosystem; we power it.

Our Environment & Culture

  • Tooling as Leverage for Impact: We value speed and impact. To ensure nothing slows you down, we arm you with a highly consistent modern stack (e.g. AWS, Kubernetes, Java, TypeScript, Python) and world-class AI-augmented SDLC tooling. We look for builders who combine high agency with deep strategic alignment; channeling their urgency and relentless iteration into what matters most. Leading from the front means multiplying the impact of those around you so we win collectively.

  • Mission-Critical Accountability: We power payments infrastructure for global market leaders, making system trust and integrity our core deliverable. We don't treat compliance (PCI, SOC2, ISO27001), security patching, and platform maintenance as administrative overhead—we engineer them with first-class product discipline. Learn More: See how our engineering practices drive trust and innovation in our official blog and our reliability practices.

About the Role

As a Senior Staff Infrastructure Engineer, you will serve as a technical leader on our Platform Engineering team. You will architect, scale, and fortify global cloud infrastructure designed to handle mission-critical, high-throughput payments applications with zero downtime.

You will take ownership of key platform foundations powering our core payments infrastructure. Rather than executing against a rigid task list or holding blanket ownership over the entire platform, you will drive the technical strategy, architecture, and reliability standards for your designated domains within our multi-region AWS environment. We are looking for high-agency engineers who want to own complex distributed system challenges end-to-end and elevate how the entire engineering team operates.
