All participants must sign the Tenderers’ declaration form attached and submit it with the proposal. Please note that the tenderer may not modify the text, it must be submitted signed as provided by EIT RawMaterials attached to this request for proposal document.

description:
Provided by: GP MENA ELECTION COMMITTEE

Deadline: November 9, 2026

For: Potential Supervisory Board candidates

Targeted Countries: Morocco, Tunisia & Jordan

Greenpeace Middle East and North Africa is seeking senior, values-driven leaders to join its Supervisory Board and help guide the organization through its next phase of impact and growth.

Operating in a region shaped by accelerating climate impacts, environmental pressures, conflict, economic uncertainty and rapid change, Greenpeace MENA needs strong, independent and forward-looking Supervisory Board members to remain resilient, relevant and impactful.

About Greenpeace MENA

Greenpeace MENA is part of the global Greenpeace network, working across the Middle East and North Africa to advance climate and environmental justice and a greener, fairer and more peaceful future.

Our vision is a MENA region where its natural richness and communities are protected and where future generations can thrive with dignity in a peaceful, sustainable and just future.

Who we are looking for

Greenpeace MENA is a dynamic, high-functioning regional organization seeking Supervisory Board members who can complement our current mix of competencies and help us navigate emerging organizational, environmental and regional challenges.

We are seeking candidates who bring a combination of:

  • Board-level or senior leadership experience
  • Strong strategic leadership and sound judgement
  • A strong understanding of the MENA region and its cultural, social, economic, political and environmental context
  • Experience leading or governing organizations through complexity, uncertainty, growth or transformation
  • The ability to provide independent oversight and strategic perspective
  • Commitment to Greenpeace MENA’s mission, independence and values
  • Strong networks and exposure across MENA and/or internationally
  • The capacity and commitment to contribute actively to an engaged and accountable Supervisory Board
  • Residence in, or a strong connection to, the MENA region is highly desirable.

Specific skills and experience

We are particularly interested in candidates who bring one or more of the following:

  • Strategic leadership and Board governance
  • Board-level or senior executive leadership
  • Organizational development, transformation and change leadership
  • Risk, resilience and crisis governance
  • Fundraising, philanthropy and resource mobilization
  • Legal, regulatory or institutional governance
  • Climate, environment, sustainability or climate justice
  • Strategic communications, media, public engagement or movement building
  • Strong regional and international networks and exposure, particularly across civil society, philanthropy, and relevant institutions

Role of the Supervisory Board

The Supervisory Board safeguards Greenpeace MENA’s mission, integrity, independence, accountability and long-term sustainability, providing strategic oversight while maintaining a clear distinction between governance and day-to-day management.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Overseeing Greenpeace MENA’s strategic direction and long-term organizational development
  • Approving organizational strategy and major strategic decisions
  • Approving multi-year and annual budgets and annual financial statements
  • Overseeing organizational risk, resilience and good governance
  • Overseeing key governance and organizational policies
  • Recruiting the Executive Director, setting their remuneration, and overseeing performance and accountability.
  • Safeguarding Greenpeace MENA’s independence, values and organizational integrity

Independence and eligibility

Supervisory Board members must exercise independent judgment and avoid actual or perceived conflicts of interest.

Candidates cannot:

  • Be current employees of Greenpeace or have left Greenpeace employment within the previous year
  • Have a vested interest that conflicts with Greenpeace’s objectives or independence
  • Be directly employed or contracted by governments, ministries or embassies
  • Hold a material financial interest in an industry, company or entity that is a target of Greenpeace campaigns

Commitment and term

This is a voluntary, non-remunerated governance role.

Board members are expected to participate actively in Board and committee work, including approximately four Board meetings per year, committee responsibilities and occasional ad hoc engagement, requiring around 15–20 hours per quarter.

Supervisory Board members are appointed for a three-year term, renewable once for one additional three-year term.

Interested in helping shape Greenpeace MENA’s future?

If Greenpeace MENA’s mission resonates with you and you believe your leadership experience, expertise, perspective and networks can contribute to our next chapter, we would be pleased to hear from you.

Please download and complete the Expression of Interest form, outlining your relevant Board or senior leadership experience and the contribution you could make to the Greenpeace MENA Supervisory Board. Once completed, please upload the Expression of Interest form along with your CV and Cover Letter through this link no later than November 9, 2026.

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to meet with the Greenpeace MENA Election Committee. All applications will be treated with appropriate confidentiality.

  • Build senior relationships with decision-makers in sourcing, supply chain, materials, product compliance, quality and sustainability functions.
  • Position bluesign around the brand's business needs, including supply-chain compliance, safer chemistry, material integrity, regulatory readiness and simplification of supplier requirements.

  • Executive presence and credibility with senior brand decision-makers.

  • Strong cross-functional and cross-regional collaboration skills.
  • Result-driven, solution-oriented and highly independent.

Processor/Underwriter aka Bridge Loan Specialist

At Knock, we put people first, value output over input, and strive to make a meaningful impact in everything we do—and the Bridge Loan Specialist role is no exception. This is a unique opportunity to contribute in a hybrid position combining traditional processing and underwriting responsibilities. As a Bridge Loan Specialist, you will be responsible for reviewing Knock Bridge Loans to verify the loan is complete, accurate, and meets regulatory compliance requirements and internal underwriting guidelines. About Net at Work

Founded in 1996, Net at Work is one of North America’s largest technology advisors and solution providers for small and mid-size businesses. Our award-winning consultancy offers a rich portfolio of next-generation technology, industry expertise, implementation and managed services to help organizations derive value from the transformative benefits of technology.

Through the integration of ERP, HCM and/or CRM solutions, Net at Work offers unique, industry-specific solutions and operation platforms that enable companies to compete more effectively in today’s digital economy. For more information, visit www.netatwork.com.

About this Position

The Consulting Manager - MSP leads the people, client experience, and service delivery operations of Net at Work's Managed Services practice, which provides 24x7 service and support to clients across North America.

Above all, this leader sets the standard for Net at Work's Client Champion value - ensuring the organization understands what matters to clients, anticipates needs, identifies risk early, communicates clearly, and follows through on commitments. Success requires building a high-performing team and operating model that delivers consistently without depending on heroic intervention.

The Consulting Manager oversees day-to-day delivery across Service Desk, NOC, SOC, field services, project execution, and other shared delivery functions. The role leads through team managers and subject matter experts, establishing clear accountability, operating discipline, and visibility while stepping in directly when leadership involvement is needed.

The Consulting Manager partners closely with the Practice Director, who owns commercial practice strategy and P&L. The Consulting Manager is responsible for service execution, managing the operational drivers that influence financial performance and providing timely insight to support decisions. The role also partners across Sales, Client Experience, PMO, Support and other Net at Work practices to create a connected One Net at Work experience for clients.

Job Responsibilities

Service Delivery & Operational Excellence

  • Oversee reliable 24x7 operations across Service Desk, NOC, SOC, field services, project execution, and other Managed Services delivery functions.
  • Ensure performance against established service levels, response and resolution expectations, quality standards, client commitments, and internal operating metrics.
  • Maintain clear operational visibility across ticket volume, backlog, escalation trends, recurring incidents, service quality, utilization, capacity, and other key indicators.
  • Establish effective escalation paths and clear accountability across team leads and delivery teams; step in directly when leadership involvement can change the outcome.
  • Identify patterns behind recurring issues and drive root-cause resolution so the organization continuously improves rather than repeatedly solving the same symptoms.
  • Establish and continuously improve processes, documentation, standards, and operating practices that enable consistent, scalable service delivery.
  • Align staffing and capacity to current and anticipated demand, and champion appropriate use of automation, AI, and integrated technology to improve quality, efficiency, and employee effectiveness.

People Leadership

  • Attract, develop, engage, and retain high-performing Managed Services talent.
  • Set clear performance expectations and create meaningful accountability for client outcomes, service quality, teamwork, and operational discipline.
  • Develop strong team leads and future leaders who can independently run significant portions of the operation.
  • Provide consistent coaching, feedback, and career development; recognize strong performance and reinforce behaviors aligned with Net at Work's values.
  • Address performance gaps early and constructively, taking decisive action when sustained underperformance is not improving.
  • Build succession plans, bench strength, and team capabilities aligned with current and future client needs.
  • Manage utilization, workload, capacity, and resource allocation to support client commitments, employee sustainability, and practice performance.

Commercial & Practice Performance

  • Understand Managed Services economics and actively manage the operational drivers that influence financial performance, including utilization, capacity, resource mix, delivery efficiency, service quality, and agreement performance.
  • Monitor agreement and service performance for trends that create client or financial risk and initiate corrective action early.
  • Partner with the Practice Director on workforce planning, forecasting, resource investments, service offering improvements, and decisions that affect practice performance.
  • Provide timely, accurate visibility into operating metrics, risks, and opportunities; reinforce disciplined time capture, documentation, and other practices needed to manage the business effectively.

One Net at Work Partnership & Growth

  • Partner with the Practice Director to execute Managed Services strategy and priorities, bringing forward operational insight, resource needs, risks, and opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Sales, Client Experience, Support, PMO, and other practices to establish realistic client expectations, create smooth transitions, and solve needs that cross organizational boundaries.
  • Identify unmet client needs and appropriate expansion opportunities, connect them to the right Net at Work resources, and maintain productive relationships with strategic third-party partners.

Client Experience Leadership

  • Maintain client health, including satisfaction, relationship risk, recurring issues, renewal or retention concerns, and commitments requiring leadership attention.
  • Identify and address deteriorating client health early, creating clear recovery plans and ownership before issues become executive escalations whenever possible.
  • Build trusted relationships with key client stakeholders and executives, engaging personally where leadership involvement can strengthen the relationship or improve an outcome.
  • Ensure strategic client conversations connect service performance to the client's business priorities, technology risks, accomplishments, future needs, and measurable value.
  • Lead significant client escalations through resolution, ensuring clear ownership, credible recovery plans, proactive communication, and consistent follow-through.
  • Use CSAT, NPS, client feedback, service data, and relationship intelligence to identify systemic opportunities to improve the client experience and reinforce a culture of Client Champion behavior.

What Success Looks Like

  • Clients view Net at Work as a proactive, trusted partner; satisfaction and retention are strong, and material client risks rarely surprise leadership.
  • Service delivery is predictable and reliable; commitments and service levels are consistently met, escalations are well managed, and recurring issues decline because root causes are addressed.
  • The team is high performing, engaged, and accountable; leaders are being developed, expectations are clear, and workload and capacity are managed sustainably.
  • Client, service, and operational data are used to identify risk early, prioritize action, and drive visible continuous improvement.
  • Utilization, capacity, agreement performance, and delivery efficiency are actively managed in support of the Practice Director's financial objectives.
  • Clients experience One Net at Work through effective collaboration, smooth handoffs, and shared ownership across Managed Services, Sales, Client Experience, PMO, and other practices.

Job Requirements

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in Managed IT Services, or an MSP environment, including meaningful leadership responsibility for service delivery teams.
  • Demonstrated experience leading 24x7 managed services operations, including Service Desk, NOC, SOC, or comparable functions of teams over 50 people in multiple remove locations.
  • Proven record of improving client satisfaction, retention, service performance, and/or operational maturity.
  • Experience building and leading teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, succession planning, resource allocation, and capacity management.
  • Strong business acumen and working knowledge of recurring-services economics, utilization, agreement performance, and delivery efficiency.
  • Strong financial literacy, understanding P&L, and service revenue and team structure optimization for target contribution margins.
  • Executive presence and the ability to lead high-stakes client conversations and escalations with tact, credibility, sound judgment, and clear communication.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use operational data to identify root causes, prioritize improvements, and drive accountability; able to move comfortably between executive-level oversight and hands-on problem solving when needed.
  • Ability to lead across functions and influence without relying on direct authority; strong written and verbal communication skills; willingness to travel periodically as client and business needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience; current industry certifications are a plus.
  • Experience with pre-sales, client technology roadmaps, service catalog development, EOS, and/or automation and AI-enabled service delivery.

Customer Requirements

This job may require access to customer information, systems, and/or premises. As a result, this job may require customer approval for such access as an essential job function.

  • Collaborative Integrator –Team player, unifier, relationship-oriented, win-win seeker, exemplify the concept of relationships through trust and unity.
  • Driven Intrapreneur – Exceed goals using independent creative thinking, optimism, self-confidence, and a can-do attitude.
  • Inspiring Coach – Help employees, clients and partners using knowledge, expertise, experience, and situational fluency.

The Feasibility Manager partners with Business Development, Clinical Operations, Medical, and other cross-functional stakeholders to ensure that recommendations are scientifically credible, operationally realistic, and clearly communicated.

The successful candidate will manage assigned feasibility deliverables, present analyses and recommendations to internal stakeholders and clients, and contribute to strategic initiatives that strengthen Precision for Medicine’s feasibility capabilities and competitive position.

  • Lead or contribute to feasibility assessments for client requests for proposals.
  • Review clinical protocols, study assumptions, client information, and operational plans for United States and global clinical trials.
  • Conduct and synthesise competitive landscape, historical recruitment, standard-of-care, treatment landscape, epidemiology, country, site, and patient-pool analyses.
  • Translate evidence into clear country, site, enrolment, and operational recommendations.
  • Develop logical, transparent rationales for assumptions and identify important data limitations and feasibility risks.
  • Present feasibility methods, findings, recommendations, and supporting rationale to Business Development colleagues, proposal teams, and clients.
  • Collaborate with internal colleagues, external consultants, data partners, investigators, and sites to gather and interpret feasibility information.
  • Plan, coordinate, and analyse targeted site and investigator outreach, as appropriate.
  • Participate in bid-defence meetings and client discussions.
  • Contribute to the continued development of feasibility methods, data sources, tools, templates, and best practices. Share knowledge and support the development of colleagues within the Feasibility team.
  • Work effectively across functions, therapeutic areas, and geographic regions.
  • Contribute to initiatives that strengthen Precision for Medicine’s scientifically driven approach and client offering.

Required qualifications and experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or a related discipline.
  • At least two years of relevant experience in clinical trial feasibility, clinical operations, site intelligence, epidemiology, clinical research, or a related area.
  • Experience conducting or contributing to clinical trial feasibility analysis and site or country identification.
  • Ability to interpret clinical, scientific, epidemiological, and operational information and develop clear recommendations.
  • Professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

  • Experience in oncology, rare disease, or other complex clinical-development programs.
  • Experience presenting analyses and recommendations to clients or senior stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with clinical-trial intelligence, epidemiology, site-performance, or claims and real-world-data platforms.

Skills

For many of us, there’s that one podcast we never miss, and video content is part of our daily routine—whether it’s professional or personal. Riverside’s technology streamlines the entire content creation process, turning real conversations into professional-grade videos, podcasts, webinars, and whatever comes next. The best part? AI-driven tools replace traditional production hurdles, automating recording and editing workflows at the click of a button.

About the Role

We are looking for a Video Education Manager to own product education end-to-end. You'll be the face of Riverside on camera—creating every video yourself from script to final cut, producing product education videos for our YouTube channel, delivering product demos, and developing the new Riverside University into the ultimate learning hub for our users.

This is a high-ownership and highly cross-functional role for someone who is equal parts teacher, creator, and product expert, and who wants their work seen by a global audience. You are also the ultimate proof that the product works: every video you publish is produced in Riverside, by you, end-to-end.

On Your Day-to-Day

You will drive product education strategy and independently produce every video—scripting, shooting, and editing as the primary face of Riverside on camera. You'll scale our YouTube tutorials, build Riverside University into a premier learning hub, and teach new features the moment they ship. Working closely with Product, Marketing, Design, and Social, you'll ensure our content looks exceptional while channeling user feedback directly back into our product lifecycle.

Requirements

  • On-camera experience: You're comfortable and genuinely good presenting to a lens, and it shows. Include links to yourself on camera in your application (a reel, a YouTube channel, tutorials, a talk, anything that shows you presenting and teaching).
  • Video editing: You can take raw footage to a finished, polished piece entirely on your own.
  • A gift for making complex things simple: You can teach a first-time user and a power user in the same breath, without dumbing anything down.
  • Fluency in the creator and content world: You understand how people actually make and publish content, and you speak their language.
  • Excellent English: Native English is a must.
  • Experience with creating content strategy and turning it into growth.
  • Technical setup knowledge: Cameras, mics, lighting, and capture gear. You can recommend a setup with confidence.

Bottom line? If you want to take part in transforming how people and businesses share their stories globally, Riverside is your place. The work is challenging, the culture is fast-paced, and the people are exceptionally brilliant. And if that’s not enough, we guarantee that your work will genuinely make an impact on a global audience.

About Schumacher

Schumacher & Co. is an innovative interior design company that is disrupting the$150 billion-dollar global interior design industry. We are a technological leader on the design frontier, constantly pushing boundaries and striving for excellence. With over 500+ employees and growing, we are driven by a shared belief that design transforms life.We are dedicated to the mission of helping our customers “celebrate the feeling of home”. F. Schumacher & Co designs and produces some of the most beautiful fabrics, wallcoverings, trims, rugs, furniture, and accessories in the world. Our portfolio of products is broad, but they are united by a passion for design, a thirst for what is next, an appreciation for what’s come before, a drive to make our products with enormous care and attention for detail. F. Schumacher & Co is a globally recognized company with a myriad of showrooms both domestically and internationally.

Our competitive advantage in the industry is our people. We believe that our employees are our most important assets. F. Schumacher & Co is deeply anchored in our company core values which are as follows:

  • Preserve Our Entrepreneurial Spirit
  • Take Ownership & Accountability
  • Be Solutions-Oriented
  • Demonstrate Courage
  • Practice Adaptability
  • Embrace Collaboration

We empower our employees to live these values daily because we understand how it will positively impact the customer's journey. F. Schumacher & Co., also known as FSCO, is the parent company to many brands within our portfolio. This role is a 12 month contract and is a part of Data Insights & AI team

Role Overview

We're looking for a hands-on, Senior Quantitative Analyst, Product Portfolio (Statistical Modeling) to own analytics and reporting in support of our Portfolio Development team, with a specific focus on SKU productivity & capital allocation across a portfolio of 20,000+ SKUs and growing. This role will report directly to the Sr. Director of AI & Data Insights, but is expected to work directly with the CEO & Chief of Staff on a day-to-day basis.

This is not a role for someone who takes data at face value. You'll need to distinguish real signal from noise (e.g., a SKU selling poorly because it's out of stock, not because demand is weak), and when you find data that's wrong or inconsistent, you'll have the access and judgment to go into Snowflake and fix it — not just flag it and wait.

What You’ll Do

  • Work hands-on with CEO & Product Strategy stakeholders to understand key strategic questions, and then build analysis and reporting to address them directly
  • Use statistical methods (e.g. conjoint analysis, multivariate regression) to identify which product attributes and characteristics (e.g., color, pattern, material, price point, availability) drive productivity, and translate that into data-driven guidance on where the portfolio should expand, contract or shift
  • Cut through data noise at scale: systematically identify and control for confounders like stock-outs, new/discontinued SKUs, and seasonality so reported trends reflect real pattern performance
  • Identify data inconsistencies at the source (e.g., ERP, web, product master data) and directly and systematically correct records in Snowflake and work with upstream platform owners to improve the accuracy of source data and downstream analytics
  • Present findings clearly and independently to executive audiences, adapting the message for technical or non-technical stakeholders
  • Recommend and maintain recurring analytics & reporting to provide accurate and timely snapshot of SKU productivity
  • Use AI across your own workflow to explore data faster, automate repetitive reporting, catch errors, and multiply output given the scale and growth of the SKU portfolio

What we're looking for

  • 2-5 years in data science, analytics, statistics in similar SKU-driven businesses
  • Solid grounding in statistics or operations research (e.g. regression, hypothesis testing, multivariate analysis, optimization). Able to move beyond descriptive reporting to model relationships between variables and quantify drivers, not just flag correlations
  • Strong SQL and Python, with hands-on Snowflake experience including writing back to correct or clean production data (not just read-only querying)
  • A track record of presenting findings and challenging assumptions directly with senior stakeholders and executives
  • Independent executor — sets analysis priorities against business goals without waiting for direction, and ships accurate, high-impact work in a timely manner
  • Curiosity — asks why the numbers look the way they do and keeps digging until the answer holds up, rather than reporting the first number that looks plausible
  • Thinks in terms of SKU-level economics: sell-through, margin, inventory position, lifecycle stage — and knows how to separate a true productivity problem from a data artifact
  • Treats data quality as part of the job, digging into root causes and correcting them directly rather than working around bad data
  • Hands-on experience applying AI/ML in a business context for task automation - automating repetitive analysis to spend more time on judgment calls
  • Strong English communication skills and a high ownership mindset

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Power BI or similar BI tools alongside Snowflake
  • Exposure to margin, pricing, or demand forecasting data
  • Experience in retail, e-commerce, or luxury/home furnishings goods

What we offer

  • Competitive salary and benefits, based on experience
  • Fully remote work within Europe, with optional time in our NYC office (1–2 weeks per year)
  • Direct visibility with the CEO, with real influence on Product Strategy and Merchandising decisions
  • Collaborative, inclusive, and low-ego working environment

New models of teaching and learning enable a personalized, student-centric experience – and deliver improved retention, engagement, satisfaction, and results for learners of all ages – in schools, campuses, and companies.

D2L is disrupting the way the world learns, by providing the next generation learning environment and solutions to engage and inspire learners. And most importantly, by giving customers a platform that is easy, flexible, and smart. No other company provides a solution as robust and innovative as D2L.

D2L has had a singular mission for 25 years and is dedicated to that same mission in the years ahead: to transform the way the world learns – and by doing so, we will help improve human potential globally.

Every application we receive is personally reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team - yes, a real person looks at your resume! While we use AI tools internally to streamline tasks like meeting notes, summaries, and administrative work, these tools never rank resumes, make hiring decisions, or influence candidate evaluations.

As a Senior Proposal Manager, you will work in a high-impact, fast-paced, deadline-driven environment and be responsible for leading complex proposal response efforts for prospective and existing customers globally. You will manage highly visible and strategic Requests for Proposals (e.g., RFIs, RFPs, RFQs), driving cross-functional collaboration, pursuit readiness, proposal quality, and strategic alignment throughout the proposal lifecycle.

This role requires advanced communication, writing, organizational, strategic thinking, and project management skills, along with the ability to influence stakeholders, navigate ambiguity, and lead complex pursuits under pressure. Successful candidates will demonstrate strong business judgment, proposal management expertise, competitive awareness, and the ability to act as a trusted advisor and mentor within the Proposal Management team. You will play a key role in supporting proposal effectiveness, operational excellence, and continuous improvement across the function.

How Will I Make an Impact?:

Strategic Pursuit Leadership

  • Lead the end-to-end management of complex, high-impact proposal responses (e.g., RFIs, RFPs, RFQs) supporting prospective and existing clients globally.
  • Facilitate and drive complex bid qualification discussions, supporting informed pursuit decisions, proposal readiness, and strategic alignment.
  • Lead proposal planning activities including timelines, stakeholder coordination, risk identification, escalation management, and management of cross-functional contributors.
  • Independently manage multiple complex proposal pursuits simultaneously within fast-paced, deadline-driven environments.
  • Apply strategic thinking, competitive awareness, and proposal management expertise to support compelling, differentiated, and high-quality proposal responses.
  • Support proposal strategy discussions and contribute recommendations related to pursuit approach, messaging, competitiveness, and proposal effectiveness.
  • Provide leadership guidance and influence across project teams to support strong pursuit execution, stakeholder alignment, and proposal quality outcomes.
  • Identify opportunities to improve proposal processes, pursuit effectiveness, and operational approaches based on lessons learned and evolving business needs.

Proposal Development & Strategic Communication

  • Lead the development, writing, editing, and refinement of proposal responses to ensure submissions are compliant, strategically aligned, compelling, and error-free.
  • Review and provide guidance on executive summaries, cover letters, messaging approaches, and other critical proposal components.
  • Work cross-functionally with Subject Matter Experts and senior stakeholders to coordinate and enhance proposal responses while maintaining a strong understanding of D2L’s products, services, value propositions, and competitive positioning.
  • Apply proposal management best practices, strong business judgment, and audience awareness to support high-quality and differentiated proposal responses.
  • Ensure proposal submissions align to established brand, messaging, and style standards while adapting approaches to suit varying audiences, opportunity types, and pursuit complexity.
  • Facilitate proposal reviews and support alignment on proposal messaging, positioning, and response strategy.

Operational Excellence & Team Influence

  • Build strong partnerships with Sales, Solution Engineering, Services, Finance, Legal, Security, Marketing, and other stakeholders involved in proposal pursuits.
  • Act as a trusted advisor and experienced resource within the Proposal Management team, sharing expertise, supporting onboarding activities, and mentoring team members on proposal best practices and complex pursuits.
  • Contribute to operational improvements, proposal management best practices, content enhancements, and scalable proposal management approaches.
  • Support knowledge sharing initiatives and contribute to continuous improvement efforts across proposal operations and team effectiveness.
  • Leverage proposal tools, AI-enabled technologies, operational processes, and proposal management best practices to support proposal quality, operational efficiency, and pursuit effectiveness.
  • Contribute positively to a collaborative, high-performing, and solutions-oriented team environment while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence.

What you’ll bring to the role:

  • 7+ years experience in a similar role in a fast-paced, high volume proposal writing environment.
  • Direct experience in high-tech industry is preferred.
  • A work ethic that thrives in a fast-paced, high volume proposal writing environment.
  • Strong writing, editing, and storytelling skills, with the ability to develop compelling, strategically aligned, audience-focused proposal responses and executive-level communications.
  • Proven ability to develop processes and content to support new business areas and growth.
  • APMP (Association of Proposal Management Professionals) certification or equivalent.
  • Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, Salesforce, Adobe applications, and proposal automation software.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply and promote AI-enabled tools and evolving proposal management best practices to improve proposal quality, team effectiveness, operational efficiency, and pursuit outcomes.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to adhere to strict deadlines
  • Experience writing proposals for education or other key verticals an asset.

Education Recommendations:

Bachelor’s Degree preferably in Business, Technical Writing, English, Communications, or Journalism

description:
*This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK and the following US states: FL, IL, MA, MD, NY, PA, TX, VA. This is a 12 month FTC position.

In the US, this is a union represented position as part of the Pacific Media Workers Guild, Local 39521 of the NewsGuild-Communication Workers of America.

Role Summary

The PLOS Publication Ethics team works to uphold the integrity and reliability of PLOS publications and supports PLOS journals in publication ethics-related issues and policy development. The team also engages with external parties and organizations in publication ethics-related discussions and initiatives.

As a Senior Editor, Publication Ethics, you investigate and resolve publication ethics cases for all PLOS journals, provide publication ethics support to PLOS journal teams, and contribute to team-level initiatives and projects that address ethics and integrity issues at PLOS.

This role is in the Publication Ethics team’s standard case group. This group’s primary case work responsibilities cover a broad array of integrity issues (e.g., image/data integrity, animal/human research ethics, authorship or data ownership disputes, etc.) that typically involve individual articles or research groups. Editors within this group may also be asked to contribute to work involving large-scale cases, as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Resolve publication ethics cases efficiently and in line with PLOS standards and COPE guidance; provide timely support for others’ publication ethics case work; address escalations and queries about publication ethics issues; prevent reputational damage to PLOS journals as feasible.
  • Contribute as requested to tasks, cases, documentation, and other processes needed to support the team’s casework and other objectives.
  • Contribute to team-level and/or cross-functional initiatives and projects that address ethics and integrity issues at PLOS. (e.g., development of workflows or policy updates; development, trials, and/or implementation of approaches to improve detection, prevention, and/or resolution of publication ethics cases)
  • Support journal staff editors in resolving publication ethics issues that arise during manuscript handling, peer review, or post-publication.
  • Communicate rapidly and effectively about ethics cases with involved/affected stakeholders, including the journal’s editorial leads, Editorial Board members, authors, members of other PLOS teams, and any other parties involved in publication ethics case work.
  • Contribute to internal discussions about publication ethics, research integrity, and related issues in team-level and interdepartmental/cross-team forums.
  • Maintain an awareness of cross-industry issues and initiatives and attend COPE Forums that fall within your working hours.
  • Help with recruitment and onboarding for vacant team positions and help to train staff on other PLOS teams in publication ethics case management and standards. Provide training and feedback for other Publication Ethics team members as needed.
  • Uphold high standards of professionalism in all internal and external communications about publication ethics issues.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, both written and oral
  • Highly organized and efficient self-starter with excellent attention to detail and excellent problem-solving and analytical skills
  • A collaborative team player who is comfortable working with a remote team
  • A commitment to open access and research integrity
  • Familiarity with peer review, publishing, editorial decision-making, and publication ethics issues and standards
  • Prior experience investigating and resolving publication ethics cases
  • Knowledge of Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) standards and guidance
  • (Preferred) Expertise in image forensics; experience delivering trainings

Qualifications

  • A Master’s degree or PhD (or equivalent) in a scientific discipline
  • Experience in an editorial or publication ethics role in science, technical, and medical (STM) publishing
  • First-hand experience resolving publication ethics cases in STM publishing
  • A demonstrated aptitude for critically evaluating scientific articles or publication ethics issues
  • (Preferred) Post-graduate research experience in a scientific, clinical, or social sciences discipline

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

  • Prolonged periods stationary at a desk and working on a computer
  • Some national and international travel may be required
  • Some flexibility to work across time zones

The base salary range we’ve established for these positions is (US): $75,000- $83,000 or (UK) £42,000- £47,000. PLOS also offers a comprehensive benefits package summarized below.

BENEFITS:

US:

  • 401k with employer match
  • Employee sponsored health, dental and vision insurance (Dental and Vision 100% employer paid)
  • Paid Vacation, 11 public holidays and sick leave
  • Parental leave
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off
  • Short term and long term disability insurance
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

UK:

  • Private medical insurance
  • Life assurance
  • Income protection 
  • Personal accident insurance
  • Pension with up to 10% employer match
  • 25 days holidays, market competitive Maternity and Paternity leave
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office

About PLOS

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

We’re committed to equal opportunity

We’re working to create a more equitable system of scientific knowledge and understanding. Removing barriers to inclusion and facilitating broad participation of voices is core to our success, inside and out.

Beyond accepting distinct perspectives, we seek and support divergent backgrounds among our staff because we know differences strengthen our teams, our work, and our communities. We strongly encourage applicants of all identities to join us as we work towards a future where science is open to all, for all.

title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
excerpt: ABOUT SINCH Sinch is pioneering the way the world communicates.
description:
ABOUT SINCH

Sinch is pioneering the way the world communicates. More than 200,000 businesses - including Google, Uber, Paypal, Visa, Tinder, and many others - rely on Sinch’s Customer Communications Cloud to power engaging customer experiences through mobile messaging, voice, and email.

Whether you need to verify users or craft omnichannel campaigns, Sinch makes it easy. Our AI-infused Super Network, APIs, and applications ensure you can connect with your customers reliably and securely, at every step of their journey.

At Sinch we “Dream Big”, “Win Together”, “Keep it simple”, and “Make it Happen”. These values are our foundation!

DESCRIPTION

Sinch provides API-based messaging, voice, and email capabilities that customers integrate into applications, workflows, data platforms, contact centers, and AI systems.

We are hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to make those integrations work in the real world. You will embed with customer engineering and operations teams, use modern AI development tools to build production software rapidly, integrate it into existing technology stacks, and lead complex technical deployments to measurable outcomes. You are a production software engineer, customer solution architect, and technical delivery lead, accountable for making the customer solution work in production.

During product ramp-up and early customer engagements, you will work closely with named Voice, Messaging, and Email subject-matter experts. These SMEs provide deep guidance on product capabilities, solution fit, provisioning, country requirements, configuration, best practices, limitations, and complex product-level troubleshooting. Over time, you are expected to become self-sufficient in routine delivery across the supported Sinch CPaaS scope. Ongoing SME involvement focuses on keeping FDEs current with changes in products, technologies, markets, and use cases, and on exceptional deep-domain issues.

Engagements favor supported, generally available Sinch APIs and repeatable implementation patterns. The goal is to accelerate the customer into production and leave its engineering team able to operate and extend the implementation, not to create a permanent dependency on the FDE team.

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

  • Help qualify the engagement. Evaluate technical readiness, feasibility, customer ownership, likely adoption, product gaps, and repeatability. Provide evidence and recommendations to the FDE lead and commercial owner, who make engagement and continued-investment decisions.

  • Lead technical delivery end to end. Run discovery, map workflows and dependencies, define measurable success and sign-off criteria, create the delivery plan, and own execution from prototype through production stabilization and handoff.

  • Design the solution. Translate business workflows into architectures that combine Sinch messaging, voice, or email APIs with customer applications, identity, data, events, AI systems, cloud platforms, and third-party services.

  • Build with AI and remain accountable. Use coding agents and AI-enabled development tools for codebase discovery, implementation, refactoring, tests, troubleshooting, and documentation. Validate generated output for correctness, security, performance, maintainability, and customer fit.

  • Integrate into the customer stack. Write production-grade services, webhook handlers, adapters, data mappings, deployment automation, tests, and operational tooling in the customer's preferred environment.

  • Engineer for production. Design for capacity, scalability, availability, resilience, idempotency, retries, timeouts, rate limits, backpressure, secrets management, least privilege, and safe failure modes.

  • Prove quality. Create unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, load, resilience, and failover tests. Validate business workflows, API and event behavior, recovery, migration, and rollback.

  • Make the system observable. Instrument structured logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerts, and cross-system correlation using Sinch identifiers, callbacks, delivery events, product telemetry, and protocol evidence where relevant.

  • Navigate security and compliance. Partner with customer security, privacy, legal, and communications teams on authentication, data handling, consent, regional requirements, channel regulations, and architecture review.

  • Drive adoption and handoff. Train customer engineers, document architecture and runbooks, establish ownership, and leave the customer able to operate and extend its implementation.

  • Use named SMEs deliberately. Rely heavily on assigned SMEs during ramp-up and early engagements. Bring evidence, absorb their guidance, and document what was learned. Become self-sufficient in routine delivery, using SMEs thereafter to stay current with product, technology, market, and use-case changes and for exceptional deep-domain issues.

  • Turn field evidence into product improvement. Provide Product and Engineering with reproducible findings, customer impact, recommended changes, and reusable implementation patterns that improve APIs, documentation, tooling, and defaults.

THE TECHNICAL SURFACE

Your primary depth should be in production software delivery, enterprise integration, and operations. You are not expected to arrive as a deep expert in Voice, Messaging, and Email. You must bring meaningful exposure to at least one communications domain, learn adjacent products rapidly with named SME support during ramp-up, become self-sufficient in routine delivery, and know when material changes or unusual complexity require specialist input.

  • AI-assisted software delivery: coding agents and AI-enabled development environments used for discovery, implementation, refactoring, testing, debugging, review, and documentation, with human verification and engineering accountability throughout

  • Enterprise integration: REST APIs, webhooks, asynchronous events, identity and access, data mapping, queues, event buses, CRMs, contact centers, data stores, legacy services, and customer-specific operating standards

  • Production engineering: automated testing, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, containers or serverless, scalability, resilience, performance, secrets, logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerts, incident response, and operational handoff

  • Voice: Voice APIs and callbacks, call flows, PSTN, SIP and WebRTC concepts, numbers, routing, recording, streaming, and common signaling, media, or network dependencies

  • Messaging: SMS, MMS, RCS, WhatsApp and Conversation API patterns; senders, templates, provisioning, delivery events, opt-in, country requirements, routing, and channel limitations

  • Email: API and SMTP sending, domains and DNS authentication, templates, webhooks, deliverability, bounces, complaints, suppressions, reputation, and regional processing

  • Customer deployment platforms: AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, containers, serverless, or on-premises environments, including regional placement, data residency, secrets, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code

REQUIREMENTS

  • Typically 7+ years of professional experience across software engineering, enterprise integration, solution delivery, or technical consulting, including substantial direct work with enterprise customers. Equivalent depth matters more than a specific degree or title.

  • A record of personally architecting, building, deploying, operating, and supporting API-driven production systems, not only presenting demos or handing designs to another team.

  • Strong production software skills in at least one relevant stack such as TypeScript/Node.js, Python, Java, or C#/.NET, with sound API, event-driven, authentication, security, testing, code-review, and maintainability practices.

  • Demonstrated ability to use coding agents or other AI development tools to accelerate working software, tests, troubleshooting, and documentation while independently validating the results.

  • Experience integrating new software into existing enterprise technology stacks, including APIs, webhooks, data stores, identity systems, cloud services, events, and operational processes.

  • Strong command of testing, scalability, and observability, including automated test strategy, capacity and failure-mode design, structured logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerting, and cross-system correlation.

  • Experience deploying services on at least one major cloud platform using modern delivery practices such as Git, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, containers or serverless, secrets management, and regional design.

  • Meaningful exposure to at least one communications domain such as programmable voice, messaging, or email. Experience across multiple domains is valuable but is not required.

  • Ability to learn adjacent CPaaS products rapidly with heavy initial support from named SMEs, then apply that guidance independently in normal delivery work.

  • Clear written and verbal communication across engineers, product specialists, security reviewers, business owners, and executives, including the ability to teach and create shared clarity under pressure.

  • Delivery judgment under ambiguity: scope an MVP, make tradeoffs, surface risks early, protect the critical path, and remain calm during planned cutovers and production stabilization.

  • Willingness to travel approximately 10-15% and support planned customer workshops and cutovers. This is not a standing customer-support or on-call assignment.

Preferred

  • Hands-on production experience with a CPaaS provider or comparable communications API platform.

  • Depth in one or more of programmable Voice, SMS, RCS, WhatsApp, Email, Numbers, Verification, SIP trunking, or related communications technologies.

  • Experience with AI-native companies, conversational AI, agentic systems, speech technologies, or real-time AI integrations.

  • Deep Voice and SIP troubleshooting, messaging-channel provisioning, or email-deliverability expertise.

  • Experience connecting communications APIs with CRMs, contact centers, data platforms, decision engines, or AI systems.

  • Experience creating reusable implementation assets, mentoring engineers, or influencing a product roadmap from field evidence.

OUR HIRING PROCESS

We are committed to ensuring a recruitment process that is fair, objective, consistent, and inclusive. Our approach includes structured, competency-based interviews designed to evaluate your skills, experience, and qualifications relevant to the role. At times, we may include a data-driven assessment to enhance our hiring success and identify candidates likely to excel.

We believe in a two-way process and encourage you to ask questions throughout the journey. If this role isn't what you're looking for, please explore the other opportunities listed on our career page: No matter who you are, we hope you find an exciting path forward - hopefully with us!

Benefits

  • STAY HEALTHY: We offer comprehensive market competitive medical, dental, and vision plans. A variety of supplemental plans are also provided to meet your individual needs including access to telehealth for all participants.

  • CARE FOR YOURSELF: Take advantage of our free virtual counselling resources through our global Employee Assistance Program. Your mental health is as important as your physical health.

  • SECURE YOUR FUTURE: Plan for your future with our Roth and Pre-tax 401(k) options including an employer match for all participants.

  • TAKE A BREAK: Enjoy a generous paid time off program. We value balance and understand that performance at work requires time to rest at home and/or rejuvenate on vacation.

  • PUT FAMILY FIRST: We know that families can be built in a variety of ways; therefore, we offer paid parental leave and family planning support.

  • WORK WHEREVER: Our flexible remote work offerings allow you to work wherever you are the most productive and successful. It is what you do, not where you work, that matters.

  • MAKE AN IMPACT: Support betterment in your community and beyond by taking paid time off to support a volunteer program of your choice.

The annual starting salary for this position is between $155,000 - $186,000. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications. This role will be accepting applications until October 5, 2026 at a minimum. Please note that the application timeline may be flexible to accommodate a comprehensive candidate evaluation.

excerpt: The World Councl of Chuches is looking for a Consultant for advocacy and strategic lobbying: 1.
description:
The World Councl of Chuches is looking for a Consultant for advocacy and strategic lobbying:

1. Background
The World Council of Churches’ Ecumenical Accompaniment Programme in Palestine and Israel (WCC–EAPPI) has worked since 2002 to accompany Palestinian and Israeli communities and organisations pursuing a just peace through non-violent means. The programme combines protective presence, systematic monitoring and documentation, and evidence-based advocacy through an international ecumenical network.
The EU-supported GUARD project will operate for 36 months in East Jerusalem and the Jerusalem periphery, with particular attention to communities affected by forced displacement, settlement expansion, restrictions on movement and worship, settler violence, home demolitions, and discriminatory planning and residency policies. The action aims to strengthen protective presence, translate verified field evidence into strategic advocacy, and mobilise international political, faith, civil-society, and media constituencies.
The project’s advocacy component includes structured international delegations, high-level policy briefings, strategic lobbying in selected countries, sustained follow-up with decision-makers, engagement of WCC member churches and EAPPI national coordinations, and coordination with local and international civil-society partners. WCC–EAPPI therefore seeks an experienced Advocacy and Strategic Lobbying Consultant to support the design, preparation, delivery, and assessment of these activities.

2. Purpose of the Assignment
The purpose of the consultancy is to strengthen the quality, reach, coherence, and measurable influence of WCC–EAPPI’s international advocacy under the GUARD project. The consultant will help convert verified field documentation and community-validated priorities into targeted policy engagement, effective lobby missions, and structured follow-up with decision-makers and influential faith and civil-society networks.

3. Objectives
• Develop and maintain a practical advocacy and lobbying strategy aligned with GUARD Outcomes 2 and 3 and the approved project workplan.
• Identify priority decision-makers, institutions, entry points, messages, and feasible policy asks in each target country or institution.
• Prepare and coach Ecumenical Accompaniers, former EAs, church representatives, community voices, and WCC–EAPPI staff for safe, ethical, and effective advocacy engagement.
• Support the organisation of lobby weeks, delegations, policy briefings, and follow-up engagement in ways that connect verified field evidence with concrete policy action.
• Strengthen coordination with WCC networks, EAPPI national coordination and the Advocacy Coordination network.
• Establish an outcome-oriented system for documenting access, commitments, follow-up actions, policy influence, learning, and risk.

4. Scope of Work

4.1 Inception and strategic planning

  • Review the approved GUARD application, logical framework, advocacy workplan, existing fact sheets, incident trends, campaign materials, prior lobby reports, stakeholder maps, and relevant WCC policies.
    • Conduct inception consultations with WCC–EAPPI coordinator, Middle East programme Executive, and advocacy staff, selected national coordination, and key partners.
    • Prepare a concise inception report and an assignment workplan, including methodology, deliverable schedule, consultation plan, risks, safeguarding measures, and information needs.
    • Refine the advocacy theory of change, priority policy objectives, messages, calls to action, target audiences, influence pathways, and indicators of progress.

4.2 Stakeholder mapping and engagement planning
• Map and prioritise relevant executive, legislative, diplomatic, faith, media, and civil-society stakeholders, including decision-makers in EU institutions and selected EU Member States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States.
• Identify credible institutional entry points, political calendars, committee processes, policy windows, and opportunities for coordinated engagement.
• Develop engagement plans that specify the objective, audience, messenger, evidence, policy ask, channel, risk, and follow-up action for each priority stakeholder.
• Ensure outreach is coordinated with WCC offices, national coordinations, and strategic partners to avoid duplication and strengthen complementarity.

4.3 Advocacy products and briefing materials
• Translate verified WCC–EAPPI documentation into concise, audience-specific briefing notes, talking points, meeting briefs, policy asks, and follow-up correspondence.
• Advise on the strategic use of living fact sheets, feature stories, videos, community testimony, and rapid-response communications within policy engagement.
• Apply a rigorous verification and clearance process so that all claims are accurate, appropriately sourced, legally and politically sound, conflict-sensitive, and consistent with WCC–EAPPI positions.
• Ensure EU visibility and acknowledgement requirements are applied where relevant and approved by WCC–EAPPI.

4.4 Training and preparation of advocacy participants
• Design and deliver practical training for selected EAs, former EAs, church representatives, staff, and other approved advocates on policy engagement, message discipline, meeting roles, ethical storytelling, media readiness, and secure handling of sensitive information.
• Facilitate simulation exercises and provide tailored coaching before each lobby mission or high-level engagement.
• Prepare participant packs with objectives, stakeholder profiles, key messages, evidence, meeting protocols, safety guidance, and debriefing tools.

4.5 Lobby missions, delegations, and strategic engagement
• Support the preparation and implementation of agreed lobby weeks and strategic engagements in Belgium/Brussels, Hungary, Italy, the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States, subject to the approved annual workplan, budget, and security assessment.
• Advise on the advocacy design and follow-up of structured international delegations to East Jerusalem, ensuring that field visits, community encounters, briefings, and calls to action are coherent and ethically managed.
• Help secure and prepare meetings with relevant parliamentarians, officials, diplomats, church leaders, journalists, policy advisers, and civil-society actors.
• Where agreed, accompany or remotely support missions, facilitate daily briefings and debriefings, troubleshoot emerging issues, and document commitments and next steps.

4.6 Follow-up, monitoring, learning, and reporting
• Establish and maintain a confidential stakeholder engagement and follow-up tracker that records meetings, policy asks, commitments, responsibilities, deadlines, and outcomes.
• Draft tailored follow-up messages and provide decision-makers with verified updates, feature stories, talking points, and responses to questions.
• Track outcome-level evidence, including access gained, commitments made, parliamentary or diplomatic actions, public statements, policy references, coalition actions, and other plausible contributions to change.
• Facilitate after-action reviews and provide practical recommendations to improve subsequent advocacy cycles.

5. Geographic and Audience Focus
The assignment will prioritise the geographic and institutional audiences approved through the project workplan. These may include:
• European Union institutions and selected Member States, initially Belgium/Brussels, Hungary, Germany and/or Italy;
• the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States;
• international and national parliamentarians, government officials, diplomats, and policy advisers;
• senior church and faith leaders, especially constituencies able to influence public policy and diplomatic engagement;
• international journalists, editors, influencers, and media representatives; and
• civil-society, legal, humanitarian, and advocacy partners participating in coordinated actions.
Priorities may be adapted by WCC–EAPPI in response to the political context, policy opportunities, security conditions, project indicators, and available resources.

Final consultancy report and handover

8. Management, Coordination, and Approval
The consultant will report to the WCC–EAPPI Programme Coordinator and work closely with the Advocacy Officer. Relevant deliverables may require review by WCC communications, legal, programme, or senior management focal points and, where appropriate, consultation with partners or affected communities.
The consultant may not issue public statements, represent WCC positions, contact stakeholders in WCC–EAPPI’s name, publish project information, or commit project resources without prior written authorisation. WCC retains final approval over advocacy objectives, messages, participant selection, itineraries, external communications, and deliverables.

9. Duration, Level of Effort, and Travel
The assignment will require up to 90 working days, deployed in tranches according to an agreed workplan and the timing of advocacy activities. The contract start and end dates will be stated in the consultancy agreement. The assignment is primarily home-based, with travel to agreed locations where required, budgeted, authorised in advance, and considered feasible under prevailing security and access conditions.
Any international travel will follow WCC travel, security, safeguarding, insurance, and expense procedures. WCC–EAPPI may replace, postpone, relocate, or convert an in-person activity to remote delivery where security, access, diplomatic, financial, or operational considerations require it.

10. Required Qualifications and Experience
• Advanced university degree in international relations, public policy, law, human rights, political science, communications, theology, development studies, or a related field; an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be accepted.
• At least seven years of progressively responsible experience in advocacy, government relations, public policy, political engagement, campaigning, or strategic communications.
• Demonstrated record of organising and supporting high-level advocacy or lobby missions involving parliamentarians, government officials, diplomats, faith leaders, or international institutions.
• Strong understanding of EU institutions and at least two of the other target environments identified in this TOR; a credible network in relevant institutions is a significant advantage.
• Substantive knowledge of international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and the political and protection context in Israel and Palestine, particularly East Jerusalem.
• Proven ability to translate complex field evidence and legal analysis into concise, audience-specific policy messages and achievable calls to action.
• Excellent facilitation, training, negotiation, political judgement, writing, and oral communication skills in English; additional relevant languages are an advantage.
• Demonstrated commitment to do-no-harm practice, confidentiality, safeguarding, gender sensitivity, cultural awareness, and responsible use of testimony.
• Ability to work independently across time zones, manage multiple stakeholders, meet short deadlines, and adapt to changing political or security conditions.

11. Proposal Requirements
Interested individual consultants or consulting entities should submit:
• a concise technical proposal demonstrating understanding of the assignment and presenting the proposed methodology, workplan, quality assurance, risk management, and availability;
• an updated CV for the proposed consultant(s), or an organisational profile identifying the lead consultant and any team members;
• two examples or summaries of comparable assignments, with references that may be contacted;
• a financial proposal in the requested currency, showing the professional fee or daily rate, number of days, applicable taxes, and any anticipated reimbursable costs separately; and
• a declaration of availability, independence, confidentiality, and any actual or potential conflict of interest.

Travel and event costs should not be embedded in the professional fee unless expressly requested. Any reimbursable cost will require prior written approval and supporting documentation in accordance with WCC procedures.

I couldn’t find it, so I decided to create it, and in 2015 Poppy & Peonies was born.

All of our bags are made from high-quality vegan leather, and our entire product line is vegan, cruelty-free, and PETA-approved. Protect Democracy seeks a Finance Operations Specialist to join our small, highly collaborative Finance team. Protect Democracy was formed with an urgent and explicit mission: to prevent our democracy from declining into a more authoritarian form of government. We anchor all of our work in service of our mission: it is the foundation of our team, be it litigation, advocacy, or ensuring that our organization has the secure financial operations to continue to meet the urgency of the moment.

This is a hands-on role with meaningful ownership. You will manage cross-functional financial workflows and participate in day-to-day transaction processing, partnering closely with Accounting, Legal/Compliance, People Operations, and teams across Protect Democracy. You should be interested in the full financial story behind a transaction—not simply whether an invoice can be paid, but what commitment it relates to, where it belongs in the budget, whether appropriate approvals and documentation are in place, and how it should ultimately appear in our financial reporting.

You can work remotely from nearly any location in the United States.* We strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds and from across the political and ideological spectrum to apply.A commitment to our mission andcross-ideological strategyfor defending our democracy is essential.

  • Sound judgment and problem-solving ability, including experience identifying discrepancies, resolving moderately complex operational issues independently, and escalating appropriately;

  • Strong organizational, communication, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to manage substantial transaction/workflow volume and competing priorities without losing sight of the larger financial context;

  • A proactive, systems-oriented approach, with demonstrated interest in improving processes, not simply maintaining them as they currently exist;

description:
Protect Democracy seeks several experienced, mission-driven Paralegal & Litigation Specialists. For these particular roles, we are only considering candidates with three or more years of filing experience in civil litigation.

By joining Protect Democracy as a Paralegal & Litigation Specialist, you’ll support multi-faceted litigation and legal advocacy projects focused on preventing authoritarianism, including work aimed at:

  • Pushing back against unlawful executive actions and egregious administrative overreach;

  • Defending advocates, journalists, and institutions from government censorship or unlawful discrimination; and/or

  • Challenging illegal voter purges, voter intimidation by law enforcement, and unauthorized compilation of voter data.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced paralegal who wishes to hone their skills in all stages of impact litigation, case management, writing and research, and communications—over time, developing expertise in one or more area(s) of our legal work.

An ideal candidate for this role brings a flexible, action-oriented mindset; excellent writing, research, and communication skills with a keen eye for detail; and a collaborative, team-oriented approach. We strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds and from across the political and ideological spectrum to apply. A commitment to our mission andcross-ideological strategy for defending our democracy is essential.

The priority deadline to apply for this role is October 15, 2026; we will review applications received after that date on a rolling basis.

You can work remotely from nearly any location in the United States*; travel is required and may, at times, be for extended periods.

As Paralegal & Litigation Specialist, your responsibilities are to:

  • Support litigation by:

    • Managing and organizing case files and documents,

    • Preparing and finalizing legal memos and pleadings,

    • Coordinating court filings, and

    • Help lead the discovery process;

  • Conduct research, synthesize findings, and draft related memoranda, reports, and other communications;

  • Cite-check and Bluebook, fact-check, proofread, and assist with drafting court filings, letters, and other public-facing documents;

  • Engage professionally with clients, opposing counsel, partner organizations, and other external stakeholders;

  • Draft external-facing communications materials, including press releases, social media, talking points, outreach emails, op-eds, and blog posts;

  • Coordinate logistics for calls, including creating agendas, and drafting internal-facing communications (i.e. emails, presentations);

  • Project manage components of litigation projects, including developing work plans, tracking and communicating progress toward goals, and offering and soliciting feedback along the way;

  • Maintain and, at times, create information management systems, processes, and tools within and amongst impact teams;

  • Strategize with other team members—actively contribute ideas during impact and litigation project brainstorming sessions and propose projects to advance Protect Democracy’s mission;

  • Contribute to culture-building initiatives across the organization.

Requirements

The ideal candidate brings:

  • A minimum of three years of filing experience in civil litigation, including familiarity with:

    • Supporting litigation through preparing, finalizing, and filing pleadings in court, cite checking and Bluebooking documents, drafting discovery materials and correspondence; and preparing administrative documents like pro hac vice applications;

    • Navigating federal rules of civil procedure and state/local court rules;

    • Case management/litigation administration (including managing large quantities of documents and case file and folder organization);

  • Strong writing, researching, editing, and proofreading skills;

  • Experience project managing, ideally in a legal context;

  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills;

  • Comfort giving feedback and managing “up, down, and sideways”;

  • Nimbleness and an ability to perform well in a rapid-paced environment;

  • Eagerness to learn new research, communications, legal and policy skills and processes;

  • Ability to foster collaborative relationships and work in a team environment with people with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives;

  • Rigorous attention to detail and the highest standards for excellence in execution;

  • Ability to track, prioritize, and balance a diverse set of responsibilities;

  • A passionate commitment to the preservation of democratic norms and institutions, and an understanding that our democracy has never fully represented communities of color.

Preferred, but not required:

  • Paralegal certification;

  • Experience with Filevine;

  • Experience with e-Discovery systems (i.e. Everlaw, Relativity).

Compensation

This position is FLSA Non-Exempt and eligible for overtime pay. The starting salary range for this role is $84,300 - $99,200 commensurate with the candidate’s relevant experience, capabilities, and skills, and in alignment with internal equity.

About Protect Democracy

  • *Flexible location. We are a remote-first organization based exclusively in the United States, meaning our staff work within the US and primarily virtually. We also offer shared workspaces for those who enjoy working in an office environment. We are established for remote work in many states across the country, and while candidates based anywhere in the United States are welcome to apply, we may not be able to offer employment in your current location. If you proceed in the hiring process, we will discuss where you currently live and what is possible in our initial interview. All staff are also required to travel at least two times per year to team retreats, and this role also requires periodic travel. (Accommodations to this requirement will be made only in exceptional circumstances.)

  • Commitment to an inclusive workplace. Protect Democracy is an equal opportunity employer. We believe that a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences strengthens our ability to analyze problems, craft solutions, and drive meaningful change. Protect Democracy encourages applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, or veteran status.

  • Phenomenal benefits. Our benefits package includes generous sick leave and a flexible vacation policy where we encourage team members to take 4-5 weeks every year, along with 12 paid holidays, 6 weeks of paid family medical leave, and 18 weeks of paid parental leave. We also offer a 401(k) plan with up to 6% employer match that vests immediately. Additionally, we cover employee medical premiums at 100% (with up to 95% coverage for dependents depending on plan selection), and employee and dependent’s dental/vision at 100%. All employees have access to long-term disability and life insurance, fertility benefits, a home office stipend, and bonuses at the discretion of the Executive Director.

  • Ample opportunities for personal & professional development. Candidates who do not meet all listed criteria should still apply, as our organizational structure focuses on providing mentorship and opportunities for professional growth.

To apply for this position, please complete the application linked below. As part of your application, you will be asked to upload PDFs of your resume and cover letter. (Applications missing any of the required materials will be considered incomplete and not reviewed.) The priority deadline to apply for this role is October 15, 2026; we will review applications received after that date on a rolling basis.

Important notes

  • Contact if you require specific accommodations at any point in the hiring process.

  • Keep an eye on your promotions/spam folders to avoid missed communication.

Every candidate flagged by our system is reviewed by a member of our recruiting team; we never rely on automated scoring alone to make hiring decisions. If you have questions about this process, or need an alternative application path as an accommodation, reach out to us at .

  • We are unable to provide status updates for each application we receive. If you reach out and do not hear back, please know it is not for lack of appreciation or interest, but simply for lack of staff capacity to respond to individual inquiries.

  • The application will include a voluntary EEO survey so that we can monitor the applicant pool as a whole for representation and equal employment opportunities, and to evaluate our progress as an organization toward a diverse and inclusive workforce, which we believe is a pillar of a thriving democracy. The categories used by the EEO survey are limited and may not reflect your lived experience; please feel free to opt out of any of the questions. Your responses to this survey are entirely separate from your application materials, are not accessible to those responsible for hiring decisions, and will not affect your candidacy in any way.

title: Field CTO

description:
Are you looking for a role that motivates and challenges you? Are you ready for an opportunity for growth? Do you want to work on teams where people roll up their sleeves to take on tough problems together, and regularly blow the doors off our clients with their outstanding teamwork? If you answered yes to those questions, 3Cloud might just be for you!

At 3Cloud, we hire people who aren’t afraid to experiment or fail. We hire people who are willing to give direct and candid feedback to their managers, leaders, and team members.
