The Field CTO will serve as the executive technology voice, technology champion, and trusted executive advisor for our Enterprise Advisory & Solution Architecture practice. This is a senior, client-facing role where you build peer-level relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and transformation leaders, shape market narrative through industry presence and analyst engagement, and translate technology direction into business outcomes that executives can fund and govern.

You operate across multiple strategic accounts, set technology vision that influences how we advise, sell, and deliver, and use your credibility to create demand, expand strategic relationships, unlock and shape large transformation opportunities, and contribute to growth. You work closely with pursuit, delivery, engineering, practice, and partner teams, but your primary lane is advisory, market presence, and offering strategy, not day-to-day deal mechanics.

This is a matrix leadership role. You lead outcomes across pursuit, delivery, and partner teams through influence, executive alignment, and decision ownership, without relying on direct line management authority. You co-own portfolio-level results with practice leadership.

Responsibilities

Executive Advisory and Peer Relationships

  • Set credible technology vision and multi-year transformation strategy that executives can fund, sequence, and govern.
  • Frame decisions in business terms by explaining options, tradeoffs, enterprise risk, and expected value.
  • Champion technical debt elimination and modernization with client technology leaders to unlock value and create demand for transformation.
  • Connect technology investment to enterprise value by helping executives define measurable outcomes, adoption requirements, operating model implications, and governance needed to realize the expected business benefit.

Market Presence and Thought Leadership

  • Act as a named external technology voice across client forums, executive briefings, industry conferences, partner events, and analyst sessions.
  • Publish points of view, briefings, and narratives that establish the practice as a market leader.
  • Engage with industry analysts, sourcing advisors, consulting firms, and ecosystem partners to shape opportunities and influence market perception.
  • Build market awareness and excitement around our capabilities in ways that unlock large transformation opportunities, expand the scope of existing opportunities, and create new ones.

Partner Ecosystem Leadership

  • Cultivate senior relationships with Microsoft field teams, ISVs, platform partners, and the broader technology ecosystem to identify and shape joint opportunities.
  • Drive partner-influenced pipeline and co-sell success through joint solutioning, executive relationships, and coordinated pursuit execution.
  • Stay current on partner roadmaps and platform direction and translate that into client options and offering decisions.
  • Connect 3Cloud and Microsoft capabilities with the broader technology ecosystem, industry expertise, and partner landscape to shape differentiated client solutions and opportunities.
  • Position Microsoft technologies credibly within heterogeneous enterprise environments, understanding how they integrate and coexist with other cloud, data, AI, SaaS, and enterprise platforms.

Leadership

  • Set consistent technical direction and quality standards, build capability through coaching and communities of practice, and represent the practice in executive and cross-practice planning.
  • Model the 3Cloud Way to Lead through personal, organizational, and business leadership, building trust across organizational boundaries, developing people, and operating with a strategic and enterprise mindset.
  • Serve as a senior technology leadership interface across advisory, pursuit, engineering, and delivery, ensuring executive technology strategy remains grounded in what can be successfully engineered, operated, and scaled.

Solution and Offering Strategy

  • Shape the portfolio across Applications, Cloud Platforms, and Data & AI so it is technically sound, deliverable at scale, and aligned with market demand.
  • Sponsor reference architectures, solution playbooks, accelerators, and guardrails that improve win rate and delivery consistency across the firm.
  • Set technical direction on principled tradeoffs across speed versus quality, custom build versus platform, and innovation versus stability at a portfolio level.
  • Connect lessons from strategic client engagements, Microsoft, and the broader technology ecosystem back into offering strategy and capability development.

Pursuit Influence and Technical Win

  • Champion priority pursuits through executive credibility, solution strategy, and competitive positioning grounded in delivery reality.
  • Engage early on the highest-stakes opportunities to surface outcomes, constraints, and enterprise risks and to shape the opportunity before it is fully formed.
  • Champion technology choices and tradeoffs with clients as they evaluate recommended solutions and lead solution defense alongside pursuit and delivery teams.
  • Create executive-level demand and help expand individual technology initiatives into broader transformation opportunities where client outcomes support it.
  • Step in when stakes are high, decisions are contested, or executive alignment is at risk and restore clarity on the path forward.

Innovation and Horizon Scanning

  • Track emerging technology and industry shifts through Microsoft, partner roadmaps, and direct ecosystem dialogue, and evaluate them based on enterprise applicability and business value rather than technology novelty alone.
  • Translate innovation into clear client recommendations, pilot approaches, and phased adoption paths that balance value, risk, and operational readiness.
  • Maintain executive-level fluency in emerging AI capabilities, including generative AI, agentic systems, AI-enabled engineering, governance, security, and responsible enterprise adoption.
  • Educate sales, pursuit, and delivery teams on key components, trends, and capabilities so they can recognize and act on opportunities.

Requirements

  • Proven experience as a Field CTO, Principal CTO, Chief Architect, Distinguished Architect, or equivalent external-facing technology leader for an enterprise modernization, cloud, AI, or technology transformation practice.
  • Executive-level technology leadership experience advising and/or directly leading complex enterprise technology organizations, including significant C-suite interaction and a track record of building peer-level relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CDOs, and transformation leaders at Fortune 500 or comparable enterprises.
  • Demonstrated industry voice through keynotes, published points of view, briefings, podcasts, analyst engagement, or other recognized external forums.
  • Deep expertise in Microsoft Azure architecture, including enterprise-scale adoption, governance, security, integration, and modernization.
  • Experience setting technology direction across Applications, Cloud Platforms, and Data & AI, including operating model and governance implications.
  • Executive-level understanding of enterprise AI strategy and the implications of generative AI, agentic systems, data foundations, governance, security, and responsible adoption.
  • Ability to credibly advise executives on integrating Microsoft technologies with non-Microsoft cloud, data, AI, SaaS, and enterprise platforms.
  • Strong executive communication skills with the ability to translate technology decisions into business impact, investment choices, constraints, and risk.
  • Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect technology strategy to investment, commercial outcomes, delivery economics, and measurable enterprise value.
  • Experience influencing large pursuits through credibility and solution strategy rather than pursuit mechanics.
  • Demonstrated ability to shape offerings, accelerators, platforms, or reusable intellectual property that improved pipeline, win rate, market differentiation, or delivery consistency.
  • Established senior relationships with hyperscaler and platform partners and the ability to drive joint solutioning and co-sell.
  • Experience leading through matrix influence across account, engineering, security, delivery, practice, and partner stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated experience developing, coaching, and mentoring senior architects or technology leaders.
  • Willingness to travel up to 25 percent as needed.
  • Maintain, or be willing to obtain and maintain, relevant professional certifications.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with hybrid environments and other cloud platforms, such as AWS and Google Cloud.
  • Prior CTO, CIO, Chief Architect, Distinguished Architect, VP of Engineering, or equivalent experience at an enterprise, software vendor, consulting organization, or hyperscaler.
  • Experience presenting in executive forums, steering committees, board-level settings, analyst briefings, or named industry events.

  • Experience working across global or multicultural organizations and complex matrixed structures.

About the Opportunity

This role is part of a broader technology leadership model across 3Cloud. The Field CTO brings deep Microsoft ecosystem expertise, industry perspective, executive advisory, and enterprise technology strategy, and collaborates with technology leaders across AI, industry, engineering, and the partner ecosystem.

Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We are a leading eco-friendly household essentials business and we donate 50% of our profits to help everyone gain access to clean water and a toilet. As of June 2024, we’ve contributed over $20 million AUD to this mission. Basically, we’re really good at making it easy to do good.

We operate scaling businesses the UK, US, Australia and Canada. Our amazing team is based in Australia, the UK, the Philippines, China, and the US. Our 250+ people aim to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next 5-10 years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

As our AR & AP Lead, you’ll be the eyes and ears of our Number Scrunchers accounting function — driving accounts receivable and accounts payable operations day to day, in close partnership with your two direct reports (our AR Expert and AP Coordinator) and the wider Financial Operations team. You’ll keep our books accurate, our customers paying on time, and our suppliers paid on time, all so we can maximise the donations we’re able to make.

If you worked here this past month here are some things you might have been involved in

  • Pulled together the monthly AR ageing report for the CFO and exec team, with a clear plan to chase down aged amounts
  • Reviewed the weekly payments file (including the Tipalti funding summary) before it went out for approval
  • Flagged an “at risk” customer account early and looped in the customer-facing team for support
  • Helped close the books accurately and on time at month-end, escalating one risk early to the Head of Financial Operations
  • Worked with the AP Coordinator to tidy up a clunky step in the AP process

Let’s talk about you

Detail is your love language

You get real satisfaction from a reconciliation that ties out perfectly and a report that lands on the CFO’s desk without a single follow-up question. You’re equally comfortable rolling your sleeves up in the detail of a customer account and stepping back to build the KPIs and reporting that keep the whole team honest.

Calm under a closing calendar

Month-end doesn’t rattle you. You know how to keep AR and AP on track to a deadline, spot a risk early enough to actually do something about it, and communicate clearly with stakeholders when something needs to change.

A coach as much as a doer

You lead a small, tight-knit team and genuinely enjoy it — you give clear, kind feedback, help your people grow, and aren’t afraid of a difficult conversation when a process or a stakeholder relationship needs a repair job.

You give a crap. Do you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off, as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the high standards of social and environmental impact. We’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world, generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys (thanks Culture Amp!) tell us that our team is really proud (over 90%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

Role Overview

This role is responsible for providing technical support and feedback to the Apprentices. The Data Mentor will ensure that teaching, learning and assessment is of a gold standard and that retention, achievement and grading outcomes are at or above national standards and learner progression is robustly monitored.

Key responsibilities:

Essential

  • Relevant Technical Qualifications
  • Relevant industry experience

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Pension with 4% matched contributions, opportunity to opt into salary sacrifice scheme

Background to our Organisation

We are an education technology company that enables corporate and government organisations to achieve their business goals by educating their workforce with critical digital transformation skills to succeed in the AI era.

We deliver unique and innovative professional education that is accelerating the digital transformation of our clients, advancing the careers of their employees, helping people get into work and closing the digital skills gap. We are in a sector that is crucial to the economy and workforce, with a lot of opportunity for change and innovation. We are at the cutting edge of teaching applied data and digital skills, with our unique patented learning platform EDUKATE.AI offering our clients and learners a unique learning experience. EDUKATE.AI was developed with support from Innovate UK and provides all of our learners with 24/7 immediate feedback on their work, helping accelerate the learning process and providing a sandbox environment to experiment on real world datasets.

Since 2016, we have supported more than 15,000 learners across four continents with nearly 550,000 pieces of code submitted for feedback on EDUKATE.AI. We are trusted by some of the most recognisable brands in the world to educate their workforce, including Microsoft, the NHS, GSK, easyJet, the BBC and John Lewis. Our focus on applied learning to create business impact sets us apart - individual learners have reported applying their skills at work to generate recorded value of up to £40m.

Our Values

At the centre of the way we work together and inspire each other to achieve success are these core values:

Entrepreneurial

We take initiative and show entrepreneurial spirit which fuels innovation at Cambridge Spark. This includes identifying opportunities for improvement, taking ownership for implementing solutions effectively and driving improvement by using proof of concepts to demonstrate the feasibility and value of their work.

Team Spirit

Everyone is part of building an open and transparent culture, communicating effectively to raise issues, discuss improvements and share the evidence used to make decisions.

Customer-focused

Our customers are at the centre of everything we do, inspiring us to create great work. We strive to build friendly, professional and lasting relationships with them to better understand and anticipate their needs.

Gold Standard

We are experts in our field and are constantly developing our technology and offering. We set the benchmark in our industry: both in what we offer customers and in how we deliver it.

Cambridge Spark is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunities for all employees and to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. ASSEMBLY INDUSTRIES

Job Title - Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)

Also known as: Client Services Engineer · Solutions Engineer · Implementation Engineer

About Assembly

Assembly Industries is The Workforce Modernization Company. For fifty years, software — the single greatest lever for business efficiency and productivity — has been gated behind two doors: buy it from a vendor, or hire an engineering team to build it. Coding agents have fundamentally changed that. Our mission is to make every employee a builder: we convert often non-technical subject-matter experts into prolific builders of software through training, a platform to execute on, and a partner standing beside them every day after launch.

Assembly Platform is our end-to-end application lifecycle platform — from problem discovery and requirements through architecture, production deployment with IT, adoption, and ongoing maintenance. The prototype is just the tip of the iceberg; Assembly Platform and our team handle everything below the waterline. Our vision is to help existing businesses build their own software operating system from the inside out.

Role Overview

We are onboarding our first 50 Assembly Platform customers, and every one of them will build their first production-grade application with us. You are the partner standing beside them. You will be the hands-on engineer and client-facing lead who takes each customer from onboarding to a live, production application — running calls, building alongside them, debugging their vibe-coded projects, and owning the path to launch.

This is a rare hybrid role: half forward-deployed engineer, half client services. You will be one of the earliest hires shaping how Assembly delivers on its promise to the Founding customer cohort.

What You'll Do

Client Services & Delivery

  • Own the customer relationship day-to-day: lead onboarding calls and training sessions with professionalism and high-proficiency English.
  • Run the follow-through: send meeting follow-ups, share project plans, and deliver regular status updates so customers always know where their build stands.
  • Keep momentum: follow up with customers after onboarding sessions and schedule their next onboarding and training sessions.

Building & Support

  • Build production-grade applications: assist each of our first 50 customers in taking their first application from prototype to production on Foundry.
  • Support customers in Slack: respond quickly, dig into their code and vibe-coded projects, and figure out what's going on.
  • QA and ship: test applications, build features on customers' behalf, and squash bugs standing between them and launch.
  • Run the board: maintain a project board per customer and always know the open items remaining to get the first application to production.

What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

  • Vibe coding portfolio: you must be able to point to at least five fully vibe-coded, productionized applications you've built. We will ask to see them.
  • AI-pilled: genuinely excited about AI and vibe coding — you stay on top of the latest open-source projects, stacks, frameworks, and packages because you want to, not because you have to.
  • Engineering foundation: solid grounding in system design and software architecture — you can reason about how an application should be structured, not just prompt one into existence.
  • Client-facing experience: you've worked directly with customers before and communicate professionally, in speech and in writing, in high-proficiency English.
  • Support instincts: experience handling customer issues — triaging, debugging unfamiliar codebases, QA-ing, and closing the loop.
  • Experience: 3+ years of relevant professional experience.
  • Availability: comfortable working US hours (PST).

Nice-to-Haves

  • Previous consulting or professional-services experience.

To apply, share your resume and links to five vibe-coded, productionized applications you've built.

This is a remote based position for candidates based out of Argentina.

description:
Overview

UPSTACK is the leading full-service technology brokerage that empowers businesses to make smarter technology investments. Through a vendor-neutral approach, UPSTACK delivers expert advisory and execution services across the entire technology landscape—including data center colocation, cloud, connectivity, networking, cybersecurity, AI, and more—at no additional cost to our clients.

Under the leadership of Founder and CEO Christopher Trapp, UPSTACK is committed to exceptional customer experiences, serving 6,500+ clients—from SMBs to enterprises—and managing over $1B+ in annual technology spend across industries.

About the Role

The IT Manager owns UPSTACK’s internal IT operations, serving as the primary point of accountability for endpoint management, internal technology projects, and UPSTACK’s outside vendor and MSP relationships — including the managed IT support provider, AV/conferencing, telecom, hardware, and software vendors. This role ensures service quality, SLA adherence, and cost-effectiveness across those partnerships, while planning and leading internal IT projects such as platform transitions, network upgrades, and hardware refresh cycles from scope through execution.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience managing Jamf and Microsoft Intune across a mixed device fleet, is comfortable directing outside vendors and an MSP helpdesk to consistent service standards, and holds an active CISM (Certified Information Security Manager) certification. This person can translate security and compliance requirements — including UPSTACK’s migration to Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access — into practical endpoint and identity management practices.

Location Preference:

Remote

Key Responsibilities

Vendor & MSP Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary owner of UPSTACK's outside vendor support services relationship: manage day-to-day engagement, ticket escalations, service quality, and SLA adherence
  • Manage other outside support vendors (AV/conferencing, telecom, hardware suppliers, software resellers), including scopes of work, deliverables, and accountability
  • Review Help Desk and vendor performance, invoices, and contract renewals; recommend changes or replacements where service or cost falls short
  • Act as the escalation point between UPSTACK employees and the MSP helpdesk, ensuring issues are routed, tracked, and resolved to standard

Internal IT Project Leadership

  • Plan and lead internal IT projects end to end, including platform transitions (e.g., Okta and Microsoft Entra ID), network upgrades, hardware refresh cycles, and new tool rollouts
  • Define project scope, timelines, and budgets; coordinate execution across the MSP, outside vendors, and internal stakeholders
  • Communicate project status, risks, and outcomes to business stakeholders

Helpdesk & Support Oversight

  • Own endpoint management across the fleet: Microsoft Intune for Windows devices and Jamf for Mac devices, including configuration profiles, compliance policies, app deployment, and patching
  • Administer and oversee internal RMM tooling for monitoring, alerting, patch automation, and remote support
  • Oversee the device lifecycle: procurement, provisioning, new-hire staging, refresh, retirement, and recycling logistics
  • Handle escalated, sensitive, or high-visibility issues directly, delivering white-glove support for senior leadership and board members, including board meeting AV

Technology Stack & Security

  • Administer and support UPSTACK's core stack: Microsoft 365, Intune, Jamf, Cisco Meraki, Okta, and Microsoft Entra ID

EDUCATION

Required Licenses | Certifications | Degree:

  • CISM (Certified Information Security Manager) certification required; no specific degree required — equivalent IT management or technical leadership experience considered

Preferred Licenses | Certifications | Degree:

  • Microsoft MD-102 (Endpoint Administrator Associate)
  • Microsoft AZ-104 (Azure Administrator Associate)
  • CompTIA Security+

KNOWLEDGE

  • Jamf, Microsoft Intune, and Microsoft Entra ID (all required): hands-on knowledge of Mac device management with Jamf, Windows device management with Intune, and identity and conditional access management with Microsoft Entra ID as UPSTACK migrates to a Zero Trust security model
  • RMM experience (required): prior hands-on work with RMM platforms (e.g., NinjaOne, Datto RMM, ConnectWise Automate, or similar) for monitoring, patching, and remote support
  • Knowledge of MSP operating models, SLAs, and vendor/contract management
  • Knowledge of Microsoft 365 administration and identity platforms, including Okta and Microsoft Entra ID, particularly through platform transitions
  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals and equipment such as Cisco Meraki
  • Understanding of IT asset lifecycle management, security best practices, and endpoint compliance standards

SKILLS

  • Strong vendor and MSP relationship management skills, including performance reviews, escalations, and contract negotiation
  • Project management skills: scoping, scheduling, budgeting, stakeholder communication, and cross- team coordination
  • Strong technical troubleshooting and escalation judgment across hardware, endpoints, networking, and conferencing
  • Excellent verbal and written communication, with the discretion and professionalism to support senior leadership and board members
  • Organizational skills to manage concurrent projects, vendors, and device inventory

ABILITIES

  • Ability to lead and manage multiple concurrent IT projects, vendor relationships, and support escalations effectively
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment in high-visibility, sensitive situations involving senior leadership and board members
  • Ability to translate business and security requirements, such as the Zero Trust/Entra ID Conditional Access migration, into actionable technical project plans
  • Ability to hold outside vendors and MSP partners accountable to SLAs and service quality standards
  • Ability to operate independently while keeping stakeholders informed of project status, risks, and outcomes

Salary Range

Employees new to UPSTACK typically come in at the start of the pay range. UPSTACK focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure, which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience, and job-related skills.

The salary range for this role is fixed at $90,000 to $120,000 annually, with no room for negotiation. Please apply with this understanding.

Clovr Labs is recruiting a Software Engineer to work on new and interesting projects.
Let's give you some context on who we're looking for and what to expect when you join the team.
👋 About us

Clovr Labs is a boutique consulting firm working at the intersection of cybersecurity, Bitcoin, and lean product development. We care deeply about building simple, elegant solutions to complex problems and believe in iterating quickly to uncover the best ideas.

We’re developing a range of products across several cutting-edge technology domains, including Bitcoin and the Lightning Network, powering instant, low-cost payments at scale. One of our flagship products is, an enterprise-grade payment service provider built on the Lightning Network.

🧩 Your role

We’re looking for engineers who are curious, driven, and excited about creating high-quality software.

As a Payments Software Engineer at Clovr Labs, you will:

  • Help evolve and expand our existing products and internal systems.

  • Work closely with a motivated and collaborative team to build new automation and infrastructure solutions.

  • Design and deliver product features that bring real value to our clients.

  • Dive into the details, polish the experiences you build, and take pride in high craftsmanship.

🎬 What do we expect from you?

  • Business mindset: you understand the business goals behind your work and choose technology that serves those goals and delivers value for customers and the company. You seek user feedback and iterate quickly based on real-world insights.

  • Strong sense of ownership: you understand the problem, find or build the right solution, and take responsibility for delivering it to production and ensuring it works reliably.

  • Strong security mindset: you proactively assess risks, anticipate threats and failure scenarios, and design and code defensively to protect our customers.

  • Experience with production systems: you are comfortable operating live services and use logs, metrics, and traces to understand system behavior, detect issues early, and resolve them effectively.

  • Correctness and financial integrity: you design for idempotency, data consistency, and precise monetary calculations, handle retries, concurrency, and partial failures safely, ensuring every transaction is traceable and can be reconciled.

  • Adaptability: you stay committed and flexible as priorities change, adjusting your approach as new information emerges.

  • Teamwork makes the dream work: you are a strong team player and believe that a team together can ship great things. you work closely with others, challenge ideas respectfully, welcome being challenged, and take shared responsibility for the team’s success.

  • AI-powered engineering: you use AI as a core part of your workflow to understand problems, explore solutions, and accelerate delivery, applying engineering judgment to validate its output and taking ownership of the results.

  • English proficiency is helpful; understanding Spanish is a nice plus.

🛠 Key roles

  • You will join a small team currently scaling up. We are passionate about it and we are not trying to hide it.

  • We expect you to bring your experience in implementing best practices to our team such as pair programming, continuous deployment, tech debt management.

  • A key part of our duties is to dedicate time to non-business requirements of the systems we are working on, such as cost, maintainability, scalability, and security.

  • Self learning is an expectation. You will be provided with enough time and resources to learn new stuff and to become a better developer.

  • You should have a cost-benefit analysis mindset and use logical reasoning to address the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions.

🎏 It's nice to have

  • Have a technical interest in Blockchain concepts, specially Bitcoin and the Lightning Network. Also in payments processors and understanding how these systems operate in practice.

  • Special interest and high understanding of modern cloud-native software solutions, with special focus on observability, security and performance.

  • Experience building software applications with a combination of Go and C# or can easily adapt to using these languages.

  • Interest in Open Source Software (OSS), we highly value contributions to Open Source Software. Many of our main components are OSS, and we take pride in contributing back to other OSS projects.

🔍 What we offer

  • Fully and asynchronous remote work within Spain, independence, ownership and flexibility is what you can expect from our mindset.

  • Fair wages for people with attitude above all (60k - 80k negotiable).

  • Evolve in a stimulating and challenging environment.

  • Share and learn with a passionate and diverse team.

  • Work from home budget, choose what you need to create your dream home office, including internet and electricity.

  • Annual learning budget, learn a new programming language or go to a tech conference, if it is important for your career, it is important for us.

  • Fully paid team building activities three or four times a year, somewhere around the world.

Clovr Labs is incorporated in Spain and the team meets regularly in Barcelona. We speak English and Spanish, most of the time at the same time, but we would appreciate it if you could send us the contents of your application in English.

About the Cornell Experience Modernization Initiative (CEMI)

The Cornell Experience Modernization Initiative (CEMI) is a multi-year program designed to improve the experience of students, faculty, staff, alumni, donors, patients, and partners by unifying and enhancing administrative systems and processes across all Cornell University locations. Its name CEMI is said as “See Me” because the focus is on you: the people who use Cornell’s systems and data to accomplish your goals.

What will you do:

Cornell University seeks an experienced and operationally focused Salesforce Operations Manager (CEMI) to oversee the day-to-day health, delivery, and continuous improvement of the university's enterprise Salesforce ecosystem. This role is responsible for managing and developing a high-performing team of Salesforce professionals who support multiple Salesforce orgs and Marketing Cloud across a diverse portfolio of academic, student-facing, administrative, marketing, and advancement solutions.

The Salesforce Operations Manager (CEMI) will provide operational leadership for the Salesforce team, overseeing workload management, sprint planning, service delivery, production support, platform enhancements, integrations, data integrity, security, and compliance. The role is accountable for ensuring team effectiveness, fostering professional development, establishing operational best practices, and promoting a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer-focused service.

This is a hands-on operational leadership role focused on maintaining a stable, scalable, and secure Salesforce environment while aligning platform capabilities with institutional priorities and delivering consistent value to campus partners.

This is a 2-year term appointment which may end or extend based on organizational needs, funding availability, and performance.

While position responsibilities vary, every member of our community is expected to foster a culture of belonging and a healthy work environment by communicating across differences; being cooperative, collaborative, open, and welcoming; showing respect, compassion, and empathy; engaging and supporting others regardless of background or perspective; speaking up when others are being excluded or treated inappropriately; and supporting work/life integration of oneself and others.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree with 5+ years of experience in Salesforce administration, operations, or platform management roles or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Experience managing teams, technical operations, or cross-functional delivery groups.
  • Strong understanding of Salesforce configuration, security, integrations, and release cycles.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage high-volume work across multiple Salesforce orgs and products.
  • Project management experience leading enhancements and small projects, defining deliverables, and keeping work on track.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate technical concepts clearly.
  • Experience with Agile methodologies and structured change management processes.
  • Proven ability to troubleshoot complex technical, data, and integration issues.

  • Collaborative leader skilled at building partnerships across units and disciplines.
  • Customer-centric mindset with commitment to delivering value and improving user experience.
  • High attention to detail, quality, and follow-through.
  • Commitment to privacy, data security, and responsible stewardship of university data.
  • Proven experience connecting inclusion, belonging and wellbeing practices to business goals.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with Salesforce Marketing Cloud.

ACV's Machine Learning organization is looking for a talented Machine Learning Engineer III to join our ML inspection team. In this role, you'll drive end-to-end computer vision solutions processing hundreds of thousands of vehicle inspections annually into reliable, actionable insights, directly reducing inspection turnaround time, improving valuation accuracy, and scaling the capabilities of our inspection platform. You'll design and train damage detection models while architecting the high-throughput serving infrastructure needed to keep those models performant under real production loads. As ACV continues to grow, you'll play a direct role in ensuring our inspection capabilities remain accurate, efficient, and resilient at scale.

This role goes beyond executing on a defined roadmap. You'll identify opportunities, shape solutions end-to-end, and take ownership of outcomes. You connect the dots between stakeholder needs and what's technically feasible, bringing recommendations grounded in both theory and practical constraints. When you hear a narrow question, you think about the broader system it lives in and build toward that.

The core responsibilities of this role are:

Design and train high-performance computer vision models for automated damage detection, focusing on precision, recall, and model robustness. Architect and maintain high-throughput, containerized microservices for model serving using REST/gRPC to ensure low-latency performance. Collaborate with business stakeholders to translate complex inspection requirements into scalable, production-grade ML solutions. Own the end-to-end model lifecycle, from experimentation and design to deployment and optimization in high-traffic environments. Design and maintain robust data pipelines using Kafka to ensure high-fidelity inputs for model serving and inference. Perform additional duties as assigned.

Experience designing and maintaining visual data annotation pipelines and evaluation frameworks for complex, real-world image datasets. Experience optimizing high-latency models for real-time inference Backend software engineering experience in the cloud (AWS / GCP) with a focus on microservices (docker) and the ML model development lifecycle. Experience building and maintaining streaming data pipelines (e.g., Kafka) for real-time model serving.

Preferred Qualifications:

Knowledge of ML frameworks and libraries, such as Kubeflow, Databricks, KServe and so on Experience designing evaluation frameworks for complex visual data

excerpt: This role is fully remote, open to candidates based anywhere in the United States outside New York.
description:
This role is fully remote, open to candidates based anywhere in the United States outside New York. Based in New York? Apply to the New York posting of this role instead.

A Different Kind Of Job Description

At Filed, we believe in radical transparency. Everything is open: company finances, team salaries, stock options, anonymous team feedback. That extends to how we talk about this job, so what you'll read here looks a little different from other job ads. It starts with why this is a terrible job. Then it explains why it might be the best career move you'll ever make.

Why this is a terrible job

This is an incredibly high-paced, high-tempo environment. We're making a generational bet to change all of our lives, and generational bets are not comfortable.

You will stop signing returns. There are no clients of your own here, no book to build, no partner track. If the thing you want is the next rung on a firm ladder, this job takes it away from you on day one.

You will be on calls most of the day. You carry 5 to 10 firms at a time through onboarding and you own whether they actually succeed, for 8 weeks each, with your name attached. When a firm is floundering in week six, that is yours to fix, and there is nowhere in this job to hide from it.

The calendar is not negotiable. Firms will not change their stack mid-season, so December and January are relentless and everything has to land before the February 1 freeze. Miss the window and you wait a year.

Tax law is objective, but what applies under it and how professionals interpret it is full of judgment. You can give two tax professionals the same task and get two different results where both are right. You will sit across from a partner who disagrees with what the system did, and you will have to explain it in their language, without hiding behind the software. At times it will feel like hitting your head against the wall.

Customers will sometimes get frustrated, because they expect deterministic results from probabilistic systems, and we're managing the expectations of some of the biggest firms in the world, including the Big Four. You will be the person in the room who has actually done their job, which means the hard calls land with you.

And the rhythm is real. It's tough. It's relentless.

Why it might be the best career choice you'll ever make

You already know how to win a room full of sceptical tax professionals, because you have been one. Here that is the whole job, and it compounds: every firm you bring through onboarding properly becomes a firm that stays, refers, and grows.

It's addictive to be part of a business when you know you're winning. Filed is adding millions of dollars of revenue every quarter, and in under two years we've become the market leader in a space with entrenched incumbents and a drastic need for new AI tools. When we come into head-to-heads with competitors, we win every time, because our product is superior.

The industry looks boring from the outside, but the problem is unsolved, and the space has been riddled with products below the mark for decades. When you push through the wall, there's a spark of joy: a customer says "wow, this is phenomenal." That keeps happening, and you will be the one in the room when it does.

The opportunity here is not only to make a great deal of money. It's to have real impact on our mission: making this profession extraordinary. Nobody became a tax professional for the admin. They got into this work to be creative with tax law, to have fun, and to change the fabric of society. Filed enables them to do exactly that.

We've raised $17.2 million to date, led by Northzone. Our focus now is to deliver the roadmap and continue to win.

What You'll Own

As a Tax Technology Specialist, you own the moment a firm goes from signed to genuinely working:

  • The technical demo on customer calls, where you show firms what Filed does and why it answers the problem you have lived yourself

  • Group onboarding, 5 to 10 firms at a time, from kickoff to the point where the firm is running real work through Filed without you

  • The relationship through the 8 weeks that decide whether a firm succeeds or quietly churns

  • The feedback loop back into product, so the friction you watch firms hit gets fixed rather than repeated

You'll see your decisions carry real weight for some of the most demanding professional users in the world within days, not quarters.

What You'll Be Responsible For

  • Running the technical demo alongside sales on firms that need a tax professional in the room

  • Onboarding firms in groups and staying their point person until they are genuinely winning, backed by customer support

  • Teaching: webinars, training sessions, and the ongoing work of making firms good at Filed

  • Translating between firms and engineering, so what you hear on calls turns into what gets built

  • Knowing the product well enough to be trusted on it, including catching output that would not pass a reviewer

Your Hard Skillset

  • You have prepared or reviewed real returns inside a real firm. Credentials are welcome but not required, what matters is that you've done the work

  • Real strength in either individual returns (1040) or business returns (1065, 1120, 1120-S, 990, 1041), enough that a partner takes you seriously in the first five minutes. One or the other is enough. Strength in both is a plus

  • You are comfortable in front of customers. Demos, training, difficult conversations, escalations

  • A high degree of confidence in a few of the major tax platforms, such as CCH Axcess, UltraTax, Lacerte, ProConnect, Drake, or GoSystem. Nobody is expert in all of them, and we don't expect you to be

  • You pick up software fast. A product surface, a new workflow, an integration conversation, none of it puts you off

  • Bonus if you've been through a SurePrep, GruntWorx, or AutoFlow implementation, or rolled new software out across a firm

Your Soft Skillset

  • Comfortable being uncomfortable and making calls with incomplete data

  • Empathetic and curious: building for the user, not just for the technically correct answer

  • Highly collaborative across product, engineering, and tax

  • Detail-oriented but pragmatic: you know when precision matters and when to move

  • You own your work and welcome the accountability that comes with it

A championship team

We think of ourselves as a sports team. Incredibly high performance, incredibly high standards, and real success to show for it. Being a championship team means working with people who are deeply proud of the work they do and have great fun doing it together.

We measure employee happiness constantly, and our eNPS is +60. We don't say that to brag. We say it because a team playing at this tempo only holds together if people genuinely love being on it. Every four months, the whole company comes together for an offsite.

What Filed Stands For

Not posters. Not corporate language. Real operating standards.

No problem is someone else's problem. If you see it, it's yours. Bugs, customer confusion, missed expectations, internal friction. We don't pass problems sideways and we don't hide behind roles. You fix the typo even if you didn't write it, jump into a customer issue even if it's not your department, escalate early, and close loops fully. Ownership means you drive resolution, not that you suffer silently or burn out doing everything alone.

Waiting is not a strategy. Momentum is our advantage. We don't wait for perfect information or stall because something is unclear. You ship a V1 instead of debating V5, test instead of theorize, run small experiments instead of requesting big approvals, and propose solutions instead of just naming blockers. Speed is powerful. Sloppiness is not, and recklessness has no place in a high-trust industry.

We run toward the fire. When something breaks, we move. Tax is high-stakes and trust is fragile. We acknowledge issues immediately, communicate clearly and often, prioritize customer-impacting problems fast, and stay on it until it's fully resolved. Firefighting is a strength, not panic, and never an excuse for preventable mistakes.

We win on customer experience. AI will commoditize. Features will copy. Pricing will compress. Experience won't. We respond faster than customers expect, communicate proactively, think like a partner rather than a ticketing system, and anticipate needs before they're raised. Overdelivering means raising the standard of care, not overpromising, hero culture, or burning the team out.

Who This Suits

This is a very fun environment, but it only suits people who meet the criteria we're looking for:

  • People who want to win

  • People who have a point to prove

  • People who want to write their own job descriptions

How We Pay

Nothing at Filed is behind closed doors. Everyone here sees everyone else's salary, because we believe transparency creates trust, and trust is the foundation of excellent teamwork. Compensation isn't a negotiation. Depending on your location, everyone receives the same three offers, and all of our offers are above market benchmarking.

This role is assessed at Level 3. The salary and equity bandings are:

  • Most Equity: $85,800 per year + $130,027 of equity

  • Great Equity: $93,600 per year + $86,684 of equity

  • Good Equity: $101,400 per year + $43,342 of equity

We run performance reviews every four months. Meet your goals and you can expect to double your equity by the end of your first year.

One more thing, in the spirit of transparency: some people who apply for this role will be assessed at a different level. If the team determines your level of responsibility sits differently, we'll adjust the offer accordingly.

Benefits

  • Platinum-level medical insurance, fully covered for you, with 100% coverage for your dependents as well

  • Dental insurance

  • Vision insurance

  • 401(k) retirement plan

  • Paid maternity and paternity leave

  • A minimum of 30 days of paid holiday every year

  • Your choice of the latest and greatest computers, plus a budget for your home office setup

  • Company-wide offsites every four months

The process

  • Quick intro call (30 minutes)

  • Product walkthrough and async exercise (60 minutes)

  • Final round with our team (60 minutes)

In just 2.5 hours, you'll be wanting early access, just like the rest of our team, to get into the product and start building a generational company, even before your first day.

About Filed

Filed is the AI tax preparer trusted by America's accounting firms.

Taxes might seem boring, but they are the $5 trillion backbone of the US economy. Globally, nearly $15 trillion in taxes is collected every year. Behind every dollar of it sits a professional making judgment calls, and the industry that does this work is breaking under a talent shortage no one has solved. We're fixing it. Firms run Filed inside the systems they already use, and we're backed by Northzone, Neo, Analog, and Raine.

There has never been a more exciting time to work on a problem this complex. Join us while "I was there when it all started" is still true.

The Procurement Manager is a broad, hands-on procurement professional responsible for leading sourcing, negotiation, contracting, supplier management, and other procurement initiatives across a diverse range of categories. This role partners directly with business leaders, Finance, Legal, and other stakeholders to evaluate commercial opportunities, negotiate favorable outcomes, manage supplier relationships, and improve how the organization purchases goods and services.

In addition to core procurement responsibilities, this role will coordinate the organization's corporate insurance program, partnering with internal stakeholders, brokers, carriers, and other external partners on renewals, coverage administration, certificates of insurance, claims coordination, and related risk-management activities.

The ideal candidate has developed broad procurement judgment rather than specializing in a single category or narrow portion of the sourcing process. This individual should be comfortable taking an initiative from initial business need and market assessment through sourcing, negotiation, contracting, implementation, and ongoing supplier management.

Essential Duties

Strategic Sourcing & Procurement

  • Lead sourcing and procurement initiatives across a broad range of goods and services, managing the process from initial business requirement through supplier selection, negotiation, contracting, and implementation.
  • Develop sourcing strategies based on business requirements, supplier markets, spend, competitive dynamics, incumbent performance, and opportunities for cost reduction or value creation.
  • Lead competitive sourcing processes, including RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, supplier evaluations, bid analysis, and supplier negotiations.
  • Negotiate commercial terms with suppliers, including pricing, fee structures, service levels, renewal terms, price protections, termination rights, and other key business provisions.
  • Evaluate supplier proposals and contract economics using quantitative and qualitative analysis, including total cost of ownership, pricing benchmarks, utilization, demand, and alternative commercial structures.
  • Develop clear recommendations and business cases that enable leaders to make informed supplier and purchasing decisions.
  • Partner with Legal and business stakeholders throughout contract negotiations to ensure commercial and contractual considerations are appropriately addressed.
  • Manage supplier renewals proactively, identifying opportunities to reduce cost, improve commercial terms, consolidate suppliers, adjust services, or test the external market.
  • Build productive supplier relationships while maintaining appropriate commercial discipline and accountability.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify the supplier landscape, improve purchasing processes, reduce unnecessary spend, and increase procurement effectiveness.
  • Support procurement operations and governance, including purchase orders, contracting processes, procurement systems, policies, and controls.
  • Use procurement and spend data to identify trends, opportunities, risks, and areas requiring management attention.
  • Prepare and present financial analyses, sourcing recommendations, supplier comparisons, and procurement updates to business and executive leadership.
  • Manage multiple sourcing, contracting, and supplier initiatives simultaneously with limited oversight.

Insurance & Risk Coordination

  • Coordinate the day-to-day administration of the organization's corporate insurance program in partnership with Finance leadership, insurance brokers, carriers, Legal, and other internal stakeholders.
  • Coordinate annual insurance renewals, including collection and validation of exposure data, completion of applications, review of coverage and pricing proposals, and preparation of information required for renewal decisions.
  • Maintain organized records of insurance policies, coverage limits, premiums, deductibles, renewals, certificates, and related documentation.
  • Coordinate certificates of insurance and other evidence-of-coverage requests from customers, vendors, landlords, and other counterparties.
  • Partner with Legal, Procurement, business stakeholders, and the organization's insurance broker to evaluate contractual insurance requirements and identify potential coverage gaps or unusual requirements.
  • Assist with claims administration and communication among internal stakeholders, brokers, carriers, and third-party administrators as needed.
  • Review insurance program costs and alternatives and help identify opportunities to improve coverage, program structure, or overall cost effectiveness.
  • Serve as a knowledgeable internal point of contact for routine insurance questions while appropriately escalating complex coverage, claims, and risk matters to brokers, carriers, Legal, or leadership.

Procurement Program & Business Partnership

  • Develop and improve procurement policies, procedures, templates, reporting, and operating practices that balance appropriate controls with efficient business processes.
  • Build strong relationships across Finance, Legal, IT, Human Resources, Marketing, Operations, and other business functions.
  • Work comfortably with stakeholders ranging from individual budget owners to senior executives, adapting communication and recommendations to the audience.
  • Help business partners challenge assumptions, evaluate alternatives, and make commercially sound decisions rather than simply processing purchasing requests.
  • Stay current on procurement practices, supplier markets, commercial trends, technology, and relevant insurance and risk-management developments.
  • Lead or support special projects and cross-functional initiatives as needed.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Strong sourcing and negotiation capability with demonstrated experience producing measurable commercial outcomes.
  • Broad procurement experience across multiple spend categories, supplier types, and business functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage the full procurement lifecycle rather than only one component of the sourcing or contracting process.
  • Strong commercial judgment and ability to understand the broader business implications of supplier pricing, contract structures, risk, and operational requirements.
  • Excellent analytical and quantitative skills, including the ability to analyze pricing, spend, supplier proposals, total cost, and financial trade-offs.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to distill complex commercial issues into clear recommendations.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and establish credibility with senior business leaders.
  • Ability to navigate competing stakeholder priorities and drive decisions without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Strong project-management and organizational skills with the ability to manage numerous initiatives simultaneously.
  • Comfortable working in procurement, contract lifecycle management, ERP, and related business systems; experience with Coupa or similar source-to-pay platforms is preferred.
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and proficiency with PowerPoint and other standard business applications.
  • Experience working with corporate insurance programs, insurance brokers, risk management, or commercial insurance is preferred but not required for an otherwise strong procurement candidate.

  • 5+ years of progressive procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier management, or related commercial experience.
  • Demonstrated experience independently leading complex supplier negotiations and sourcing initiatives.

  • Experience partnering directly with Finance, Legal, and senior business stakeholders.

title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Summary

The Clinical Nurse Educator – Agency Operations serves as the primary clinical education liaison to subcontracted agency partners and is responsible for assessing education needs and for the development, delivery, and evaluation of clinical education and training programs tailored to each agency. This role ensures that agency nursing staff receive comprehensive onboarding, continuing education, and performance support in alignment with organizational standards, regulatory requirements, and evidence-based practice. The Clinical Nurse Educator partners with agency leadership, utilizes virtual learning technologies, and supports staff development to promote high-quality, patient-centered care across the agency network.

This position will primarily focus on subcontracted agency partnerships, while maintaining a collaborative relationship with CSI Nursing to support shared initiatives and operational needs when appropriate.

include the following. Other duties may be assigned, as necessary.


Agency Partner Liaison and Needs Assessment

☎ Community Phone

Community Phone is building the best phone for communities in America. You’ll spend your time connecting with customers who already want to hear from us. That means taking inbound calls and reaching out to people who’ve submitted form fills requesting more info or callbacks. No cold calling, just helping customers who’ve already raised their hands, and making sure to ALWAYS BE CLOSING.

We love to laugh, but we take values and performance seriously. Community Phone probably isn’t for you if you:

If you don’t have these, this role isn’t for you.

💙 Community Phone Culture

Community Phone has a customer-obsessed culture. We are looking for team members who love our product and mission.

Beyond the job description, here are some traits members of our team share:

We value Curiosity and learning in our employees. We promote open-mindedness, embrace mistakes, and encourage challenging questions for personal growth. We create a culture of continuous learning to empower our team to tackle challenges and excel in their roles.

Efficiency Where it Counts. We operate lean, optimizing resources to improve our products and deliver a world-class customer experience. We prioritize value over excess, embodying a scrappy and resourceful spirit to achieve our mission and values.

We prioritize taking decisive action over deliberation, recognizing that building a world-class product requires pushing personal limits and taking risks. We believe that a Bias Toward Action is essential for achieving our goals and delivering exceptional results to our customers.

We strive for Transparency and prioritize open, Direct communication. This helps us resolve issues quickly and build strong relationships with our stakeholders.

We take our work seriously and see it as a reflection of who we are. We're always looking for ways to improve and are open to feedback. We approach our work with a sense of ownership and a desire to deliver the best possible results. By embodying a Founder Mindset, we're able to achieve our goals and create exceptional products.

We value a Caring Mentality. Our customers come first, and we collaborate to provide exceptional service. We prioritize teamwork over personal accolades, fostering a customer-focused culture that drives our success and promotes a supportive work environment.

Growth at Community Phone

We’re not here to play small. Landlines are disappearing, customers need us, and we’re growing like crazy. That means if you crush it here, we’ll keep giving you more responsibility (and more money) until you say, “uncle”.

  • More sales = more base. Love selling? Keep crushing your goals, and your base pay can grow right alongside your commission checks.
  • Switch it up. Think you’d shine in another department? People have moved into different teams here and thrived.

We move fast. If you’re ambitious, hungry, and ready to prove yourself, there’s basically no ceiling on what you can do here.

Keeping it 💯

We take feedback seriously- that’s how we keep getting better. Community Phone has already made big changes, and we’ll never stop improving to make this a place where ambitious, kind people love to work.

That said, we’re not for everyone. We’re a startup growing fast into something big-which means it’s fast, challenging, and always changing. If you see yourself as hungry, empathetic, and ready to grow with a team that’s building something meaningful, we can’t wait to meet you!

Security Engineering is a new organization at DGX Cloud, accountable for the security outcome of the platform, and this is the architecture function inside it. You will define the security design standard for DGX Cloud, a bar that sits above the company floor, and hold it from inside the teams doing the building.

Security here is fleet horizontal and stack vertical, so your scope runs from the hardware root of trust and the hardened baseline, through tenancy and GPU workload isolation, to the services and APIs built on top, across every DGX Cloud engineering organization. A small team of Principal Engineers will report to you and hold the bar at domain depth. This is still a hands-on seat, and you stay in the design with them. You will also serve as DGX Cloud's technical interface into NVIDIA's central security organization. There is no architecture review board here and no approval queue; the bar holds because the strongest security engineers in the room helped set it and helped ship it.

What You Will Be Doing:

  • Set the DGX Cloud Security Bar:Own the security design standard across DGX Cloud (tenancy, GPU workloads, identity, supply chain, and isolation) and make it concrete. Reference architectures, golden paths, and requirements engineers can actually build against, not a policy library.

  • Hold the Bar by Building:Embed with engineering teams on real work: join the design, learn the code, help ship the thing rather than grade it afterward. The posture is not "you did this wrong." It is "here are the considerations we need to meet, I will help, let's go to work."

  • Architect the Security Platform:Drive the multi-year architecture for the common security infrastructure the fleet runs on: hardened baselines and patch SLOs, deploy-time policy and admission control, workload identity, supply-chain provenance through signing and attestation, and detection and response tuned to GPU workloads.

  • Engineer Classes of Risk Out of Existence:Finding a vulnerability is 4% of the work; building the system where it cannot happen again is the other 96%. You will attack recurring risk at its architectural root, including offensively against our own designs, and feed what you find back into the paved roads, the baselines, and the detections.

  • Grow the Principal Engineering Bench:Lead a small team of Principal Engineers who report to you and hold the bar across domains. Set their technical direction, hire into the gaps, and grow each of them into deeper scope than they arrived with.

We operate horizontally across vertically organized teams, with influence rather than authority.

  • Communicate Risk Upward:When something is going to ship below the bar, write down the gap and what closing it would take, and put it in front of the executives who hold the risk pen. This is a developer relations role rather than an engineering role because the leverage is breadth. An engineer improves one engine. This role shapes how acceleration lands across the ecosystem and influences which parts of it get there first.

  • Build and deepen technical expertise in analytical data processing, including query execution and optimization, columnar and vectorized processing, and distributed execution. Serve as a technical advocate and trusted resource for the developers building and operating these systems, working with cross-functional partners to drive adoption of NVIDIA technologies such as Sirius, cuCascade, RAPIDS, cuDF, nvCOMP, and CUDA-X Data Processing.

Hire the top 1%

  • You'll make sure we hire the right people at the right time, not just the roles hiring managers announce they need, and that the people we hire are connected to our mission and likely to grow and succeed here.

Keep extraordinary people, and only them

  • You'll be the primary voice of culture alongside the co-founders. You'll make sure everyone understands the mission, what part of the system they're in, what their work feeds into, how their performance is evaluated, and why it matters.
  • You'll make sure our most remarkable people stay: that they have the space, control and authority to do great work, that they feel pushed, capable and cared for, and that they get bigger scope before someone else offers it.
  • You'll make sure we don't keep the people we shouldn't.   • You'll partner with the executive team to build a bench of phenomenal leaders. We're building our leadership bench; your job is to make sure that in 18 months we have the leaders we need, whether we grow them or hire them.

We're a fast-growing, YC-backed company built on curiosity, a bias toward action, and a founder mindset. We'd rather ship something small and learn than debate it for a month. You'll report directly to Ellie Lasater-Guttmann, a cofounder. You will sit on the leadership team.

You will sit at the center of a three-sided relationship: Kevel as the platform provider, our retail partners as the network operators, and their supplier advertisers as the demand side. This is a high-impact role for someone who understands that context and can navigate it fluently, translating platform capabilities into real results for both retailers and the brands buying their media.

LOCATION: REMOTE - UNITED KINGDOM. This position is 100% remote. Applicants located anywhere within the United Kingdom are encouraged to apply. Applicants must be legally eligible to work within the United Kingdom.

Our compensation philosophy is based on the candidate’s specific working location and experience level. This means that we will take a no negotiationapproach in our recruitment and offer processes. We also have a transparent ‘Total Rewards Philosophy’ we’d be happy to share with you which describes our overall approach to compensation and benefits in full detail! Our recruitment team can share more about this with you in an initial phone interview and will be happy to answer any questions you have related to compensation at Kevel!

Campaign Trafficking & Operations

  • Hands-on experience with actual analysis tasks, ideally recent, leveraging modern AI tools.

Community Phone is building the Toast for phones. We are the friendliest phone company in the country, supporting >20,000 customers nationwide.

You’ll coach, guide, and develop your team to deliver outstanding customer experiences while maintaining strong operational execution. Team Leadership & Performance Management

  • Own your team’s core KPIs: CRI, CSAT, Retention, and Expansion.
  • Monitor daily performance dashboards and coach continuously toward improvement.
  • Conduct weekly 1:1s and structured coaching sessions with each team member.
  • Identify knowledge gaps, skill gaps, or behavioral inconsistencies and build targeted improvement plans.

  • Learn from team behaviors, both positive and negative, and share patterns and themes that improve team operations.

  • Build and manage agent schedules to ensure full coverage across shifts.
  • Handle monthly rotational shift assignments for your team.

  • Raise flags proactively when performance shifts, spikes occur, or process breakdowns appear.
  • Share insights with the Support Manager and other internal teams to drive continuous improvement.

Process Improvement & Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Identify operational bottlenecks and suggest fixes that improve efficiency or customer satisfaction.
  • Work with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing teams to surface recurring issues and propose solutions.
  • Improve documentation, training materials, and playbooks based on real case patterns.
  • Participate in cross-department initiatives to improve customer experience or internal workflows.

  • Participate in the hiring process by reviewing resumes, conducting interviews, and selecting top candidates.
  • Own all disciplinary actions, including coaching plans, written warnings, and terminations when required.
  • Hold team members accountable to expectations, performance targets, and behavior standards.
  • Calculate bonuses for your team each cycle with full accuracy and transparency.

Customer Experience

  • Maintain a customer-centric mindset and ensure decisions center on customer satisfaction and long-term value.
  • Perform customer-facing work roughly 10 percent of the week to remain close to customer pain points.
  • Use insights from customer interactions to inform coaching, process improvements, and strategy.
