The Opportunity

As a Sales Practice Risk Consultant, you will help identify emerging sales practice risks, uncover meaningful trends through data analysis, and influence risk mitigation strategies across MassMutual's advisory and securities business. Partnering with Compliance, Legal, Supervision, and Field leaders, you'll provide actionable insights that strengthen supervisory practices, support regulatory compliance, and help protect both advisors and clients.


The Team

The MassMutual Financial Advisors Supervisory Controls Group (SCG) is an established team of experienced Principals who collaborate to deliver practical solutions for advisors and management. Team members demonstrate strong business acumen, clear communication, accountability, and relationship-management skills.


Within SCG, the In-Depth Risk Analysis team generally conducts targeted reviews of advisor activity to identify patterns, trends, and potential areas of elevated sales practice risk across brokerage, advisory, annuity, and securities-related insurance business. The team translates complex data into actionable observations, documents areas of concern, and identifies where additional review, advisor education, file testing, or follow-up may be appropriate.


By documenting risk themes and helping determine whether additional monitoring is warranted, the team promotes consistent supervision, stronger documentation practices, and alignment with applicable Firm policies and regulatory expectations.


The Impact

As a Sales Practice Risk Consultant your responsibilities will include, but not be limited to the following:

  • Evaluate FINRA and SEC annual guidance and disciplinary actions, information from internal business partners, and direct observations to proactively identify potential sales practice risks, particularly those involving Regulation Best Interest (Reg BI).
  • Gather and analyze company-level data to establish metrics for Key Risk Indicators (KRIs).
  • Conduct in-depth reviews of advisors who meet or exceed established KRI thresholds.
  • Prepare clear, professional reports that communicate the risks reviewed and any resulting Items of Note for each advisor.
  • Meet with Regional Supervisory Directors (RSDs) and Agency Supervision staff to discuss written reports, observations, and consult on appropriate follow-up.
  • Track documentation of agency supervisory activity and notify RSDs when documentation is not received or does not sufficiently address identified risk areas.
  • Partner with Compliance, the Field, MMLIS, Legal and other Home Office business partners on regulatory matters and surveillance escalations.
  • Stay apprised of current knowledge of Firm policies and the evolving regulatory environment.
  • Complete ad hoc projects, reviews, and other duties as requested.

Job Description Summary:

Location: Charlotte, NC


The Director, Franchise Commercial Execution leads the integrated execution capability agenda for CDE, MSC, PICOS, ESH, and Space within bottler operations. This leader translates the commercial agenda into practical standards, connected deployment plans, bottler adoption, and sustained marketplace execution.


The role owns the day-to-day leadership, integration and delivery of these capabilities: connecting equipment, space, outlet standards, execution routines and market activation into one coordinated approach rather than separate programs.

This role partners with bottler commercial and sales teams, Franchise Operations, category and channel leaders, Customer teams, RGM and Finance to improve availability, visibility, execution quality and asset productivity, supporting balanced growth in revenue, volume, mix and transactions. Its primary accountability is execution capability performance across priority channels.


What You’ll Do for Us


Integrated Execution Capability Leadership


1. Lead CDE and Space Deployment and Productivity


  • Lead the Franchise CDE and Space agendas, aligning equipment deployment, redeployment, and shelf, cooler, and display opportunities with commercial and channel priorities.
  • Partner with bottlers, category, Customer and Finance teams on practical placement and merchandising recommendations, balancing outlet opportunity, utilization and investment requirements.
  • Track equipment and space implementation and productivity, close execution gaps and escalate investment or resource decisions through agreed governance.

2. Lead MSC Activation and PICOS Adoption


  • Own MSC (Market Street Challenge) planning and follow-through, coordinating market selection, readiness and field engagement around priority growth opportunities.
  • Lead PICOS deployment across priority channels, translating category and customer requirements into clear outlet standards embedded in selling tools, coaching and routines.
  • Use market findings and execution assessments to close availability, assortment, visibility, and merchandising gaps; assign actions, verify sustained improvement, and scale effective practices.

3. Strengthen ESH and Connected Capability Delivery


  • Lead the Franchise ESH agenda, aligning capability assessments and development plans with execution priorities set by the Senior Director II.
  • Partner with bottlers to embed practical standards, coaching and accountability in daily execution; simplify tools and strengthen measurement consistency.
  • Integrate CDE, MSC, PICOS, ESH and Space into one deployment plan, connecting milestones, dependencies and bottler commitments rather than managing separate programs.

4. Commercialize Category Innovation


  • Lead Franchise commercialization of category innovation, translating brand strategies and launch priorities into channel-specific deployment plans with bottlers.
  • Coordinate launch readiness across assortment, pack-price architecture, customer activation, availability, merchandising and field communication with accountable partners.
  • Track launch execution and commercial outcomes, resolve adoption gaps and convert market learnings into corrective actions and stronger future launches.

5. Deploy Pillar Programs


  • Lead bottler deployment of Coke TM pillar programs, aligning activation calendars, outlet priorities, execution standards and partner commitments.
  • Connect brand activation to selling routines and in-market execution, using CDE, Space, PICOS, MSC and ESH where relevant to deliver the intended shopper and customer experience.
  • Review program readiness, implementation and sustained execution; address gaps with bottlers and scale effective activation practices.

6. Lead Channel Planning


  • Lead commercial channel planning with category, channel, Customer, RGM and bottler teams, translating growth opportunities into prioritized channel and outlet actions.
  • Align portfolio, assortment, pack-price, availability, space and merchandising priorities with customer needs, bottler economics and execution feasibility.
  • Embed category priorities in JBP and ABP, agree execution measures, and review channel performance to refine plans and resource recommendations

Qualification & Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
  • At least 5 years of progressive experience in CPG, beverage, or a related industry, across commercial execution, sales, customer management, franchise operations, or execution capability roles.
  • Hands-on experience with equipment deployment and productivity, space and merchandising, outlet execution standards, market activation or sales execution capability building; working knowledge of CDE, MSC, PICOS, ESH and Space.
  • Demonstrated ability to turn commercial priorities into bottler-ready plans, field routines, adoption, and measurable marketplace improvements.
  • Experience working with bottlers or within a franchise system, influencing commercial and sales partners without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical skills, including execution scorecards, gap diagnosis, asset and space productivity analysis, and translation of insights into action.
  • Experience leading planning, deployment, and cross-functional stewardship routines in a complex, matrixed environment.
  • Understanding of channel strategy, customer dynamics and system economics, with the ability to balance growth opportunities, execution feasibility and bottler profitability.

Leadership Profile


  • Execution ownership: Takes accountability from planning and readiness through adoption, follow-through, and sustained results.
  • Connected thinking: Integrates CDE, MSC, PICOS, ESH and Space into one capability agenda rather than optimizing programs in isolation.
  • Influence without authority: Builds alignment and mobilizes bottler, field and cross-functional partners.
  • Commercial judgment: Connects execution choices to customer needs, asset productivity and balanced system growth.
  • Clarity and discipline: Simplifies complex priorities into usable standards, focused scorecards and actionable routines.
  • Capability builder: Uses coaching, practical tools and shared learning to strengthen execution consistency.
  • Constructive challenge: Surfaces gaps early, tests improvements, and escalates decisions with clear recommendations.

What We Can Do For You


  • Iconic Brand: Work on the most recognized brand in the world and be part of developing the next chapter.
  • Exposure to World-Class Leaders: Access to global leaders who will expand your network and expose you to emerging digital platforms and marketing insights.
  • Learning Culture: Access to resources and management programs that give you the tools to continually develop your skills and knowledge.

Position Title: Senior Director, Franchise Transformation

The Senior Director, Franchise Transformation is a strategic transformation leader responsible for unlocking the next generation of competitive advantage across assigned bottler geographies by redesigning how the KO–bottler system operates and ensuring transformation initiatives are fully adopted and realized in-market, unlocking step-change growth.

This role goes beyond stewardship of current performance. It is focused on redefining how the system wins by diagnosing structural opportunities, designing future-state models, and leading high-impact transformation initiatives that materially shift performance versus current ways of working.

Critically, the role serves as the bridge between enterprise strategy and in-market execution, ensuring that national transformation initiatives are effectively translated, embedded, adopted, and realized within local bottler markets. Identify, design, embed, and deliver transformations that fundamentally improve how the KO–bottler system operates and wins in-market and ensure their adoption and value realization at scale..

What You’ll Do for Us

1. Transformation Strategy and Opportunity Identification
Identify next-generation growth and capability opportunities across assigned territories
Diagnose structural performance gaps and define where to play and how to win shifts
Translate insights into a prioritized transformation roadmap
Quantify size of the prize and build clear, fact-based business cases

2. Design of Future-State Models
Lead the design of new operating models across critical domains, including route to market redesign, de-averaging and segmentation, and portfolio acceleration
Challenge existing paradigms and define best-in-class system approaches
Ensure alignment with enterprise priorities

3. End-to-End Transformation Delivery
Lead cross-functional teams to deliver transformation initiatives end-to-end
Drive from concept to pilot to scale with clear success criteria
Establish governance, milestones, and execution discipline
Remove barriers across KO and bottler organizations to ensure delivery at pace

4. Enterprise-to-Local Translation and Embedding
Act as the primary integrator of national transformation initiatives within assigned geographies
Translate enterprise strategies into clear, actionable plans tailored to local market realities
Ensure initiatives are understood, embedded, and operationalized
Partner with bottler leadership to adapt execution while maintaining strategic integrity
Establish feedback loops to refine enterprise strategies based on in-market learning

5. Transformation Adoption and Realization
Own adoption and realization of transformation initiatives, not just deployment
Define and track adoption KPIs such as routine integration, usage rates, and capability activation
Define and track value realization KPIs such as incremental volume, share growth, revenue quality, and productivity gains
Ensure initiatives deliver measurable business impact versus business case
Drive corrective action where adoption lags
Institutionalize successful changes into standard ways of working

6. Bottler and System Leadership
Act as a strategic transformation partner to bottler leadership
Influence and align stakeholders across bottler teams and KO functions
Drive behavioral and organizational change across the system

7. Capability Building and Replication
Codify successful transformations into scalable playbooks
Enable replication across markets and bottlers
Build system capabilities in segmentation, data-driven decision making, and execution routines
Contribute to a repeatable transformation engine for Coke Florida + Puerto Rico

Transformation roadmaps with quantified value creation
Pilot programs with clear success metrics
Redesigned strategies across RTM, segmentation, and portfolio
Execution playbooks and replication frameworks
Demonstrated impact on volume, share, revenue quality, and efficiency

10–15+ years in franchise operations, commercial strategy, or transformation roles
Proven track record of leading large-scale transformation initiatives
Experience working within or alongside franchise systems

Capabilities

Strategic problem solving

Transformation leadership

Commercial acumen
Influence without authority
Adoption and realization focus

Challenges legacy ways of working
Owns outcomes end-to-end
Balances strategy and execution
Drives speed, focus, and accountability
Acts as a force multiplier across the system

Position: Road and Trail Program Coordinator

Reports to: Manager, Marketing and Events (Domestic Programs)

Overview

Athletics Canada is the national sport organization for track and field, cross county, road, mountain, and trail running. Its purpose is to support high performance athletics excellence at the domestic and international level and to provide leadership in developmental athletics in partnership with its provincial/territorial branch partners. Athletics Canada is a not-for-profit, charitable organization operating under a Board of Directors elected by provincial/territorial members.

The Job

Athletics Canada is seeking an organized, collaborative and passionate Road & Trail Program Coordinator to support the continued growth and development of road running, trail running and mountain running across Canada.

The successful candidate will play an important role in delivering Athletics Canada's national Road & Trail programs and services, working closely with Athletics Canada staff, Provincial/Territorial Branches, event organizers, athletes, coaches, and volunteers. The position will have direct responsibility for several national programs while also supporting the delivery of several Canadian Championships and the Mountain & Trail National Team.

This is an ideal opportunity for someone who understands the culture and landscape of road, trail and mountain running and is excited by the opportunity to help build stronger, more accessible and better-connected programs across Canada.

The position reports to the Marketing & Events Manager, while working closely with the Director, Domestic Programs & Safe Sport on program development, policy implementation, governance and the broader Athletics Canada Road & Trail strategy.

Responsibilities

1. Program Development & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop strong relationships with Athletics Canada Branches, event organizers, clubs, athletes, coaches, officials and other stakeholders within the Road & Trail community.
  • Provide leadership to the Athletics Canada Off-Track Committee and related working groups.
  • Monitor developments within Canadian and international Road & Trail running and identify opportunities for program improvement.
  • Assist with communications, resources and educational materials for event organizers and participants.
  • Collect and maintain program data and provide regular updates and reports to Athletics Canada staff.
  • Contribute to broader Athletics Canada initiatives that support participation, athlete development, competition and excellence in Road & Trail running.


2. Road, Trail & Mountain Canadian Championships

Support the Marketing & Events Manager in the planning and delivery of Athletics Canada Road, Trail and Mountain Running Canadian Championships, including:

  • Assist with championship documentation, host selection, contracting, and coordination with host organizations.
  • Assist with event planning, timelines, communications and operational requirements.
  • Support championship eligibility, registration, technical and event information.
  • Support championship marketing and promotional activities.
  • Assist with post-event reporting, evaluation and continuous improvement.
  • Develop strong working relationships with Race Directors, Local Organizing Committees, and other event partners.

3. Road Race Label Program

Lead the ongoing delivery and development of the Athletics Canada Road Race Label Program, including:

  • Manage applications, label requirements, agreements and communications with approved Road Race Label events.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for event organizers
  • Coordinate event requirements, including sanctioning, course certification, technical requirements and other Athletics Canada standards.
  • Support the development and implementation of event benefits, marketing opportunities and athlete-facing communications.
  • Monitor program participation and identify opportunities to strengthen the quality, profile and reach of the national road race calendar.
  • Work with Athletics Canada staff and Branches to ensure consistent application of national requirements.

4. Mountain & Trail National Team

Support the delivery and development of Athletics Canada's Mountain & Trail National Team program, including:

  • Support Athletics Canada's participation in international mountain and trail running championships and events.
  • Assist with athlete and coach communications and team administration.
  • Support team selection, registration, travel and logistical planning.
  • Assist with national team event preparation and on-site team operations.
  • Contribute to the continued development of a strong and sustainable national mountain and trail running program.

5. Course Measurement & Certification

Coordinate the Athletics Canada Road Course Measurement & Certification Program, including:

  • Manage applications and communication with event organizers seeking course certification.
  • Maintain an accurate national database of certified courses and renewal dates.
  • Support the transition to updated course certification requirements and processes.
  • Provide guidance to event organizers regarding course measurement and certification requirements.
  • Help develop and coordinate pathways and training for certified course measurers.

6. National Road & Trail Sanctioning

Support the implementation and ongoing administration of the Athletics Canada Road & Trail Sanctioning Framework, including:

  • Work with Athletics Canada Provincial/Territorial Branches and event organizers to support adoption and implementation of national minimum requirements.
  • Assist with the development of tools, resources and communications to support consistent application across Canada.
  • Monitor implementation and identify areas requiring clarification, education or additional support.
  • Work closely with the Director, Domestic Programs & Safe Sport on policy implementation and governance matters.
  • Help ensure that Athletics Canada's national Road & Trail programs are aligned with broader organizational policies and strategic objectives.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of technical knowledge, organizational ability and a genuine understanding of the Road & Trail running community.

  • Understanding of the Road & Trail landscape – Knowledge of competition rules, age categories, competition formats and the culture of the road, trail and mountain running community. Familiarity with event management and delivery is strongly preferred.
  • Strong organizational skills – Ability to manage multiple programs, deadlines, projects and communications streams simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail.
  • Program coordination experience – Experience coordinating programs, events or projects, ideally within sport, nonprofit, community development or a similar environment.
  • Strong communication skills – Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with athletes, coaches, volunteers, event organizers and organizational partners.
  • Bilingualism – Fluency in both English and French is considered an asset.
  • Athlete and participant focused – Comfortable communicating directly with athletes and participants in an empathetic, respectful and responsive manner and able to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds and at different stages of their athletic journey.
  • Collaborative mindset – Ability to work effectively with the Athletics Canada Off-Track Committee, Provincial/Territorial Branches, Local Organizing Committees and colleagues across Canada.
  • Solution-oriented approach – Proactively identifies opportunities to improve programs, solve problems and strengthen the overall Road & Trail system.
  • Independent and self-motivated – Comfortable working remotely and managing responsibilities independently while maintaining strong communication with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Passion for sport – Genuine interest in running and a commitment to supporting the growth and development of Road & Trail running in Canada.

Work Location

This is a fully remote position based in Canada.

The position requires occasional evening and weekend work, particularly around competitions, meetings and national team activities.

Regular domestic travel will be required for Canadian Championships, national team activities, meetings and other Athletics Canada events.

Occasional international travel may be required in support of the Mountain & Trail National Team or other international activities.

The position requires the ability to work independently in a remote environment while maintaining effective communication and collaboration with colleagues and stakeholders across Canada.

Today, we're harnessing the boundless possibilities of AI to build the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brain of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Accomplishing unprecedented goals calls for imagination, inventiveness, and exceptional talent from around the world. As a NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in a diverse, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Join our team and discover how you can build a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA's Silicon Co-Design Group (SCG) leads the full product development lifecycle, from early architecture definition through silicon bringup to product release. The ArchDev team is the hub for silicon and system-level feature development, driving tradeoff analysis, system integration, and POR alignment across the entire organization. This is where ideas become chips, and chips become products that define the state of the art — and we're building that future with some of the most motivated engineers in the industry. We're looking for a Senior Memory Systems Engineer to own HBM and LPDDR integration in sophisticated SoCs. This role covers the full stack, including silicon, package, embedded software, testing, and product development. The engineer will resolve the toughest system-level memory challenges throughout the process, building solutions that hold up at scale.

What you'll be doing:

  • HBM & LPDDR System Integration and Bringup: Drive HBM and LPDDR system integration, bringup, characterization, and debug for next-generation SoCs — taking memory subsystems through the full arc from first silicon to production-ready at scale.

  • Full-Stack Memory Closure: Own memory performance, power management, thermal, and reliability closure across silicon, package, board, and firmware — translating characterization results into signed-off operating points and release criteria that the full program depends on.

  • Post-Silicon Margining, VF Shmoo & Correlation: Lead post-silicon margining, VF shmoo, eye, and correlation work across voltage, temperature, and frequency — building the characterization foundation that underpins every product decision downstream.

  • Memory Debug: Training, Calibration, SI/PI & Stability: Debug and resolve memory training, calibration, SI/PI, and system-level stability issues — the class of problems that sit at the intersection of electrical, physical, and software behavior and demand deep cross-domain expertise to resolve at scale.

  • Validation & Characterization Planning: Define validation, characterization, and issue-tracking plans across chip programs — building the framework that ensures the right tests exist, the right data gets collected, and issues are tracked with enough fidelity to close.

What we need to see:

  • BS or MS in EE/CE — or equivalent experience.

  • 12+ years in HBM, LPDDR, or high-speed memory systems, with hands-on depth in silicon bringup, characterization, and debug at scale. PHY controller development experience is a significant plus and will set you apart.

  • Deep command of SI/PI, timing, margining, and memory training behavior — and the multi-functional fluency to work across design, package, firmware, validation, and product teams without losing the thread.

  • HBM PHY and controller architecture familiarity is useful context, but what this role actually demands is rarer: the system-level instinct to see where memory behavior is about to become a product problem — and the inventiveness to resolve it before it does.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

  • AI-Accelerated Debug & Root Cause Analysis: Use LLM-assisted tools and ML models to pattern-match failure signatures across VF shmoo, eye diagrams, and margining datasets — converging on root cause and outlier detection faster than manual triage, with engineering judgment setting the bar for what the model can decide.

  • Experience with HBM3/HBM3E specifics, specific JEDEC margins, thermal-electrical co-sim, ECC methodology & power management is highly desired.

  • Intelligent Test & Validation Automation: Automate data collection, test sequencing, and results analysis across characterization programs — cutting cycle time from silicon arrival to product-ready data and freeing bandwidth for problems that require human expertise.

  • LLM-Assisted Architecture & Trade-Off Exploration: Accelerate architecture exploration, spec navigation, and cross-domain trade-off analysis using LLMs — surfacing precedents from prior programs and building characterization plans for expert review.

Memory is where performance lives or dies. At the power densities and bandwidths NVIDIA's next-generation SoCs demand, memory systems engineering is one of the most consequential disciplines on the chip. The engineer in this role will have direct influence over whether products meet their performance, power, and reliability targets — and will resolve those challenges alongside some of the most motivated memory and silicon teams in the industry. We're building an encouraging environment where inventiveness is expected, and impact is real. If this is the level you want to operate at, we'd like to hear from you.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 196,000 USD - 310,500 USD.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Leave Specialist is responsible for administering and managing leave of absence programs, including but not limited to company-provided disability benefits (STD, LTD) as well as locally mandated programs across the United States and Canada, ensuring compliance with federal, state/provincial, and local regulations.

Typical responsibilities include but are not limited to the following.

  • Communicates with employees regarding their needs for leave and/or modified work schedules. Ensures that employees are aware of their responsibilities and of any documentation and notice required to qualify for and to take leave.
  • Handles the leave administration process from the employees’ initial notice of the need for leave to the return to work. This includes gathering and completing all required paperwork, determining leave eligibility, designating leave as FMLA-qualifying, requesting medical certification as needed, and accounting for intermittent and reduced schedule leave use.
  • Maintains reasonable communication with employees on leave to facilitate smooth and timely return to work; relays communication between employees and their managers during leave within reason.
  • Advises managers and employees on the interaction of leave laws with paid time off, workers compensation, and short-term and long-term disability benefits.
  • Oversees the return-to-work process for employees returning from extended FMLA, workers compensation, or other leave(s).
  • Facilitates other leave requests, which may include accommodation requests under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ACA) or the Accessible Canada Act (ACA).
  • Drafts and/or recommends revisions to company leave policies to ensure compliance with federal, state/provincial, and local laws and regulations.
  • Maintains complete and accurate records of leave and accommodation requests in accordance with specified legal requirements and documentation of best practices.
  • Preserves confidentiality of employee medical documentation and files.
  • Maintains knowledge of all applicable leave and accommodation laws including but not limited to the FMLA, ADA, Canada Labour Code, ACA and state/provincial and local laws.
  • Collaborate with key stakeholders including HR Business Partners, managers, payroll and legal teams to deliver timely, accurate and high-quality support.
  • Lead all ADA and ACA accommodation requests by facilitating the interactive process with employees and managers.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Extensive knowledge of the leave requirements and other legal protections afforded by the FMLA, ADA, Canada Labour Code, ACA and other applicable laws.
  • 5+ years of human resource experience managing centralized leaves and accommodations required.
  • Completion of specialized certification or training on FMLA/leave administration a plus.
  • Experience utilizing a digital workflow case management system to manage Leaves and Accommodations. ServiceNow Leave Management experience preferred
  • Experience working in a geographically dispersed organization with an employee population of at least 5k employees.
  • Experience with leave and absence tracking within an HRIS system. Workday experience preferred.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.

Frontline workers increasingly rely on intelligent, speech-enabled applications to access information, complete tasks, and interact with industrial systems. Cerence is bringing Voice AI and Embedded AI to tablets, industrial devices, HMIs, and operator interfaces across manufacturing environments.

The Senior Application Developer will build intelligent applications used directly by frontline workers and manufacturing operators. The Director of Demand Generation & Integrated Marketing builds and runs the connected demand-generation programs and integrated campaigns that create interest among priority audiences and move that interest toward meaningful action, with a primary focus on Shine Early Learning.


Reporting to the Vice President of Marketing, this role translates established Marketing strategy, OKRs and business priorities into executable programs, then carries the work through implementation, measurement and optimization. The Director has meaningful autonomy within that direction to make campaign and channel decisions, manage agency partners and improve performance.

This role sits at the center of a modern marketing ecosystem. It requires strong strategic judgment, disciplined execution and a clear understanding of how audiences move from awareness to action. The Director brings teams together around clear objectives, creates visibility into performance and keeps priority initiatives moving toward measurable results.


This role connects audience strategy, paid media, content, lifecycle marketing, web, creative, social media, and marketing performance intelligence around priority growth opportunities. The right person can build interest before an audience is ready to act, see how the full journey fits together and use evidence to improve the work over time.

Demand Generation & Integrated Marketing

description:
The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD)

About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

Compensation:

For this senior role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD based on experience level per month and in gross amount. This range acknowledges the strong expertise and significant contributions expected at this level. This is a fully remote role. We believe the best engineers can do world-class work from anywhere, and we hire accordingly. Work from where you do your best work.

About the Role:

We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform, to build and own the platform the security team runs on: the services that discover, scan, triage and route security findings, the event-driven bus that connects them, and the CI security gates every team's pipeline runs through.

This is a development role on the security team, not a security-analyst role. Most of your time goes into designing, building and operating services in Go and Python on Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, the existing fleet where it has grown faster than its upkeep, and the NATS-based event platform that moves findings, inventory changes and notifications between them. The security gates in our GitLab CI (SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning) and the agentic triage and review workflows are part of that platform, not the whole of it. Your job is to make these systems fast, low-noise, and reliable enough to be trusted by default without slowing delivery.

You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own detection and response and network and zero trust — your platform is what their work composes with.

At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we build. In this role you will build reusable agentic workflows (Claude Code skills, CI review agents, automated triage and verification) that multiply what the team can cover, and hold that review discipline in the platform code you own.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design, build, and operate security engineering services primarily in Golang and Python, on AWS and Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, and the upkeep, hardening and retirement of the existing ones.
  • Own the event-driven platform between the security services: the NATS bus, its contracts and consumers, delivery guarantees and observability — so a finding, an inventory change or an alert reaches every service that acts on it.
  • Integrate the platform end-to-end: scanners → finding system-of-record → tickets → metrics, so remediation state is visible and exam evidence is a by-product of engineering.
  • Own delivery of the security gates — SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning: scanner selection and tuning, suppression workflow mechanics, false-positive burn-down, and the rollout tooling that takes a gate from advisory reporting to enforcing without blocking delivery.
  • Build agentic security workflows: CI review agents, automated finding triage and verification, remediation helpers — tooling other engineers actually adopt.
  • Build the triage-to-remediation automation: validate true positives by hand enough to prove the tooling right, then automate the loop — reproduction context, fix guidance, and routing to the owning teams and to vulnerability-management operations.
  • Participate in threat modeling and secure design reviews for the services you build and the pipelines you own.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation for the services you own.

What We Look For:

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant backend experience.
  • Deployed significant changes to a production application in the past 30 days.
  • Strong proficiency in Golang, plus working proficiency in Python.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating event-driven or message-based systems (NATS, Kafka, or similar): contracts, idempotent consumers, replay, back-pressure.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipeline tooling — jobs, shared templates, runners — GitLab CI at fleet scale is a strong plus.
  • Hands-on web application security knowledge: the OWASP Top 10 in real code — able to find these issues, fix them yourself, and encode the detection so they stop recurring.
  • Hands-on experience with SAST, SCA, and secret-scanning tooling (e.g., Semgrep, CodeQL, Snyk, Trivy, Grype, gitleaks), including tuning them to a signal-to-noise ratio developers will tolerate.
  • Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your development work today, have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't, and have built agentic workflows that other engineers adopted.
  • Working knowledge of AWS and Kubernetes as deployment targets for the services you build.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills:

  • Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or consumer lending, especially with systems in cardholder-data or regulated scope.
  • Working knowledge of PCI DSS and SOC 2 as they apply to software development and change management — the platform you build is what produces that evidence.
  • Software supply-chain integrity: SBOM pipelines, dependency governance, artifact signing and provenance (Sigstore, SLSA).
  • Familiarity with policy-as-code and admission control (OPA, Kyverno, conftest) — your gates compose with the cluster's runtime policy-enforcement layer.
  • Exposure to bug bounty or external vulnerability report triage — enough to know what the automation you build has to get right.
  • Experience with threat modeling at a system level.

About You:

  • You measure yourself by other teams' code - a fix you shipped is good; a vulnerability class that stopped appearing across the fleet is better.
  • You'd rather ship a gate than publish a policy - you know that enforcement changes behavior and documents do not, and you build the enforcement so well that engineers want to keep it.
  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things.
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting.
    You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.
  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

Sezzle’s Technology Stack:

  • Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python
  • Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native
  • Backend: Golang
  • Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch
  • DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes
  • Version Control: Git
  • CI/CD: Gitlab
  • Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests
  • Open Source: Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome?

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

description:
Description

Fluent Trade Technologies is a global fintech software firm at the forefront of providing state-of-the-art technology to the world's largest global banks and hedge funds. Specializing in ultra low-latency strategy and market data solutions, Fluent is committed to delivering cutting-edge innovations to the Financial Industry. With a prominent Israeli R&D center in Jerusalem and global development centers, Fluent is a dynamic and collaborative environment.

Learn more about us at.

We are seeking a Big Data & Infrastructure Architect to spearhead the data architecture for our new FX Trading Analytics platform. You will be the primary authority on the big-data engine that powers real-time and historical analysis of liquidity, fill ratios, and market impact. This is a foundational role where you will select, implement, and optimize the "brain" of our analytics suite. The position is a remote position based in Ukraine.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Architecture & Tool Selection: Evaluate and select the optimal Big Data/NoSQL engine to handle high-frequency FX market data and trade execution logs.
  • Infrastructure Ownership: Own the end-to-end installation, configuration, scaling, and long-term maintenance of the database environment.
  • System Design & Configuration: Design the database schema and storage strategy to support massive datasets while ensuring high availability and resilience.
  • Query & Performance Optimization: Build and tune complex time-series queries (calculating metrics like Effective Spread and Last Look Hold Times) to ensure sub-second responses for real-time monitoring tools.
  • Knowledge Leadership: Act as the subject matter expert, training GUI developers and team members on best practices for efficient data retrieval and interaction with the data layer.
  • Technical Collaboration: Work closely with the team leader and GUI developers to ensure the data infrastructure perfectly supports the product requirements.

Requirements

  • Deep knowledge of at least one industry-leading Big Data or Time-Series database (e.g., ClickHouse, InfluxDB or ScyllaDB/Cassandra).
  • Proven experience managing "high-velocity" data environments (streaming ticks, execution logs, and order book events).
  • Strong proficiency in writing and optimizing complex queries for massive datasets (billions of rows).
  • Extensive experience in a Linux-heavy environment with a focus on system-level performance and low-latency tuning.
  • Ability to translate business metrics into efficient data structures without necessarily writing application-level code.
  • Excellent English communication skills.

Advantages:

  • Experience in the financial industry (FIX protocol, FX trading, etc.).
  • Background in high-performance hardware/software integration.
  • Experience with scripting for automation (Python, Bash)

Discovery Implementation Optimization Results Leveraging our in-house reporting dashboards, you will identify and select campaigns to review based on shortfalls you see from established client expectations. In other circumstances, cases will come directly to you from our Sales and Brand Management team, soliciting your advice on recommendations to correct campaign performance. Dive deep into campaign goals and make recommendations to help achieve results Partner with Data Science to build complementing reporting aspects related to campaign performance insights where needed.

Creative thinker with strong time management and organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail Ability to lead the discussions related to strategic recommendations or campaign performance in critical in-person meetings including quarterly business reviews, annual reviews, or save efforts. Director of Development & Automation

Why Digacore?

We’re a fast-paced, people-first MSP recently recognized as one of New Jersey’s Top Workplaces for 2026, with:

About the Role

Reports to: CTO

We’re looking for a Director to take ownership of Digacore’s Development & Automation (DNA) team — a capable group of developers, data, product, and AI specialists working across three streams: AI services for clients, internal data and reporting, and a client-facing software product. The direction is set; now it needs a leader to turn it into structure, consistency, and results, so the CTO can step back from the day-to-day.

You’ll start by getting to know the team and what’s in flight, then put the foundation in place — SOPs, guidelines, a delivery cadence, and KPIs that give leadership a clear view of where things stand — and grow the team as the work demands. You’re comfortable rolling up your sleeves to unblock a build or prove out a solution, but your impact comes from leading through others, not writing the code yourself.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the existing team: learn each person’s strengths, set clear ownership, and manage each one the way they need — including senior specialists who are deeper than you in their own domains
  • Set the standards: write and roll out SOPs and guidelines for how the team works — intake, prioritization, delivery, documentation, and handoffs — starting with our repeatable client AI Services processes
  • Own the KPIs: define and track the metrics that prove impact (time to deploy, delivery against dates, time saved, adoption, ROI) and give the CTO a clear monthly view of what’s on track and what isn’t
  • Run the team’s weekly delivery cadence so every initiative has an owner, a priority, a next step — and status is visible at any point without chasing people down
  • Own the roadmap across all three streams — when urgent asks compete, decide what comes first, what waits, and what doesn’t happen, and reset expectations with stakeholders
  • Take ownership of client AI engagements — assessment, setup, training, and custom builds — so they move from signed to live quickly and run without escalating to the CTO
  • Oversee product releases with the Product Owner and developers — pressure-test estimates, surface risk early, and hold to commitments
  • Back the internal data and reporting work — the data warehouse and leadership scorecard, including AI Services results — so leadership gets numbers it trusts
  • Be the escalation point on client issues — including security, compliance, and data privacy questions — and prepare the team to handle them well
  • Partner with leadership and department heads to identify manual work and friction, and turn it into automation and AI solutions
  • Grow the team when needed — identify gaps, define new roles, and hire and onboard as the function scales
  • Own tooling and vendor decisions, budget input, and capacity planning for the function

What Success Looks Like in Year One

  • Every team member known with clear ownership, and every initiative inventoried with an owner, priority, and next step
  • A weekly delivery cadence running, and a monthly KPI report the CTO can read in two minutes
  • Core SOPs written and followed, starting with client AI deployment
  • The CTO out of routine client engagements, with client builds moving from signed to live on a fast, predictable timeline
  • Shipped wins with documented ROI, and a clear view of where the team needs to grow next

What You Bring

  • Proven leadership: 7+ years in automation, development, data, or technical operations, including 3+ years leading a technical team with direct reports — coaching, accountability, and running a delivery cadence
  • You’ve built the playbook: a track record of putting SOPs, operating rhythms, and KPIs in place for a team that didn’t have them — and getting people to actually follow them
  • Experience leading people more technical than you — you set outcomes and check progress without micromanaging
  • Shipped AI, automation, or software that moved a measurable number — not pilots and slide decks
  • Strong technical grounding in the Microsoft stack (M365/Azure, Power Platform, Power BI), APIs, and integrations — enough to unblock, review, and build when needed
  • Comfortable in client-facing work, including tough conversations around data, security, and compliance
  • Strong business translation — you turn “we need X” from non-technical stakeholders into a delivered solution
  • Thrives in a lean, fast-moving environment — candidates who need heavy corporate structure won’t be the right fit

Nice to Have

  • MSP, SaaS, or multi-client service experience
  • Background in software product delivery or data/BI leadership

About the company:

The company is a purpose-driven provider of Patient Care products dedicated to improving the lives of patients and caregivers. With thousands of positive reviews and a globally distributed team, the company focuses on creating practical, well-designed solutions that address real-world caregiving needs.

Own Supply Chain Execution & Pipeline Visibility

  • Maintain >98% in-stock rate on top revenue SKUs, aged inventory <8% of total units, and drive inventory turns toward 5–8x annually.
  • Secure a minimum of 3 freight quotes per booking and ensure no forwarder is retained without performance data (ETD accuracy, delays, cost benchmarks).
  • Maintain and update a rolling 12-week supply plan, with AI-driven risk detection and reorder triggers before stockouts occur.

Drive Financial Discipline in Operations

  • Maintain a standing financial analysis for every active supplier — including cash flow impact, landed cost, and MOQ trade-offs — continuously updated via AI-powered tools.
  • Ensure no purchase order is committed to excess inventory without documented financial justification.
  • Track landed cost against target COGS on every order.
  • Deliver a monthly operations cost summary (freight, duty, storage, COGS trends) — compiled and formatted automatically via AI tools.
  • Ensure 100% application of Nairobi Protocol and all applicable duty exemptions.
  • Build and maintain an AI system that verifies HS codes and eligibility before every freight booking — zero exceptions.

  • Conduct a full operational audit within the first 60 days, clearly identifying what is working, broken, missing, and where AI can enhance execution.

  • Ensure all SOPs are documented, tested, live in Asana, and followed without supervision.
  • Audit every SOP for AI acceleration opportunities.
  • Build and implement at least 2 AI-powered tools within the first 6 months, and document and hand them off as repeatable team processes.
  • Ensure SOPs are reviewed quarterly and continuously optimized.

  • Address performance gaps within 7 days — no prolonged underperformance.

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

The Senior Director, AI Enablement owns the production of role-specific AI capability: the Skills, projects, agents, product education and workflows that make GPS, Prism and our data platform usable inside the job, for the roles that matter most. Training is a delivery mechanism for this work, not the product. The product is a working set of content and tools a Greystar team member can pick up and use, on real Greystar data, and a measurable change in how they operate.

This is the technical counterpart to the Director, Talent Development in People & Culture. That role owns the enterprise learning framework, leadership development and the learning technology stack, and is the distribution channel to the workforce. This role owns what gets distributed — the artifacts, the technical standards behind them, and the adoption they drive.

This is a builder’s seat with a leader’s remit. The right person is fluent enough in Claude, ChatGPT, AI tools, MCP and data platforms to author skills personally and set the bar for a team that does, and commercial enough to argue, in NOI terms, why a given workflow should be rebuilt at all.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Key Responsibilities

Role-Based Capability Production

  • Define, for each priority role, what “AI-enabled” concretely means in the workflow — which decisions, which reports, which repetitive steps — and build the artifacts, or work with the teams to build the artifacts and education that deliver it.
  • Author and ship Skills, projects and agent workflows grounded in Greystar’s metric definitions (Atlas), data platform (DMP) and intelligence products (GPS, Prism, LEAP); personally build the first versions, then scale the team’s output working closely with your HR counterpart to expand delivery.
  • Maintain a governed skill & tool library with ownership, versioning, test cases and deprecation — treated as a product, not a training catalogue.
  • Sequence work by leverage: key roles first, in lockstep with leadership, the GPS roadmap and the FDI Pod deployments.

Adoption and Measurement

  • Own the adoption metric for AI capability across eligible roles: active users, repeat usage, workflow coverage, time-to-first-value.
  • Instrument enablement artifacts so usage is visible without self-report; partner with Data Engineering on the consumption and usage feeds.
  • Run the feedback loop from the field into the artifacts — what breaks, what is ignored, what gets copied — and iterate weekly.
  • Report adoption alongside FDI Pod impact so cost and value are always shown together.

Partnership with People & Culture

  • Serve as the primary technical partner to the Director, Talent Development, and to People Strategy & Programs on AI readiness; P&C owns the pathway, readiness approach and competency framework, and this role owns the technical content and the tools.
  • Feed enablement artifacts and technical curriculum into Workday Learning and P&C programs as the distribution channel; do not build a parallel LMS.
  • Share role-level adoption data (active users, workflow coverage, time-to-first-value) with People Strategy & Programs so manager enablement and communications can target where readiness lags.
  • Jointly define what an “AI-ready” role profile looks like for hiring and internal mobility, with P&C owning the competency framework.

Standards, Safety and Governance

  • Set the technical standards for enablement artifacts: data access aligned to the External Data Sharing Framework and Unity Catalog permissions; no ungoverned data paths.
  • Ensure every skill is grounded in the definition of record (Atlas/GPS); when a skill and a legacy report disagree, the platform number travels.
  • Partner with InfoSec on prompt, data and model-flexibility standards as the model landscape changes.

Team Leadership

  • Lead and retool the AI Enablement team from a training orientation to a build orientation; hire for skill authorship and applied AI over instructional design where the two conflict.
  • Build a champion network inside the business units that extends the team without adding headcount, with clear standards for what champions may and may not ship.
  • Model the operating principle of the function: narrow aperture, ship, measure, iterate; say no to requests without a role, a workflow and a metric attached.

What We’re Looking For

Experience

  • Led an AI or technology enablement function in a large, complex organization through an actual adoption curve — not a pilot program.
  • Demonstrated hands-on record building with LLM tooling in production: skills, prompt systems, agent workflows or equivalent that other people used at scale.
  • Partnered closely with data or engineering teams to ground enablement in real systems and real data, and with HR or L&D as the distribution partner.
  • Measured adoption and outcomes rigorously and can distinguish reach, adoption and impact without prompting.
  • Experience in operations-heavy, distributed businesses (real estate, financial services, healthcare, logistics) is an advantage; multifamily is not required.

Skills and Capabilities

  • Technically credible: comfortable in Claude Enterprise / API, MCP, prompt and skill design, and reading a data model. Can build a working skill against a governed dataset without an engineer.
  • Commercially literal: connects an enablement artifact to a line in the P&L (NOI, hours, CAC) or does not build it.

  • Strong influencing across functions and levels; holds a boundary with HR and the business without creating friction.
  • Clear, concise communicator to a senior founder-led audience; candid about what is not working.
  • Comfortable in ambiguity, building structure where none exists, and abandoning it when it stops working

THE COMPANY
Established in early 2024, at Analogue Insight we are bridging the Analogue and Digital Worlds for Tomorrow through our Chiplet Solutions. Our core expertise lies in developing cutting-edge Chiplet technology that serves as the building block for advanced communication systems. Our Chiplets are designed to offer high performance, scalability, and integration flexibility, enabling our clients to achieve breakthroughs in computation speed, data processing, and connectivity. For more information about us, check out our website (Analogue Insight) and LinkedIn Page (Analogue Insight™: Overview | LinkedIn).

THE ROLE
We are seeking a motivated Graduate Custom Layout Engineer to join our layout team and help deliver high-quality analog and mixed-signal IP for our chiplet-based solutions, including high-speed SerDes, UCIe die-to-die PHYs and ADC/DAC blocks. Working alongside senior layout engineers and analog designers, you will learn to take blocks from floorplan through verification to tape-out on advanced FinFET technology nodes. This role is well suited to recent graduates who are fascinated by how circuits become silicon, enjoy detailed hands-on work, and want to grow quickly in a fast-moving, high-impact environment.
Hiring Manager:Christian Borelli, Founder and CSO.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Analog & AMS Block Layout: Implement layout for analog and mixed-signal building blocks (e.g. current mirrors, differential pairs, bias circuits, comparators, passive structures) under the guidance of senior layout engineers.
  • Advanced Node Layout: Learn and apply FinFET layout rules and practices on advanced technology nodes, including matching, symmetry, guard rings, well proximity and layout-dependent effects.
  • Verification & Sign-off Support: Run DRC, LVS and parasitic extraction, and debug and fix issues efficiently. Build exposure to EMIR, ESD/LUP and PERC checks as you progress.
  • Collaboration with Design Teams: Work closely with analog designers to understand circuit intent, sensitive nets and constraints, and translate them into robust physical implementations.
  • Scripting & Automation: Learn and use scripting (e.g. SKILL, TCL or Python) to automate repetitive tasks and improve layout productivity and consistency.
  • Documentation & Reviews: Document layout decisions and verification status, and take part in layout reviews to learn and share best practice.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR
Must-have Technical skills:
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Microelectronics or a related field (recent graduates and those graduating within the next 6 months are welcome)
  • 0–2 years of experience in IC layout, including internships, placements or university projects
  • Solid understanding of CMOS device physics, semiconductor fabrication basics and analog circuit fundamentals
  • Awareness of key analog layout concepts such as matching, symmetry, parasitics, electromigration and latch-up
  • Hands-on exposure to a layout environment such as Cadence Virtuoso or Synopsys Custom Compiler (coursework or projects count)
  • Basic familiarity with physical verification (DRC/LVS), ideally with Pegasus
Nice-to-have:
  • Internship or project experience on a FinFET or other advanced-node technology (TSMC, Samsung, GlobalFoundries)
  • A completed tape-out from a university, MPW or internship project
  • Basic scripting experience (SKILL, TCL, Python or shell)
  • Comfort working in a Linux environment

Soft & Professional Skills:
  • Clear, structured communication in professional English—able to explain your work concisely
  • Collaborative and feedback-oriented mindset, open to learning from reviews
  • Strong attention to detail and pride in high-quality work
  • Ownership, reliability, and follow-through on commitments
  • Curious, self-motivated attitude, eager to learn and explore new tools or methods
  • High level of integrity and professionalism in representing the company and handling sensitive information.

OUR CULTURE
We’re a fully remote team of around 45 people distributed across the UK, Armenia, Italy, the US, Estonia, India, and beyond. We believe great talent is everywhere!
  • Our values are our north star: We Grow Together, We Win Together. Excellence Builds Relationships. Trust Is Our Currency. Results Matter, but People Create Them.
  • Connected, even remotely: We invest intentionally in staying connected through regular all-hands, 1:1s, technical reviews, and informal coffee chats, so collaboration feels natural and human despite the distance.
  • High ownership, real impact: Everyone contributes directly to customer-facing IP. Your work doesn't disappear into layers of management – it ships.
  • How we work: We move fast but thoughtfully, communicate openly, and balance autonomy with support. Technical decisions are debated openly and grounded in data, trade-offs, and first-principles thinking.

WHY JOIN US
  • Remote-first flexibility – work from anywhere, with flexible hours
  • Equipment & setup – we’ll provide the tools you need to succeed
  • High-impact projects – design real analog IP used in customer silicon
  • Supportive team culture – a dedicated manager and a team of colleagues ready to help
  • Competitive, transparent compensation– adjusted for your location and engagement model
  • Learning & growth – AI–DLP sessions, technical deep dives, and peer-led knowledge sharing that build both technical depth and system-level perspective

RECRUITMENT PROCESS
  1. Founder Call (30 min) – mutual introduction and interest alignment
  2. Technical Interview(90 min) – fundamentals, reasoning, and problem-solving
  3. Optional: Second Technical Interview (60 min) – another deep-dive into specific topics, which might include a presentation that we'll let you know about in advance
  4. HR & Culture Call (45 min)–values, collaboration style, and ways of working
  5. Offer & Next Steps– we send the offer and kick off the onboarding process.

Disclaimer: This is our standard process for most roles. For more senior, specialized, or higher-authority positions, we reserve the right to amend or tailor these steps as we see fit.

If you don’t meet every requirement but feel excited about the role, apply anyway. We value curiosity, integrity, and potential as much as experience.

US LBM is one of the leading and fastest growing distributors of specialty building materials in the United States, with a team of over 13,000 employees located throughout the country. Since our founding in 2009, we have acquired over 100 companies and have expanded to more than 450 locations serving 37 states. US LBM is a progressive organization that promotes a unique culture that focuses on the value of its customers and associates. Developing our people is critical to our strategy and fostering our culture of empowerment.

.

A Brief Overview

The US LBM Lead Software Engineer – Application Development (Pricing) will provide technical leadership while remaining hands-on in the design, development, and support of applications, APIs, and integrations supporting US LBM’s pricing operations.


This role focuses on technology used to manage and execute pricing across our wholesale and distribution business, including pricing engines, price management, customer-specific and contract pricing, discounting, quoting, margin management, and integrations with ERP, order management, sales, and customer-facing applications.


Working closely with Product Managers, Architects, Pricing, Sales, Finance, and business leaders, this individual will translate complex pricing requirements into scalable, reliable technology solutions.


The ideal candidate brings strong full-stack engineering experience, relevant pricing systems domain knowledge, and the ability to mentor engineers, guide technical decisions, and improve pricing accuracy, efficiency, and business performance.


What You Will Do

  • Design, develop, test, deploy, and support applications, APIs, and integrations supporting pricing, quoting, and commercial operations.
  • Remain hands-on in complex development while providing technical leadership, mentoring, code reviews, and engineering guidance.
  • Partner with Product Managers, Architects, Pricing, Sales, Finance, and business stakeholders to translate pricing needs into scalable solutions.
  • Apply domain expertise across pricing engines, price calculation, customer-specific and contract pricing, discounting, promotions, margin controls, quoting, and pricing optimization.
  • Lead technical design decisions to ensure applications are scalable, secure, reliable, and capable of supporting complex pricing environments.
  • Guide engineering delivery, managing technical priorities, risks, dependencies, and production readiness.
  • Establish reusable engineering patterns, APIs, integration standards, and CI/CD practices across pricing platforms.
  • Identify opportunities to improve pricing workflows through automation, AI, analytics, and modern application development.
  • Champion AI-assisted development practices, including specification-driven development, automated testing, and AI-supported code reviews.
  • Support integrations between pricing systems and ERP, order management, product/catalog, CRM, e-commerce, and third-party platforms.
  • Troubleshoot complex production issues involving pricing rules, calculations, data synchronization, integrations, and distributed systems while ensuring data accuracy.
  • Collaborate with business teams to understand pricing workflows and deliver measurable operational and commercial improvements.

Required For All Jobs

  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Comply with all company policies and standards.
  • Adhere to workplace safety requirements.

Education Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.


Experience Qualifications

  • 5+ years developing and delivering custom web, mobile, enterprise, or integration solutions.
  • 4+ years of full-stack software development experience.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership through mentoring, code reviews, architecture decisions, and delivery ownership.
  • Strong hands-on experience developing applications within Microsoft Azure.
  • Experience developing or supporting pricing engines, price management systems, pricing rules, quoting, discounting, contract pricing, margin management, or pricing optimization applications.
  • Experience with retail, wholesale, distribution, B2B pricing, CPQ solutions, or related enterprise pricing platforms strongly preferred.
  • Experience integrating pricing applications with ERP, order management, product/catalog, CRM, sales, or third-party systems.
  • Experience partnering with Product Managers, Architects, commercial leaders, and business stakeholders.
  • Experience with version control, automated testing, and CI/CD pipelines.

Skills and Abilities

  • Advanced proficiency developing applications and serverless REST APIs using C#/.NET within Microsoft Azure.
  • Strong experience with SQL, relational databases, and NoSQL databases.
  • Knowledge of API design, integrations, distributed systems, event-driven architecture, and modern application development.
  • Working knowledge of Infrastructure as Code and CI/CD tools, including Terraform, GitHub, and Azure DevOps.
  • Understanding of containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Strong understanding of pricing processes, including price calculations, pricing rules, contracts, discounts, rebates, margin controls, quoting, and pricing optimization.
  • Ability to integrate pricing technology with ERP, inventory, product/catalog, order management, CRM, and customer-facing systems.
  • Ability to communicate technical decisions, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to align engineering priorities with business objectives and measurable operational outcomes.
  • Experience with or interest in AI-assisted development and AI-first engineering practices.
  • Ability to balance hands-on engineering, technical leadership, delivery oversight, and stakeholder engagement.

Travel Expectations

Approximately 20%, depending on business needs.

Build your technology sales career with hands-on experience in a developing field, learning from experienced colleagues and engaging with organisations tackling real challenges in digital trust.

As an Account Manager, you will be responsible for developing sustainable and profitable customer relationships in the Italian market. You will manage existing accounts, identify new opportunities and connect customers with the right organic ingredients from our broad portfolio.

  • Representing DO IT Organic during customer visits and trade fairs in Italy and abroad.

You should be comfortable working independently while actively staying connected with colleagues. Some days will be filled with customer conversations and travel, while others require you to focus on follow-ups, administration and developing your pipeline. Ready to grow the Italian market with us? The sooner you apply, the sooner you can start contributing to our mission!

BeOne Medicines Global Research and Development Technology Solutions (GRDTS) team is seeking a motivated, enthusiastic, and experienced Digital & Technology Systems Director to join our Development Technology team. The director, Global Digital & Technology Systems will own the end-to-end system management life cycle of the portfolio of external systems and solutions used by the Global Clinical Operations (GCO) function at BeOne.

Essential Functions of the Job:

    • Implementation and delivery of systems/applications and projects that meet GCO business needs, including key initiatives to support GCO goals and objectives.

  • Liaise with computer system vendors, IT partners, audit, and compliance to coordinate system implementation and change activities.

  • Work within a framework and operating model that supports the current and future technology needs for GCO, that comprises requirements management, solutioning, build, implementation, and administration (run) of global Development platforms, master data, and system interfaces

GRDTS GCO Systems Management Team Leadership:

Team Leadership & Talent Development:

  • Lead, mentor, and manage a high-performing GCO Systems Management team focused on end-to-end system lifecycle management for all external GCO systems and platforms.

  • Foster a culture of innovation, accountability and drive professional development.

Operational Excellence, Compliance & Governance:

  • Ensure all systems and platforms adhere to relevant pharmaceutical industry regulations and internal security policies.

  • Liaise with vendors, Enterprise IT partners, audit, and compliance to coordinate system implementation and change activities

  • Ensure the team is trained in and embeds CSV, compliance, and health authority requirements into operational activities.

Collaboration & Partnership:

  • Collaborate with R&D functions and teams on standards and best practices to attain business goals

  • Engage with peers to define, sponsor, and execute continuous improvements.

Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience working on validated applications in a pharmaceutical or regulated environment, primarily clinical applications and/or systems management in a pharmaceutical or medical device industry especially in CTMS, eTMF, IRT, EDC, SSU management.

  • 8+ years of experience working in a GxP or regulated environment with a strong understanding of SLC methodology, 21CFR Part 11 and GAMP principles.

  • 5+ years of proven leadership at a senior level managing a team of direct reports and associate staff

  • Proven experience in overseeing the direction, planning, installation, implementation, and maintenance of software solutions especially in the SaaS/Hybrid cloud environment.

  • Good working knowledge of O365, active directory technology and schema, and SaaS to SaaS application integration framework.

  • Working knowledge of IaaS (Amazon Web Services, Azure) PaaS and SaaS architectures and technology options a plus.

  • Extensive experience in business and technical analysis, including developing requirements and translating them into data-driven and technical solutions

  • Strong expertise in data management practices, including data integrity, accuracy, and reliability

  • Significant experience delivering technical projects and managing multiple initiatives across diverse functions in a global environment

  • Ability to quickly learn and adapt to several technology areas, demonstrating a proactive approach to industry trends and innovations

Supervisory Responsibilities:

· Manage team members (employees and contingent workers) at global sites, including coaching and mentoring of staff with training and professional development.

· Must be an effective leader and communicator and considered to be a developer of people comfortable working with a broad cross-section of people in direct and matrixed relationships.

Key Capabilities

  • Strategic System Roadmap: Translating long-term clinical objectives into a multi-year system capability roadmap for external GCO systems.

  • Clinical & Technical Translation: Fluency in "clinical domain speak" related to GCO to accurately translate complex clinical workflows into structural, technical system and data requirements.

  • Stakeholder Orchestration & Influence: Navigating a matrixed environment to align with various clinical functions, internal IT groups, and external vendors around external systems standards.

  • Solution Lifecycle Oversight: Managing the end-to-end delivery of digital & technology systems & solutions—from initial scoping and vendor selection through deployment and value realization.

Key Competencies

  • Pharma Industry R&D Domain Literacy: Understanding of the pharmaceutical research and development value chain, mainly for the Clinical Operations function.

  • AI & Data Literacy: Comprehensive understanding of how AI solutions integrate within external systems and platforms, including knowledge of machine learning lifecycles, foundational models, and the requirements for "AI-ready data" to ensure effective clinical systems implementations and management.

Key Deliverables

  • GCO function Data, Digital, & Technology Roadmap for external systems: Short-term and long-term strategic blueprint mapping technology solutions directly to clinical capability milestones.

  • Business Capability Maps: Visual matrices mapping out current-state vs. future-state technical capabilities across GCO, and relationships to other functions.
