description:
Job Description Summary

The Technical Support Engineer 2 (TSE II) drives customer satisfaction through Service Excellence by providing advanced technical support, implementation leadership, project participation, and expert consultation for Digital Central Monitoring Unit (Digital CMU) solutions. This role partners with internal project teams and customer stakeholders to support implementations, upgrades, migrations, and other project activities, ensuring the successful deployment, adoption, and ongoing support of Digital CMU products and services.

As a senior technical resource, the TSE II provides guidance and support to remote and onsite Field Engineers (FEs), Client Service Technicians (CSTs), customer technical support personnel, clinical staff, peers, and customers experiencing system performance issues. The position serves as a primary escalation point for service-related issues involving Digital CMU software, hardware, networking, infrastructure, and integration components.

The TSE II participates in a shared 24x7x365 support model, delivering expert software, hardware, and network troubleshooting, incident management, and technical consultation. During ongoing customer support, the role collaborates closely with customer technical teams, clinical personnel, GE HealthCare resources, and Field Engineers to resolve complex issues, optimize system performance, support customer operations, and drive long-term customer success.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Advanced Technical Support & Incident Management

  • Provide advanced remote technical support for GE HealthCare software solutions and customer hardware environments, including coaching customers and field teams on contributing factors such as antivirus software, Cisco networking, Citrix, Microsoft technologies, and third-party infrastructure.
  • Lead customer escalation meetings, define logical engagement plans, and drive timely issue resolution using appropriate escalation processes.
  • Apply advanced diagnostic methods and remote support tools to reduce case resolution times and improve Time to Repair (TTR).
  • Serve as a recognized technical expert for complex customer issues involving software, hardware, networking, cloud, virtualization, and integration technologies.

Project Support & Implementations

  • Provide technical leadership and support for customer implementations, upgrades, migrations, system expansions, and related project activities.
  • Participate in project planning, technical reviews, testing, validation, and go-live support.
  • Collaborate with project managers, implementation teams, field resources, and customer stakeholders to ensure successful project execution.
  • Identify, communicate, and help mitigate technical risks that may impact project timelines, system performance, or customer outcomes.
  • Provide onsite support as needed during customer implementations, upgrades, migrations, and go-live activities throughout the United States and Canada.

Escalations, Quality & Productivity

  • Serve as the senior technical resource for service-related escalations and coordinate corrective action plans with customers, leadership, and cross-functional teams.
  • Champion productivity initiatives and serve as a change agent for product serviceability, reliability, quality improvement, trend analysis, and new product introduction (NPI) activities.
  • Identify, lead, and implement process improvements, troubleshooting enhancements, and business process initiatives that improve service delivery and organizational effectiveness.
  • Analyze recurring issues and quality trends and work with engineering and product teams to develop corrective actions.

Knowledge Management & Tools

  • Develop, approve, and publish Knowledge Management (KM) content to expand technical solutions available to Field Engineers and Technical Support Engineers.
  • Contribute ideas and participate in continuous improvement initiatives designed to enhance productivity tools, service readiness, and support effectiveness.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of GE HealthCare products, service processes, and diagnostic tools to maintain subject matter expertise and trusted advisor status.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & New Product Support

  • Partner with Service Engineering, Product Engineering, Development, Quality, and onsite engineering teams to improve product quality, serviceability, and escalation resolution.
  • Provide valuable input into new product development, service readiness activities, diagnostic tools, feature enhancements, and overall product quality.
  • Represent Technical Support during design reviews, service readiness activities, and product lifecycle initiatives as required.

Training & Mentorship

  • Coach and mentor TSE I team members, onsite engineers, and peers to ensure technical and customer-facing skills meet business needs.
  • Frequently serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for GE HealthCare software applications, technologies, and support processes.

Director, Digital Engagement

College Board - Operations

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team

College Board's Operations division is a best-in-class digital assessment delivery and customer engagement function that supports millions of students and thousands of test centers, annually. The Operations team is also leading exciting work to advance user experience using innovative solutions, products, and technology to enhance the end-to-end delivery of digital assessments and all aspects of customer support. Within Operations, the Assessment Delivery Operations (ADO) team is responsible for the successful execution of digital assessments like the SAT and Advanced Placement (AP) examinations, working closely with partners across College Board, the education sector, and beyond to improve testing technologies, customer experience, and outcomes. ADO’s User Readiness team ensures every district-level member, school-level educator, and test taker has what they need, and takes the critical actions required, to succeed on test day. This is done through multi-channel community engagement, effective digital communications, curated technical guidance, and risk-based outreach.

About the Opportunity

As the Director of Digital Engagement, you will own the full lifecycle of seasonal User Readiness campaigns and communications that reach thousands of coordinators, staff, and students across every College Board program. You’ll design and execute the strategy for how we communicate to our users, i.e., who needs to hear what, and when, then run the experiments and dig into user behavior to figure out what actually drives people to act and scale what works.

Not every educator or student needs to hear the same thing, the same way. You will help define the segments and personas that capture those differences and own the communication strategy built on top of them, translating a deep understanding of program policy, and the latest system and technology content, into messaging that surfaces what each user most needs to know and is delivered in the way that’s most likely to reach them. You will partner across College Board functional teams to get that translation right and connect every campaign directly to the User Readiness outcomes we’re driving toward for test day.

In this role, you will:

Seasonal Campaign Strategy & Lifecycle (30%)

  • Own the full lifecycle of seasonal User Readiness campaigns, from planning through execution and post-season retrospective
  • Set the cadence and sequencing of communications against program milestones, deciding who needs to hear what, and when
  • Build and maintain the campaign calendar that keeps every message landing at the right moment in a user’s readiness journey

Segmentation & Messaging Craft (25%)

  • Design and maintain audience segmentation based on coordinator type, program, and readiness stage, and refine segments over time with analytics partners
  • Translate program policy and the latest system and technology updates into messaging that surfaces what each user most needs to know
  • Own message quality end to end, from clarity and tone to the specific call to action and resources each segment needs
  • Write, build, test, and deploy email campaigns and automated journeys in Salesforce Marketing Cloud
  • Pilot AI tools to speed up drafting, personalization, and quality checks of content

Experimentation, Insights, and Partnership Outcomes (45%)

  • Design and run experiments and dig into user behavior to find what drives engagement and action. Examples include testing subject lines, timing, content, and channel
  • Define and track engagement metrics, from opens and clicks to completion of target actions, and report results and recommendations to stakeholders
  • Connect every campaign directly to the User Readiness outcomes we’re driving toward on test day, using engagement as a signal, not the goal itself
  • Partner across College Board functional teams to align messaging and ensure campaigns reflect the latest program, policy, and technology updates
  • Share audience insights with partner teams in community engagement, technical readiness, and proactive outreach to improve their work and reduce the need for intervention
  • Build relationships across teams that let you move quickly when a message needs to be revised or a new campaign needs to launch

About You

  • Expertise in lifecycle, CRM, or digital communications, with 5-7 years of experience planning and delivering multi-channel campaigns to large, segmented audiences
  • Hands-on experience building and deploying campaigns in an email marketing platform, with Salesforce Marketing Cloud experience preferred
  • Experience designing audience segmentation and personalization, using data to decide who receives which message and when
  • A track record of running experiments, analyzing engagement data, and turning results into measurable improvements
  • Strong writing and editing skills, including turning complex operational, policy, or technical information into clear, actionable messages
  • Experience with SMS and in-app messaging, including best practices for deliverability and message compliance
  • Experience managing a high volume of requests across many stakeholders, with familiarity with Jira or similar work-tracking tools
  • Preferred: Experience communicating with educators or school-based audiences
  • A bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • The ability to travel 4-6 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, a performance exercise relevant to the role, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $80,000–$130,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Torsh Inc. is an education technology company that produces a suite of coaching and professional development support products, including Torsh TALENT, a cloud-based coaching and professional learning platform through which all of the disparate elements of coaching can be organized, tracked, implemented, and managed and SESEBA powered by Torsh, a research based and evidence-backed coaching model that supports educators who teach Dual Language Learners in grades pre-K through 3. Our core mission is to improve student outcomes by increasing educator effectiveness, and we do this by helping schools and organizations increase educator instructional capacity, improve the delivery of educator professional development, and generate insights into educator effectiveness.

As Director of Customer Success, you'll lead and develop a team that helps customers realize the full value of TORSH's solutions. You'll play a critical role in driving customer retention, renewals, account growth, and overall customer satisfaction.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for someone who enjoys both the people and operational sides of Customer Success. You'll coach and support your team, strengthen customer engagement strategies, improve processes, and use data to make informed decisions.

Working closely with Business Development, Product, Engineering, and Marketing, you'll help shape how we deliver a consistent, high-quality customer experience as TORSH continues to grow.

What You'll Do

Lead, Coach, and Develop Your Team

  • Lead and mentor Customer Success Managers and Customer Enablement Managers, fostering accountability, collaboration, and continuous development.
  • Establish clear goals, performance expectations, and consistent coaching practices that help team members succeed.
  • Support team development, hiring, onboarding, and workforce planning.
  • Identify opportunities to improve team effectiveness, workload distribution, and customer coverage.

Drive Customer Retention and Growth

  • Own the overall strategy and performance of customer renewals, retention, and expansion opportunities.
  • Develop accurate renewal and growth forecasts, identify risks early, and implement proactive customer retention strategies.
  • Partner with Customer Success Managers to strengthen account planning, customer engagement, and renewal readiness.
  • Monitor account health and portfolio performance, using data to identify trends, opportunities, and areas requiring attention.

Build Scalable Customer Success Practices

  • Develop and improve Customer Success processes, playbooks, and operating standards.
  • Strengthen customer onboarding, account transitions, executive business reviews, and escalation management.
  • Design customer engagement approaches that balance personalized support with scalable service delivery.
  • Maintain accurate customer information, renewal forecasts, and account activity within our CRM.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, and the overall customer experience.

Build Strong Customer and Cross-Functional Partnerships

  • Serve as an executive-level partner for strategic, high-value, and at-risk customers.
  • Build trusted relationships with customer leaders, helping them connect TORSH's solutions to their organizational goals.
  • Collaborate with Business Development, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to address customer challenges and improve customer outcomes.
  • Represent customer needs internally and help prioritize improvements that support retention and long-term growth.
  • Provide leadership with meaningful insights into customer performance, revenue opportunities, and business risks.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in Customer Success, account management, or implementation within a SaaS environment.
  • 3+ years of experience managing, coaching, and developing customer-facing teams.
  • Demonstrated success improving customer retention, renewals, account growth, and overall portfolio performance.
  • Strong understanding of Customer Success operations, including account health monitoring, renewal forecasting, customer lifecycle management, and escalation processes.
  • Experience developing scalable Customer Success strategies and service models across different customer segments.
  • Proven ability to build relationships with senior and executive-level customer stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical skills, including experience using CRM data, reporting, and customer performance metrics to guide decisions.
  • Excellent communication, problem-solving, and leadership skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across Sales, Product, Engineering, and other business functions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in EdTech, K–12 education, early childhood education, or education-focused SaaS.
  • Experience with HubSpot or similar CRM platforms.
  • Familiarity with Gong or other conversation intelligence tools.
  • Experience leading customer success operations in a growing SaaS organization.
  • Experience developing tiered customer engagement models, including high-touch, mid-touch, and technology-enabled support.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base Salary: $110,000 annually
  • On-Target Earnings (OTE): $130,000, including performance-based incentives
  • Competitive employee benefits package
  • Paid time off and company holidays
  • Fully remote work environment
  • Professional development opportunities

Join Our Team

If you're a Customer Success leader who enjoys developing people, solving complex challenges, and building strong customer partnerships, we'd like to hear from you.

Join TORSH and help us strengthen the customer experience while supporting educators and organizations in achieving meaningful outcomes.

Principal, Global Capability Strategy & Planning

This role partners with the executive sponsor and key stakeholders to shape, evaluate, and operationalize the Blackbaud India workforce strategy spanning the Product and Enterprise Technology Groups. The role drives strategic analysis, stakeholder engagement, and transition planning, translating direction into structured transition roadmaps, governance, and enablement materials across annual and quarterly planning cycles.

Acting as a central point of orchestration across Talent Acquisition, HR, Finance, and Technology leadership, this role ensures workforce plans are executable with rigor and confidentiality across a complex, global stakeholder set – providing leadership‑ready insights into how strategy translates into effective hiring, operational efficiency and delivery impact. Success requires comfort operating across organizational boundaries, facilitating complex discussions, and bringing clarity, discipline, and coherence to a highly distributed, multi‑year transition effort.


What you’ll do:

  • Enable Blackbaud India workforce strategyby partnering with the executive sponsor and stakeholders across Product and Enterprise Technology Groups to model strategic scenarios and tradeoffs (e.g., capacity, cost, timing, risk) and translating that strategic direction into multi‑year transition roadmaps that drive accountability across annual and quarterly planning cycles.
  • Leverage AI to accelerate workforce modeling, forecasting, and reporting, and actively experiment with emerging capabilities as they evolve to improve the speed and quality of insights.
  • Track progress against plans using agreed measures (e.g., hiring velocity, attrition, onboarding effectiveness, and transition readiness), surfacing risks and mitigation actions and translating insights into clear, decision‑supporting updates.
  • Serve as a trusted point of contact for leaders and teams, answering questions and providing clarity on how strategy translates into execution while acting as the central point of orchestration for transition‑related risks, issues, escalations, and decision support.
  • Lead operating forums and program communications to ensure consistent information flow, clear expectations, and disciplined status tracking – tailoring messages on strategy, plans, progress, and risk for audiences at all levels.
  • Partner with Finance to support workforce budgeting and quarterly forecasting, tracking progress against plan and monitoring budget‑to‑actuals to surface variances, risks, and implications for decision‑making.
  • Serve as the source of truth for how workforce plans translate into approved positions and hiring pipelines, partnering with Talent Acquisition, Finance, and technology leaders to enable hiring execution, onboarding readiness, and training enablement, and coordinating globally to keep execution aligned and predictable.
  • Manage hiring operations with discipline and continuous improvement, including requisition intake, position reviews, and reconciliation across planning and tracking mechanisms, while identifying opportunities to improve scale, quality, and time‑to‑productivity as plans evolve.
  • Maintain confidentiality of workforce planning activities by enforcing disclosure processes and information‑sharing boundaries so sensitive materials are accessible only to approved participants.
  • Define, document, and continuously refine workforce planning, hiring, and operating processes for Blackbaud India, including approval flows, governance, hiring/backfill models, and tracking, and identify where broader enterprise business processes must adapt to support the evolving global operating model.

What we’ll want you to have:

  • 8+ years of experience in workforce planning, transformation, or complex program leadership, preferably in a modern SaaS or product‑led technology organization
  • Demonstrated experience supporting multi‑year, cross‑organizational initiatives, with a strong track record of orchestrating cross‑functional work and partnering effectively without direct authority.
  • Proven ability to partner with senior leaders as a trusted thought partner, contributing analysis, challenging assumptions, and translating strategy into executable plans
  • Strong ability to communicate strategic intent and influence decisions, bridging complex workforce, operating‑model, and financial considerations with business priorities for stakeholders at all levels
  • Proven ability to manage confidential, high-sensitivity planning initiatives

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

Creation Technologies is a leading global electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider. Our 14 business units span across four countries and many customers. We are seeking a highly experienced and strategic Senior EDI Architect to join our team.

In this role, you will be the primary technical authority for our Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) strategy and infrastructure. You will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing robust data exchange solutions that connect Creation Technologies with our global customer and vendor base. This role requires a deep technical mastery of EDI platforms, specifically Oracle and Cleo, alongside a strong understanding of supply chain business processes. The successful candidate will lead the architectural vision for our B2B integrations, ensuring scalability, security, and seamless data flow across our enterprise ecosystem.

Responsibilities

  • Define and maintain EDI communications & design, ensuring the architecture supports global scalability and high availability across all business units.
  • Lead the end-to-end design and deployment of complex EDI integrations using Oracle EDI modules, Oracle integration cloud (OIC) and Cleo Integration Cloud (CIC).
  • Manage and optimize communication protocols (AS2, SFTP, HTTPS, API) and oversee the onboarding of new trading partners (customers and suppliers).
  • Collaborate with IT developers and ERP specialists to integrate EDI workflows with ERPs like Oracle, ensuring data integrity across the transactions.
  • Oversee the creation and maintenance of complex EDI maps (X12, EDIFACT) and translation rules to meet diverse partner requirements.
  • Conduct thorough analysis of existing EDI processes to identify latencies or manual touchpoints, implementing automated solutions to improve operational efficiency.
  • Lead the development of comprehensive test plans and coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for all new partner integrations or system upgrades.
  • Provide Tier 3 technical support for EDI failures and mentor junior analysts/developers on EDI best practices and standards.

Personal Characteristics

  • Exceptional ability to troubleshoot complex integration failures and design long-term architectural fixes rather than temporary patches.
  • Advanced ability to translate technical EDI concepts into business language for stakeholders and executives.
  • Proven track record of building trusting relationships with cross-functional teams, including Supply Chain, Finance, and IT.
  • Ability to work with a high degree of accuracy, specifically regarding data mapping and compliance with global messaging standards.
  • Self-motivated individual who thrives on autonomy and takes ownership of the entire B2B integration lifecycle.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced EMS environment with shifting priorities and diverse customer requirements.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, or equivalent experience in related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in EDI architecture and development.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with either Oracle EDI/E-Business Suite and Cleo (CIC) is required, experience with both is preferred.
  • Deep knowledge of EDI standards (ANSI X12, EDIFACT) and communication protocols (AS2, FTP/S, API).
  • Prior experience in the EMS (Electronics Manufacturing Services) or High-Tech Manufacturing industry is a must.
  • Strong grasp of supply chain business processes, including Demand Planning, Manufacturing Operations, and Intercompany transactions.
  • Familiarity with SQL, XML, and JSON; experience with ERP-integrated EDI is essential.
  • Understanding of secure data transmission standards and B2B security best practices.

In accordance with pay transparency regulations, the anticipated starting salary for this position ranges from $90k-$120k CAD|USD annually. Full-time employees are also eligible for performance-based bonuses and a range of benefits. Please note that this salary range is not guaranteed, and the final offer may vary based on experience, education, location, and shift. Additionally, the benefits and programs available may differ depending on the hire date, schedule type, and hours worked.


If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

    - RF spectrum analysis, e.g. CRFS

    - Land Mobile Radio technologies (TETRA, APCO P25, DMR)

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

  • You are a team player: At Samsara, sales is a team sport. We help each other out by sharing best practices and focus on winning as a team.

Click here to learn about what we value at Samsara.

In this role you will:

  • Develop Executive-Level relationships within your territory
  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
  • Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales process in complex sales campaigns
  • Strategically outbound prospect
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Minimum of 2+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Experience selling full-cycle sales into complex environments (preferably within Public Sector - Local Gov, K-12, High Education)
  • Must have a strong track record of overachievement to quota
  • Cold calling, generating outreach, building relationships excites you
  • Solid understanding of SFDC and accurate forecasting methodology
  • Must be able to travel up to twice per quarter for onsites

  • Awards for top achievement (President’s club, Winner’s circle, Top 10%)

  • Passion in closing large, complex deals

$152,000—$190,000 USD

We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

  • Own the commercial partnership lifecycle end to end for Revenue Accounting
  • Establish an end-to-end framework for evaluating, structuring, approving, contracting, launching, operating, and closing partnership arrangements for Revenue Accounting.
  • Collaborate with Partnerships, Commercial, Product, and Legal teams to define requirements, design processes, and test new GTM solutions that support forward-looking deal roadmaps and scalable accounting, operational, financial, and control outcomes.
  • Define clear stage gates, ownership models, approval requirements, and handoffs from deal concept through contract execution and operational delivery.
  • Create visibility into the partnership pipeline, including upcoming launches, key obligations, revenue implications, operational dependencies, and close requirements.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to leadership on accounting considerations, operational readiness, and execution risk impacting accounting and financial statement completeness and accuracy.
  • Drive standard contract terms and commercial guardrails for Revenue Accounting
  • Partner with Legal and Partnerships to develop standard contract terms, fallback positions, approval thresholds, and playbooks for recurring partnership structures.
  • Review and advise on provisions, as they impact Revenue Accounting, related to pricing, discounts, fees, minimum commitments, incentives, services, usage, data, fulfillment, returns, termination, settlement, and other commercial obligations.
  • Translate accounting and operational requirements into contract language that is clear, enforceable, and scalable.
  • Identify when a proposed arrangement falls outside standard terms and lead the cross-functional assessment, escalation, and documentation of exceptions for Revenue Accounting.
  • Build a library of standard deal structures, accounting conclusions, operational requirements, and lessons learned for Revenue Accounting.
  • Build scalable operational rails to support Revenue Accounting
  • Support the Revenue Accounting requirements in the establishment in repeatable operating models with Partnerships, Revenue Operations, Order-to-Cash, Product, and other process owners for partner onboarding, order flow, billing, invoicing, collections, cash application, settlements, reporting, customer eligibility, fulfillment, and issue resolution.
  • Define operational requirements and controls for new partnership models, including ownership, data inputs, system workflows, reconciliations, exception handling, and reporting impacting Revenue Accounting.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Commercial teams to design more standardized solutions rather than one-off processes.
  • Help prioritize system, data, and process improvements that reduce manual work, improve control quality, and accelerate partnership launches.
  • For Accounting establish launch-readiness criteria and post-launch monitoring to ensure the operational model performs as designed.
  • Lead technical review of Commercial Partnership Contracts for Revenue Accounting
  • Provide revenue accounting requirements and guidance to Product, Commercial, Partnerships, and Legal teams during deal ideation and contract drafting.
  • Analyze complex partnership arrangements under ASC 606, including identifying contracts with customers, performance obligations, transaction price, variable consideration, principal-versus-agent considerations, contract modifications, and timing of revenue recognition as applicable.
  • Partner with Revenue Technical Accounting team to prepare or oversee technical accounting analyses, conclusions, and documentation for new and non-standard arrangements.
  • Partner with Revenue Accounting peers to ensure consistent application of policy across partnership structures and alignment with broader revenue processes.
  • Own the accounting setup and ongoing accounting execution for assigned partnerships, including the preparation and review of journal entries, reconciliations, schedules, and supporting documentation.
  • Support month-end and quarter-end close, including identifying close dependencies, resolving exceptions, and ensuring partnership activity is recorded completely and accurately.

  • Work closely with FP&A on support for overall Finance deal approval.

  • CPA or equivalent professional qualification.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field.
  • Strong knowledge of ASC 606 and experience applying revenue recognition principles to complex or non-standard commercial arrangements.
  • Experience working across the full lifecycle of commercial partnerships, contracts, or other complex commercial programs—from structuring and drafting through operational execution and financial close.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate commercial objectives into practical contract terms, accounting conclusions, system requirements, operational processes, and controls.
  • Experience preparing, reviewing, or owning journal entries, reconciliations, close activities, and audit support.
  • Strong understanding of cross-functional order-to-cash processes, including billing, collections, cash application, settlements, and reporting.
  • Experience partnering with Legal, Partnerships, Product, FP&A, Revenue Operations, and senior business leaders.
  • Strong project leadership skills, with the ability to establish structure and drive complex work across teams without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical accounting and operational topics to executive and non-finance audiences.
  • High attention to detail, sound judgment, and a bias toward building scalable, standardized solutions.

  • Experience with strategic partnerships, channel programs, bundled offerings, platform arrangements, or other multi-party commercial models.

SET : Strategy, Execution, Talent (for managers)

As a Sales Engineer at Samsara, you’d be an integral part of a diverse team working to help modernize essential industries through the application of cutting edge IoT solutions. Your work would directly contribute to a cleaner, more efficient and productive supply chain by creating safer roadways, reducing fuel consumption and emissions, and providing a consolidated platform for connecting operations. You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

  • You build genuine relationships with your customers: The industries we serve have relied on pen-and-paper solutions for years and haven’t been met with the type of technology we offer. Our customer's value earned trust and human relationships built over time.

description:
A Contently Managing Editor is responsible for supervising and coordinating a team of freelance journalists to manage the timely delivery of quality content for client projects. The Managing Editor provides updates to the Account Manager as a freelance editor assigned to projects w/ monthly, weekly, or daily assignments. The Managing Editor is responsible for maintaining strict quality and style standards; managing assignments and the editorial calendar; and coordinating communication between the Clients (Publishers) and writers.

Contently maintains strict quality standards and relies on the Managing Editor to control the quality of content, request revisions from freelance journalists and make staff changes when required. As such, the Managing Editors success is judged primarily on the quality of the content.

The position is freelance, performed remotely, typically range from 5 hours to 20 hours per week. Pay is competitive.

Contently Managing Editor tasks include

  • Bring big ideas to the table

  • Help the clients and journalists generate new pitches

  • Assign articles

  • Prepare, rewrite and edit copy to improve readability

  • Detect and correct errors in spelling, punctuation, and syntax

  • Verify facts, dates, and statistics, using standard reference sources

  • Ensure compliance to the publication's style, editorial policy, and publishing requirements

  • File brief stories and blog posts when necessary

Contently Managing Editors should have experience hiring and managing freelance journalists; assigning news and feature articles for a monthly, weekly, or daily publication; fact checking and editing news copy; editing for publication style.

The position is freelance, performed remotely, and can range from 4 hours to 20 hours per week. Pay is competitive.

If interested, apply online at Contently.com/jobs.

About Contently

Contently ( a venture-backed startup in New York City, empowers brands and journalists to connect and tell stories. Our solution combines the largest network of vetted, ready-to-work journalists with a workflow platform designed to help brands more efficiently manage their content programs. Clients currently include some of the world's largest brands, agencies and media companies.

description:
Build and scale the data infrastructure for a fast-growing, profitable health-tech company. In this role, you will design the robust pipelines, storage architectures, and data models that ensure our datasets are accurate, secure, and ready to drive critical decisions helping millions of insured Americans access their medications.

We are hiring a Senior Data Engineer to own the evolution of the data platform. You will be responsible for moving our client toward modern data engineering standards—structuring our warehouse, enforcing clean data modeling practices, and managing our infrastructure via code.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and implement scalable data models in Snowflake utilizing modern frameworks like the Medallion Architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold layers).

  • Build, maintain, and optimize robust data transformation pipelines using dbt.

  • Provision, manage, and scale cloud infrastructure securely using Terraform.

  • Develop high-quality data ingestion and orchestration pipelines using Python and Openflow (Apache NiFi) within an AWS environment.

  • Enforce software engineering best practices with Git (GitHub/Bitbucket) and manage secure access controls via Microsoft Entra.

Must-Have Experience & Skills

  • Deep experience writing, testing, and documenting complex dbt models.

  • Experience configuring, querying, and optimizing Snowflake data warehouses.

  • Strong conceptual understanding and practical application of data warehouse modeling (e.g., Kimball, Medallion Architecture).

  • Strong Python skills specifically tailored for data manipulation, scripting, and pipeline creation.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS cloud services and managing infrastructure via Terraform.

  • Professional experience using Git (Github or Bitbucket).

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with Openflow / Apache NiFi for data flow orchestration.

  • Familiarity with identity and access management using Microsoft Entra ID.

  • Experience with Sigma Computing for business intelligence and data visualization.

Job Description:

GDIT has been supporting the Indian Health Service (IHS) mission for 20+ years; working with the agency to provide integral services to raise health access and availability to 2.6 million American Indians and Alaska Natives.


You'll be part of modernizing the EHR platform to enable better data access, patient experience, and quality of care for 567 tribes, 37 states and over 600 medical facilities.


As a Major Incident Manager supporting the IHS Electronic Health Records Modernization (EHRM) program, you will be responsible for leading Major Issue Management and supporting triage, incident, problem, and change management activities within the Sustainment Operations Incident and Delivery pillar.


***The shift hours for this role are 7:00PM-7:00AM with:


5 days off, 5 days working, or:

4 days off, 5 days working, or:

5 days off, 4 days working.

HOW A MAJOR INCIDENT MANAGER WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:

  • Play a critical role in maintaining the stability, availability, and usability of the PATH (Oracle Cerner Millennium) environment by leading the response to high-severity incidents and coordinating major issue resolution.
  • Ensuring timely, well-coordinated incident management, reduce downtime, protect data integrity, and help clinicians and staff focus on delivering safe, high-quality patient care.
  • May be required to work non-standard hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, as directed by management and based on client needs and incident response requirements.
  • Provide 24/7 coordination for major incidents (SEV1–SEV3) affecting critical systems such as EMR, clinical workflows, financial systems, and imaging platforms.
  • Assess incident criticality at engagement and throughout the lifecycle; oversee monitoring, prioritization, escalation, and resolution against defined SLAs.
  • Engage and coordinate cross-functional technical resources as necessary, ensuring all steps and activities required for escalation are executed efficiently.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for major incidents, providing timely, professional communication to clients, internal stakeholders, and executive leadership.
  • Ensure accurate, comprehensive documentation in ServiceNow, including Service Requests, Incident Reports, and associated Change Requests, capturing timelines, actions, and outcomes.
  • Lead root cause analysis efforts, document findings and corrective actions across vendors, and deliver clear summaries to leadership.
  • Analyze incident data to identify trends and contribute to process improvement, problem management, and preventive strategies.
  • Support triage, incident management, problem management, and change management when not directly engaged in a major incident, helping to strengthen reliability and resiliency.
  • Mentor team members, support incident response drills, and maintain operational readiness for potential outage.
  • Help strengthen customer trust, support contract performance, and enable mission success across the healthcare environment.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in incident management, preferably in healthcare IT or large, complex IT environments.
  • Strong knowledge of ITIL practices (incident and problem management) and IT troubleshooting in mission-critical systems.
  • Experience with PATH (Oracle Cerner Millennium) or similar EHR platforms and enterprise incident management tools (ServiceNow; xMatters preferred).
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-team incident response and make effective decisions under high pressure.
  • Training/education/experience in task coordination and functional knowledge of IT project management concepts and tools.
  • Ability to participate in an on-call rotation and work irregular hours to support 24/7 operations.
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the year, if needed.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:


  • 5+ years of relevant incident management or operations leadership experience.
  • Experience supporting federal contract programs and working with government stakeholders.
  • Experience with healthcare systems and standards such as HL7, PACS, and EMR platforms.
  • Strong task and incident management skills, with excellent organizational and time management capabilities.
  • Ability to manage frequently changing priorities of competing importance in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to communicate and interact effectively with internal/external teams, including key stakeholders and customers.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and within tight deadlines, following detailed written policies, processes, procedures, and work instructions.
  • Ability to produce high-quality documentation (incident reports, root cause analyses, playbooks, and process documents) that contributes to the overall success of our program.

SECURITY CLEARANCE LEVEL:

  • This role requires you to obtain and maintain an in-depth Public Trust Level 5. This investigation will review personal and criminal behavior, financial conduct, foreign influence, as well as other adjudications.

GDIT IS YOUR PLACE:

  • Full-flex work week to own your priorities at work and at home.
  • 401K with company match.
  • Comprehensive health and wellness packages.
  • Internal mobility team dedicated to helping you own your career.
  • Professional growth opportunities including paid education and certifications.
  • Cutting-edge technology you can learn from.
  • Rest and recharge with paid vacation and holidays.

Job Description:

The Director, FP&A leads Confluent's corporate financial planning and analysis function and serves as a key financial partner to the Chief Financial Officer and Senior Leadership Team. This role owns the corporate FP&A calendar, including the annual budget, monthly forecast, and long-range planning processes, and is responsible for SG&A budgeting and centralized cost accounting across the organization. The Director, FP&A also leads Commercial Finance and pricing analysis, business intelligence and reporting, owns the Company's cash flow forecasting process, and leads financial due diligence and integration for M&A activity.


This position leads the corporate FP&A team and delivers value-added analysis, meaningful financial and operational metrics, and clear executive-level communication that supports insightful business decision-making.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


Corporate FP&A & Planning

  • Own the corporate FP&A calendar and operating rhythm, ensuring appropriate information is available for internal operating reviews and Senior Leadership/Board reporting.
  • Lead the Company's annual budget process, including budget guidance, timelines, tools, and templates, acting as project manager to ensure all business unit and corporate budgets are accurate, aligned, and reconcile in total.
  • Lead the monthly and 12-month rolling forecast process, coordinating across Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, and Commercial to deliver a cohesive, aligned company forecast.
  • Develop and monitor short-range (1-year) and long-range (3-5 year) strategic planning models in partnership with the CFO and Senior Leadership Team.
  • Prepare the monthly corporate reporting package, including consolidated financial statements, KPI reporting, variance analysis, and executive-level commentary.
  • Administer enterprise planning and consolidation tools, including Adaptive Planning and Epicor.

Business Intelligence & Reporting

  • Own the Company's business intelligence and reporting function, leveraging Power BI and Domo to build and maintain dashboards and self-service reporting for Finance, Operations, and Commercial stakeholders.
  • Establish data governance standards and consistent metric definitions across BI and reporting platforms to ensure a single source of truth for financial and operational data.
  • Partner with IT and business unit finance leaders to prioritize and deliver new reporting and analytics capabilities.

SG&A & Centralized Cost Accounting

  • Own budgeting, forecasting, and monthly reporting for SG&A and other centralized corporate cost centers.
  • Lead centralized cost accounting processes, ensuring consistent cost methodology and reporting standards are applied across the organization.
  • Own centralized LEAN capitalized labor and overhead accounting, ensuring consistent capitalization methodology and reporting across all business units.
  • Partner with department leaders across the organization to monitor spending against budget and identify cost management opportunities.

Commercial Finance & Pricing

  • Lead Commercial Finance support, partnering with Sales and Commercial leadership on quote analysis, customer profitability, revenue trends, and annual MSA price reviews
  • Own the Company's pricing analysis function, including price/cost bridges, margin analysis by product and customer, the Company's PSR and MPR processes, month-end price measurement, and income variance analysis.

Cash Flow Forecasting

  • Own the Company's cash flow forecasting process, partnering with Treasury, Controllership, and business unit finance leaders to deliver accurate short-term and long-term cash visibility.
  • Set free cash flow and working capital targets in partnership with business unit leadership and monitor performance against those targets.

M&A Diligence & Integration

  • Lead financial due diligence for M&A opportunities, including valuation models, synergy analysis, and evaluation of target company financials. Partner with CFO and Advisors on reporting, modeling, and analysis.
  • Lead financial integration planning and execution for completed acquisitions, coordinating with Operations, IT, Accounting, and business unit finance teams.
  • Lead post-acquisition synergy measurement and tracking, along with financial systems & costing integration for acquired businesses.
  • Provide financial modeling and analysis support for acquisitions, divestitures, new product development, and other ad hoc strategic projects.

Team & Stakeholder Leadership

  • Develop the FP&A team through effective recruiting, coaching, training, and performance management.
  • Partner with the CEO, COO, CFO, Corporate Controller, Director of Operations Finance, and other functions to provide value-added analysis, improve processes and tools, and eliminate redundancies.
  • Prepare Board and Senior Leadership materials.

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration, Accounting, or Finance required; MBA preferred.
  • 10+ years experience in FP&A or Operational Finance leadership roles. 10+ years of people management experience.

Parexel is a leading global clinical development partner delivering insights-driven clinical and consulting solutions to the life sciences industry. About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Salesforce Functional Analyst to join our team. As a Senior Salesforce Functional Analyst, you will turn business needs into Salesforce solutions that help our teams manage the client relationships, proposals, and contracts that make clinical research possible. This position plays a key role in requirements gathering, solution design, user acceptance testing, and process improvement, ensuring that every change serves the people who use it.


You will collaborate with project managers, developers, quality assurance teams, and business stakeholders, work within Agile methodologies, and contribute from initial requirements through implementation. Responsibilities include gathering and documenting requirements, designing Salesforce solutions, configuring declarative tools, supporting user acceptance testing, developing change management strategies, and continuously improving how we use Salesforce, with opportunities to deepen your expertise and influence outcomes.


You'll join a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment focused on making a meaningful impact through well-designed Salesforce solutions and clear, actionable requirements. With diverse teams and continuous learning opportunities, the Salesforce Business Analyst can explore career paths and expand skills across the Salesforce platform, Agile delivery, and the clinical research business.

Key Responsibilities

  • Requirements Gathering and Analysis: Conduct workshops and interviews with stakeholders to elicit and document detailed business requirements. Create user stories, acceptance criteria, and use cases to communicate requirements clearly to technical teams, and create Visio flows that document new and existing business processes and functionality
  • Solution Design: Collaborate with the team to develop comprehensive solution designs that leverage Salesforce capabilities to meet business objectives. Evaluate and recommend appropriate Salesforce features and third-party applications to enhance business processes
  • User Acceptance Testing (UAT) Support: Develop UAT plans and test scenarios, and support business stakeholders with test data creation, training, and demos. Analyze UAT results and work with development teams to address any issues
  • Salesforce Configuration: Administer a range of declarative solutions in support of sprint work and resolve production issues when needed. Implement and maintain Salesforce configurations that support business requirements
  • Process Improvement: Analyze current business processes and identify opportunities for optimization using Salesforce capabilities. Propose and design process improvements that increase efficiency and user adoption
  • Collaboration and Stakeholder Management: Work closely with project managers, developers, and quality assurance teams to align business needs with technical solutions. Facilitate communication between IT and business units, manage stakeholder expectations, and provide regular updates on project progress
  • Change Management: Develop and execute change management strategies that support smooth adoption of new Salesforce features and processes. Create training materials and conduct user training sessions as needed
  • Continuous Improvement: Stay current on the latest Salesforce releases and features, assessing their potential impact and benefits for the organization. Proactively suggest improvements to business processes and Salesforce utilization, and mentor junior team members in Salesforce business analysis practices and methodologies

You'll thrive in this role if you bring:

  • Strengths in business analysis, requirements gathering and documentation, and translating complex business needs into clear, actionable Salesforce solutions
  • A proven track record of providing exceptional customer service to stakeholders at all levels, including C-suite leaders, and managing production issues with meticulous attention to detail
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships and facilitate decisions across diverse stakeholder groups
  • Comfort working with Salesforce declarative tools, Agile methodologies, and tools such as Jira and Visio
  • A proactive mindset, a bias for action, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment while adapting readily to changing priorities

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree
  • Salesforce Administrator Certification
  • 5+ years of hands-on Salesforce experience with a strong focus on business analysis and solution design
  • Strong understanding of Salesforce architecture, data model, and business processes, and of the Salesforce security model and best practices
  • Understanding of the full sales cycle, from lead generation and request for proposal through the contract lifecycle
  • Demonstrated experience delivering Salesforce projects from conception to implementation
  • Ability to design and implement solutions using Salesforce declarative tools, such as Flow, Process Builder, Validation Rules, and Approval Processes
  • Experience with Salesforce Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, and other relevant Salesforce products
  • Understanding of Agile methodologies and experience working in Agile environments, including tools such as Jira
  • Proficiency in the Microsoft Office suite, especially Excel and Visio
  • Familiarity with API testing tools and techniques
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills
  • Ability to work in shifts from 5 PM to 2 AM or 6 PM to 3 AM IST and provide support on weekend releases

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in healthcare, clinical development, or a related field
  • Salesforce Certified Advanced Administrator, Salesforce Sales Cloud Consultant, or Salesforce Certified Business Analyst certification

We believe in flexibility, growth, and creating space for people to do their best work. Join us and be part of a team where your contributions help shape the future of clinical research.

  • Serve as the named operational risk enablement partner for regional business unit heads — maintaining a regular engagement cadence with each major regional business unit to understand needs, track progress, and resolve barriers — and build and maintain productive relationships with regional business leaders, local compliance teams, Internal Audit, and other key stakeholders across the first, second, and third lines of defense.

Software Engineering Team Manager

(USA)

About PSG-CP

Pearson is the world's lifelong learning company, and PSG-CP (Pearson Software Group - Content Platform) is the organization powering how that learning gets created, enriched, delivered, and measured. PSG-CP's focus is content. We handle authoring, semantic enrichment, transformation, delivery, assessment, and analytics, serving every Pearson line of business and millions of learners worldwide. We are reshaping the platform around AI in a serious way, and we are looking for a leader who wants to build that with us.

About the role

PSG-CP is in need of a leader who can help manage our global team of engineeers to help our lines of business receive the content they need to power their applications. The engineering team is embedded directly with our most strategic internal businesses and ship production AI applications against real problems. Running software, not decks or specs. As this practice grows, we need a founding leader to build and scale it.

This role leads four teams at the heart of the PSG-CP platform: Prizm, Semantics, Transformation, and Delivery Services. These are the groups that own how content is structured, semantically enriched, transformed, and delivered at global scale. Your job is to lead them forward while changing how they work: closer to the businesses they serve, faster from "we need something that does X" to "here, try this," and increasingly built around frontier AI.

You will hire and develop a strong group of engineers and set the technical and operational bar for engagements with lines of business, and build the playbooks that turn one-off wins into repeatable patterns.

This is a player-coach role with a strong bias toward leadership. You will stay close enough to the technical work to review architectures, debug production issues, and pair with your team when it matters, but your primary impact will come from the people you hire, the standards you set, and the culture you create. You will partner with Product, Architecture, and leaders across Pearson's lines of business to shape how the content platform evolves, and your team's field insights will directly influence platform direction.

Responsibilities

  • Set a high bar for technical talent, customer instincts, and AI-first engineering judgment.
  • Conduct regular 1:1s, provide technical mentorship, and invest in the career growth of each team member. Create an environment where strong engineers do the best work of their careers.
  • Staff and oversee engagements with lines of business across your team's portfolio, making resource allocation decisions that balance stakeholder needs, platform health, team development, and business priorities.
  • Own delivery across the Prizm, Semantics, Transformation, and Delivery Services roadmaps, keeping the core platform reliable, scaled, and moving.
  • Work with line-of-business leaders to qualify engagements, scope work, and set expectations before your team commits. Own the relationship through the lifecycle of the engagement, not just the kickoff.
  • Review technical architectures and code produced by your teams, ensuring they ship high-quality, production-ready solutions that meet enterprise expectations for reliability, observability, security, and cost.
  • Stay hands-on enough to lead technical discovery sessions, prototype solutions, and debug complex production issues alongside your team when needed.
  • Build repeatable playbooks, starter repositories, integration templates, and an internal knowledge base that captures what your team learns in the field. Route field-proven patterns back into the platform teams so wins compound instead of staying one-off.
  • Set and uphold a high standard for AI-augmented engineering practice. Coach the team on the effective, responsible use of agentic coding tools, and shape how AI fits into how this group designs, ships, and operates software.
  • Define team OKRs that tie to line-of-business outcomes and platform adoption goals. Create operational cadences (standups, retros, engagement reviews, design reviews, incident reviews) that keep the teams aligned, accountable, and continuously improving.
  • Partner with Product and Architecture to translate field insights into platform improvements. Serve as the voice of the internal customer in planning.
  • Represent the platform with senior stakeholders across lines of business at the highest level.

You may be a good fit if you have

  • 10+ years of experience in software engineering, solutions architecture, or a technical customer-facing role such as forward deployed engineering or consulting.
  • 4+ years of people management experience with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining strong engineers, ideally within a services, post-sales, or forward deployed organization.
  • Experience building teams or practices from 0 to 1, plus the judgment to do that inside an organization with real systems already in production.
  • Experience working directly with enterprise stakeholders on technical implementations, including comfort navigating complex organizational dynamics in a large company.
  • Real production experience building on large language models and generative AI: agents, retrieval, evaluation frameworks, prompt management, guardrails, and the harder operational realities of running AI in production (rate limits, non-determinism, provider outages, schema drift, cost and latency).
  • A genuine point of view on AI-first engineering. You use agentic coding tools daily, you have opinions on which tools work best for which tasks, and you have shaped team practice around responsible AI adoption.
  • Enough depth in distributed backend systems and cloud-native architectures (AWS, Azure, or GCP) to credibly review what your teams ship: services, async processing, event-driven pipelines, and content and data systems at scale.
  • Strong operational instincts around observability, on-call, incident response, security, and the kind of platform discipline that keeps services trustworthy at multi-tenant scale.
  • Executive presence and the ability to move between strategic conversations with senior stakeholders and hands-on debugging sessions with engineers without losing either audience.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You can translate technical complexity into clear narratives for different audiences.
  • Genuine excitement about building something new and defining what great looks like for a practice that doesn't yet exist.

Logistics

  • Minimum education: Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
  • Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Compensation at Pearson is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and specific location.

At Terrific, every role directly impacts how we grow from product to revenue to customer experience. We’re building the next generation of social commerce through live shopping powered by real-time data and AI.

And we believe customer data should belong to the brands who earn it — not third-party platforms.

Commerce Integrations Lead / Sales Engineer

LATAM · Full-time Contract · Remote
Product & Engineering · eCommerce · Integrations · AI

Integrations & Technical Solutions Lead

LATAM or EMEA · Full-time Contract · Remote
Product & Engineering · eCommerce · Integrations · AI

See something that should connect? Build it.
See a process that should exist? Create it.

At Terrific, we’re building the next generation of social commerce—helping brands turn content, creators, live experiences and AI into commerce they own.

Our technology brings shoppable video, live shopping, interactive timelines, polls and product carousels directly onto a merchant’s website or app.

Now we’re looking for an Commerce Integrations Lead/Sales Engineer to help us connect Terrific to the wider commerce ecosystem—and build the systems that make those connections faster every time.

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is not a role where you’ll inherit a finished playbook.

You’ll help write it.

You’ll work across Product, Engineering, Sales and Customer Success to solve the technical problems that determine whether a customer can launch, how quickly they see value and how easily we can support the next merchant.

One day, you may investigate how a global retailer’s cart works across multiple markets. The next, you may build a lightweight integration, help shape a live commercial opportunity, automate part of our technical-discovery process or prepare an app for a commerce marketplace.

You’ll work directly with teammates and customers across Latin America, Europe, Israel and the United States. You’ll have visibility into the full journey—from the first sales conversation through integration, launch and ongoing performance.

If you enjoy moving between technology, customers and commercial problems—and want the freedom to build rather than simply maintain—this role offers unusual room to make an impact.

WHAT YOU’LL BUILD

Terrific needs to connect with the platforms and tools merchants already use.

You’ll help us expand and improve integrations across:

  • Shopify

  • VTEX

  • Adobe Commerce/Magento

  • WooCommerce

  • Salesforce Commerce Cloud

  • BigCommerce

  • Tiendanube/Nuvemshop

  • Wix

  • PrestaShop

  • Shopware

  • Custom and headless commerce environments

  • Native mobile applications

You’ll also explore integrations with platforms such as Klaviyo, Attentive, Gorgias, Zendesk, Yotpo, Segment, Zapier, Google Merchant Center and Meta Commerce Manager.

Over time, you’ll help Terrific build a stronger marketplace presence, a more repeatable onboarding process and a technical integration layer that can scale across customers and markets.

WHAT YOU’LL OWN

  • Investigating merchant websites, applications and commerce stacks.

  • Understanding how product catalogs, variants, carts and checkout flows work.

  • Assessing technical feasibility for active commercial opportunities.

  • Turning customer requirements into clear technical recommendations.

  • Building, testing and improving integrations across major ecommerce platforms.

  • Helping merchants move from signed agreement to their first live Terrific experience.

  • Working directly with customer engineers and internal commercial teams.

  • Supporting technical discovery, proposals, security reviews and proofs of concept.

  • Improving the reliability of product feeds, event tracking, cart actions and embeds.

  • Publishing and maintaining Terrific apps across relevant commerce marketplaces.

  • Building tools, scripts, automations and AI agents that make integration work faster.

  • Turning repeated customer friction into clear Product and Engineering priorities.

  • Creating the documentation and processes that will support future customers and teammates.

You won’t be expected to solve everything alone. You will be expected to take ownership, bring the right people together and move the problem forward.

WHO YOU ARE

You’re technical, curious and commercially aware.

You want to understand why something matters to the customer—not only how it works in the code.

You’re comfortable opening DevTools, tracing an API request, reading someone else’s implementation and building a practical solution. You can move from a technical conversation with engineers to a commercial conversation with Sales or a customer without losing the thread.

You communicate clearly, ask good questions and know when to challenge an assumption.

You don’t need every process to be defined before you begin. You like taking something that is currently handled differently each time and turning it into a system the company can reuse.

You also understand that speed and judgment matter in a startup. Sometimes the right answer is a full integration. Sometimes it is a simpler path that gets the customer live this week.

HOW YOU’LL USE AI
