Success is not following a process perfectly.

Success is leaving us with a better process than the one you joined.

WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

Many technical integration roles begin with a ticket and end when the ticket is closed.

This one begins with a customer opportunity.

You’ll see how technical decisions affect sales, launch timelines, customer experience and revenue. You’ll work across teams and countries, with direct access to the people making product and commercial decisions.

Role:Pressure Vessel Engineer

Employment Type: Full-Time

Location: Remote (U.S.-based)

Becht is looking for an early to mid-career Pressure Vessel Engineer (PVE) who wants to take the next step in their technical career. We are a world-class, family-owned multidiscipline engineering firm serving the energy sector (refining, petrochemical, and power generation industries), providing expertise that spans both traditional and emerging technology.

Who is Becht?

Founded in 1964, Becht is a rapidly growing, family-owned multidiscipline engineering firm serving the energy sector (refining, petrochemical, midstream, and power generation industries). We combine deep technical expertise with practical execution to help clients operate safely, efficiently, and reliably.

Becht is a technical leader in pressure vessels, piping, structures, and materials and as such has a major role in international codes and standards, allowing a unique opportunity to both learn and contribute at an industry-wide level. We emphasize multidiscipline problem-solving and collaboration to solve the most challenging design and equipment reliability problems, and our unique network of over 1200 accomplished technical experts spanning all engineering disciplines provides even further opportunities for learning and growth.

All of Becht’s services revolve around our mission: To Help Our Clients Succeed.

Key Responsibilities

The PVE will be tasked with providing technical guidance for fixed equipment assets from a mechanical engineering perspective. The work will focus primarily on in-service pressure vessels and heat exchangers but may also include piping, tanks, or other associated equipment as the need arises. The PVE will be expected to manage projects from the proposal phase through project completion as the primary point of contact and primary technical resource. Alternately, they may also serve as a technical resource for larger, multidisciplinary projects. Some typical examples of daily project activities for this role are:

  • Perform rerate or alteration calculations.
  • Perform fitness for service assessments.
  • Create, review, or certify fixed equipment repair plans.
  • Evaluate bolted flange joints for troubleshooting leakage issues.

This opportunity is for the Mechanical Division within Becht, consisting of more than 40 full time team members. This position is offered as remote work with the need to travel up to 25%, which may include onsite turnaround support.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering or closely related discipline.
  • 5-20 years’ experience in a technical role in the refining, petrochemical or power generation industries with a focus on pressure equipment engineering. More senior candidates are welcome to apply as well.
  • Experience with rerates/alterations, repairs, fitness for service, bolted flange joints, and ASME Section VIII pressure equipment.
  • Experience with the application of industry codes and standards for pressure vessels such as ASME Section VIII, API 579, ASME PCC-1, ASME PCC-2, API 510, NBIC NB-23, etc.
  • Experience with field troubleshooting and system walk-downs and the ability to travel to customer sites.
  • Experience with turnaround support, planning, & execution.
  • Experience with the commercial software COMPRESS or PV Elite.
  • Strong grasp of engineering fundamentals and mechanics.
  • Self-motivated with strong interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills.
  • Capable of managing multiple projects and clients.

Qualifications that set you apart (but not required):

  • Professional Engineer licensure in at least one US state.
  • API certifications for 510, 570, 571, and/or 653.
  • Experience with ASME Section VIII, Division 2 design and construction.
  • Experience with advanced analysis such as ASME Section VIII, Division 2 Part 5 – Design by Analysis or Level 3 Fitness for Service assessments.
  • Experience with ABAQUS finite element analysis software.
  • Knowledge of other fixed equipment such as piping, tanks, and boilers.
  • Knowledge of refractory, relief valves, and NDE techniques.
  • Memberships or experience with industry codes and standards committees.

Build Your Career with Becht

A creative and innovative work environment isn’t all we have to offer! When you join Becht, you can expect:

  • A positive, collaborative workforce

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.

Here's what "end to end" actually means here.

You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.

You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.

You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

We're growing fast and we keep the bar high.

We believe the best media buyer today is a sharp marketer who uses AI every day. We built an internal creative analysis tool that connects to Claude, and we use Pipeboard to read and write to ad accounts and run heavy analysis. You don't need to know our stack yet. You do need to actually use AI in your work, not be afraid of it, and teach yourself what you don't know.

Requirements

What the job looks like

Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.

Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.

Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.

Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.

Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.

Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.

Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.

Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.

You're a fit if

You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.

You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.

You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.

You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.

You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.

You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.

Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.

You're not a fit if

  • "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.

Benefits

Why This Role Is Exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

We are currently looking for an 100% remote Funeral Sales Consultant to handle inbound inquiries from families and private individuals who need to arrange funeral services in the United Kingdom.

Your primary task is to guide clients through our comprehensive range of funeral services based on their specific needs, providing professional, warm, and comforting guidance during a difficult time.

Shaping the Future of Funeral Services

The UK funeral market has long been dominated by a traditional, conservative approach. However, our strength at Fenix lies in recognizing that the modern UK is beautiful, diverse, and fluid. Many of our clients do not fit the traditional British mold, and we are incredibly proud to serve them exactly as they are, respecting all cultures, beliefs, and personal wishes when planning a final farewell.

We are specifically seeking candidates with origins in, or significant professional experience from, the United Kingdom. You must be fluent in English and operate through your own limited company (Aktiebolag or equivalent), as you will be working as an independent contractor. Upon agreement, we will sign a consultancy agreement and an NDA.

Key Responsibilities

  • Inbound Funeral Consultation: Receive and handle inbound calls from individuals and families needing immediate or pre-planned funeral services.

  • Empathetic Advisory: Engage in respectful, advisory dialogues to tailor funeral arrangements, legal services, and memorial choices to the customer’s needs.

  • End-to-End Support: Ensure customers receive accurate information, transparent pricing, and emotional support throughout the entire funeral planning process.

  • Goal Alignment: Collaborate closely with the Fenix team to achieve established quality and sales goals.

Schedule & Scope

  • Start: Immediate.

  • Hours: Flexible. Because loss doesn't follow a schedule, our clients require assistance 24/7.

  • Training: Comprehensive digital training via our portal + 4 hours of live onboarding with a Fenix expert to get you fully acquainted with the funeral industry and our platform.

Compensation

  • Base Pay: An hourly consultancy fee of X SEK per hour.

  • Commission: Additional commission is paid at X SEK per completed and confirmed funeral order.

  • Invoicing: All payments are made via invoice from your limited company (excl. VAT).

Who Are You?

To thrive in this unique and meaningful role, you should meet the following criteria:

  • UK Background: You have your origins in the UK or extensive experience working within the British market, understanding its cultural nuances.

  • Language Skills: You are fluent in English (native level is highly meritorious) and possess native-level proficiency in Swedish (written and spoken).

  • Empathy & Sales Experience: Documented sales or advisory experience, preferably within insurance, banking, or other relationship-driven sectors. You know how to balance sales targets with deep emotional intelligence and sensitivity.

  • Setup: You run your own limited company and have access to a quiet home-office environment, a computer, a stable internet connection, and a professional headset.

  • Mindset: You enjoy personal responsibility, possess high emotional resilience, and are driven by the opportunity to influence your own earnings.

About Fenix Funeral Agency

Fenix is a modern, innovative funeral agency dedicated to making the planning and execution of a funeral simpler, more transparent, and more secure for the bereaved. As part of our external sales team, you will have the opportunity to make a real difference when people need it most. We prioritize human well-being and provide warm, empathetic, and professional service during one of life’s most emotional moments.

Through our wide range of services—from funeral arrangements to legal matters—we create a personalized experience for every client. At Fenix, you get a deeply meaningful assignment in an organization that values care, accessibility, and innovation.

Our service that we provide in UK you will find on our webb.

Welcome to Fenix – where you help people through grief while growing in your professional role.

Project details

The project focuses on building an AI-powered platform that enables production-grade LLM agents for

complex audit workflows. It combines intelligent agents, evaluation pipelines, and observability tooling to

continuously improve quality, reliability, performance, and cost eﬃciency in production. We're looking for an

experienced engineer with strong data engineering and AI systems expertise to build the infrastructure that

evaluates, monitors, and optimizes AI agents at scale. You'll work across backend services, data pipelines,

analytical databases, and agent architecture, designing systems for evaluation, experimentation, logging,

tracing, and debugging. Many of the challenges involve building reliable infrastructure around

non-deterministic AI systems with no established blueprint to follow. You should be comfortable working in

complex backend environments, making sound architectural decisions, and delivering scalable solutions

that help production AI systems continuously improve.

Key responsibilities

You'll help design, build, and operate the infrastructure that supports our production AI agents, with a strong

emphasis on data platforms, evaluation, observability, and continuous optimization. Your responsibilities will

include:

  • Developing online and oﬄine evaluation frameworks for LLM agents using benchmark datasets, ground-truth labels, human feedback, and experimental results.
  • Implementing automated validation pipelines that verify changes to prompts, models, context, and agent behavior before deployment.
  • Investigating large-scale execution logs and agent traces to uncover quality issues, performance bottlenecks, reliability problems, and opportunities to reduce inference costs.
  • Designing and maintaining data solutions built on analytical databases and column-oriented storage technologies such as BigQuery, ClickHouse, or comparable platforms.
  • Building systems for long-term storage, replay, and analysis of production agent activity to support debugging and continuous improvement.
  • Creating observability capabilities, including monitoring, trace inspection, logging, dashboards, and debugging tools for AI services.
  • Contributing directly to the backend platform and agent ecosystem by enhancing existing AI agents and developing new capabilities when required.

Requirements

  • Solid experience developing backend applications in Python or similar server-side technologies.
  • Confident writing advanced SQL queries and working with large-scale datasets.
  • Experience in deploying and maintaining cloud-based applications, preferably on Google Cloud Platform.
  • Experience designing and implementing data pipelines, ETL/ELT processes, streaming systems, or production feedback loops.
  • Familiarity with analytical databases, data warehouses, columnar storage solutions, and processing high-volume event or trace data.
  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, observability, monitoring, logging, debugging, and the trade-oﬀs involved in building reliable software.
  • Ability to quickly navigate complex codebases and gain a deep understanding of existing architectures.
  • Senior engineering judgment by making sound architectural decisions, evaluating technical trade-oﬀs, and building solutions that are easy to maintain and extend.
  • Ability to work in ambiguous environments, approach problems from first principles, and enjoy building infrastructure that powers production AI systems.

Nice-to-haves

  • Hands-on experience developing infrastructure for LLM-powered applications or AI agents, including prompt optimization, model selection, context management, or inference optimization.
  • Experience analyzing production traces from distributed applications.
  • Building internal developer platforms or tooling for engineering, operations, or business teams.
  • Experience with workflow orchestration platforms such as Temporal, Airflow, or similar technologies.
  • Familiarity with highly regulated industries such as finance, compliance, risk, or audit.
  • Previous experience working in an early-stage startup or another fast-paced engineering environment.

Job Description Summary

We are seeking a Director to lead AIS ISC Digital & AI Capabilities, the AI, analytics, and data organization within the AIS Integrated Supply Chain.

This leader-of-leaders role will oversee a team of approximately 18, including Digital Leads, Product Owners, and Data Governance specialists, supporting five core supply chain processes: Market to Order, Forecast to Plan, Source to Pay, Plan to Produce, and Produce to Deliver.

You will own the overall digital and analytics roadmap, ensuring governed KPI products, consistent data definitions, strong data governance, and trusted data foundations that enable business teams to self-serve analytics and AI solutions.

A key priority will be leading Heartbeat, a unified SQDC analytics product designed to replace 500+ fragmented operational reports with a single, drillable source of truth integrated into daily management systems.

While your teams will build and own the governed KPI products, you will remain hands-on and technically credible, able to address complex cross-process analytics, executive requests, and emerging business needs.

Job Description


Responsibilities


Lead the Organization

  • Lead leaders. Select, develop, and grow four Digital Leads and a Data Governance Lead, with full accountability for the capability, performance, succession, and bench strength of the whole organization – Product Owners and Data Stewards included.
  • Hold the bar through your leads. Ensure the review standard for SQL, semantic models, and metric logic is real in every pillar – sampling the work often enough to know, without becoming the bottleneck.
  • Build ownership, not dependency. Develop your Digital Leads’ direct relationships with their process owners and executives; measure your success by how well the organization operates without you.

Own the Capabilities Portfolio – Analytics and AI

  • One portfolio. Own a single Capabilities roadmap spanning both the certified analytics and data products and the AI capabilities built on them – agentic AI, digital twin, predictive, simulation and optimization, and generative – built from the five pillar roadmaps, synchronized with segment and region priorities and agreed with the Global Process Owners – not a collection of separate backlogs.
  • Make trade-offs explicit. Allocate capacity across pillars, arbitrate when demand exceeds it, and state clearly what the organization will not take on, and why.
  • Protect the balance between running certified products, improving them, and building new capability.

Deliver the Single Source of Truth

  • Own the goal. Consolidate the Heartbeat Bowler KPIs (L0–L4) into one certified source of truth connected to daily management systems – the organization’s reason to exist.
  • Lead Factory Heartbeat. Deliver the unified PSQDC analytics product – single drillable dashboard, integrated action tracking linked to problem solving, real-time data – and drive the disciplined retirement of the fragmented reporting it replaces.
  • Advance the Digital Framework maturity. Move each process from Organized to Digitized to Connected, with certified foundational data products as the gate – and report that maturity honestly to the business.

Run the Hub, Enable the Spokes

  • Own the fundamentals only the hub can own. Certified data products, one agreed definition per KPI, approved data connectors, platform standards, and certification – the non-negotiables that make everything built on top trustworthy.
  • Make the platform self-service. Publish certified products as documented, discoverable, consumable components – through Digital Compass and the data marketplace – so business users across segments, sites, and functions build their own analyses, reports, and AI use cases on trusted foundations, without a ticket queue.
  • Set the certified / experimental boundary. Define what self-built, experimental work may touch versus what production and executive use requires – and provide the path for a spoke-built prototype to graduate into a hub-certified product.
  • Grow fluency in the spokes. Scale data and AI capability in the business through enablement, training, and communities of practice – platform adoption, not consumption of your team’s time, is the measure of success.

Own Data Governance and KPI Arbitration

  • Direct data governance. Through the Data Governance Lead and Data Stewards: documentation, validation, quality monitoring, correction of bad data, and publication of validated datasets to Digital Compass.
  • Arbitrate across pillars. Act as the escalation point for KPI definitions and cross-pillar decomposition – metrics such as On-Time Delivery and Past Due Backlog span the entire supply chain – and ensure every KPI has one agreed definition and a named accountable owner.
  • Assign Data Owners deliberately. Per the organization’s design principles, place the Data Owner role with the most knowledgeable person within the Digital Lead and Product Owner group – ownership follows knowledge, not hierarchy.
  • Partner with CDAO on the enterprise governance, data platform, and data marketplace layer.

Operate the Ways of Working

  • Wire analytics into the operating model. Sub-process owners own standard work; KPI owners own standard bowlers; your organization certifies the numbers behind both – so that DMS runs on governed data, not local extracts.
  • Run one front door. New process requirements raised in DMS flow through the single digital intake into the Capabilities roadmap – partner with the Transformation Programs pillar on intake, scoring, stage gates, value tracking, and adoption cadence.
  • Partner across the pillars. Work as one team with Digital Core for Business on process taxonomy (P1–P4), standard work, master data operationalization, and PLM/ERP alignment, so data definitions and process definitions never diverge.
  • Show up in the business. Hold standing relationships with the five Global Process Owners and with segment and region leadership; represent Capabilities in executive operating mechanisms including the Monthly Operating Review – in the room with a point of view, not a report.

Deliver the AI Capabilities Portfolio

  • AI capabilities are products of this organization. The agentic AI factory, digital twin, forecasting, simulation and optimization, and generative capabilities are part of the Capabilities portfolio you own – managed with the same roadmap, certification, and ownership discipline as the data products, not as side projects.
  • Sequence AI behind certified data. Own the foundational datasets – documented, validated, published – on which AI use cases are built, and hold that line when delivery pressure arrives.
  • Scale the AI factory hub-and-spoke. The hub certifies data connectors, agent standards, and ownership under one interface; the spokes build agents and use cases on them – govern grassroots AI energy without extinguishing it.
  • Advance the capability curve. From descriptive analytics through predictive, simulation and optimization, digital twin, and generative and agentic capabilities – toward a connected, intelligent enterprise in which people always own the decisions.
  • Embed AI-enabled ways of working across your own organization first, and scale what works to the spokes.


Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Data Science, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Engineering, or a related quantitative field.
  • Strong professional experience in analytics, data, or supply chain, including 5+ years leading analytics or data teams and experience leading leaders (managing managers or team leads).
  • Hands-on SQL and modern BI – able to pull and transform data and build an analysis independently, and to review and challenge query logic, semantic models, and metric calculations across multiple teams.
  • Track record of owning an enterprise analytics portfolio and roadmap end to end, agreed with senior business stakeholders across functional boundaries.
  • Experience establishing KPI hierarchies, definitions, and ownership models across functions, and arbitrating metric disputes between domains.
  • Working knowledge of data governance – definitions, data quality management, stewardship, and metadata practices – including operationalizing governance through dedicated roles.
  • Experience partnering with senior operational leadership in executive operating mechanisms, and influencing without authority in a global, matrixed organization.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep domain expertise in two or more supply chain process areas – logistics, manufacturing, sourcing, planning, or order execution.
  • Applied experience with AI and machine learning in an enterprise setting, including LLM / GenAI and agentic tooling, and responsible AI practices.
  • Experience with cloud data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, AWS Redshift, Snowflake, or Azure Synapse, and with enterprise systems such as Kinaxis, SAP, or Oracle Fusion.
  • Experience consolidating a fragmented reporting landscape into certified data products, including the retirement of legacy reporting.
  • Experience operating a hub-and-spoke or federated analytics model – building self-service data platforms, enablement programs, or communities of practice that scale capability beyond the central team.
  • Lean / Six Sigma or equivalent process improvement background; familiarity with tiered daily management systems (DMS).

What We Look For

  • Builds leaders, not dependencies – measures success by how well the organization runs without them, and develops Digital Leads who could hold this seat one day.
  • Technically credible – still writes SQL and builds their own analysis, which is what makes their review of the organization’s work land.
  • Decisive on trade-offs – says what the organization will not do, and why, to the business – one roadmap, not five backlogs.
  • Protects foundations – holds the line on certification, documentation, and stewardship when delivery pressure arrives; sequences AI behind trusted data.
  • Platform builder, not report factory – measures success by what the business builds self-service on certified foundations, not by the size of the central queue.
  • Scales what works – turns one pillar’s practice, one site’s initiative, one flagship product into the system – federating energy rather than centralizing it away.

Job description:

Revenue Cycle Manager

The Revenue Cycle Manager will serve as a hands-on player-coach, overseeing billing, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and financial operations for ABA Therapy Partners. This role is ideal for a strategic, solutions-oriented leader who can manage day-to-day operations while identifying opportunities to streamline workflows, improve accuracy, strengthen collections, and reduce manual processes through automation and scalable solutions. The successful candidate will bring a strong understanding of revenue cycle best practices, billing requirements, authorization processes, and reimbursement rules for California regional centers, school districts, and insurance payers. Reporting directly to the CEO, this individual will play a key role in strengthening financial processes, improving revenue performance, and building the operational infrastructure needed to support the company’s continued growth.

Key Responsibilities

1. Process Improvement

  • Process Mapping: Document every finance workflow end to end (session data to invoice to payment to cash to month-end close) with clear owners, inputs, outputs, deadlines, and handoffs.
  • Find and Fix Friction: Identify bottlenecks, rework, duplicate entry, and error sources. Prioritize fixes by impact on the business.
  • Automation: Lead automation across billing, AR, AP, and reporting using our systems (HiRasmus, Lumary, Rippling, Quickbooks, Google Workspace) and other tools as needed.
  • Standard Operating Procedures: Write and maintain SOPs and checklists so any team member can be trained to run each process the same way every time.
  • Controls: Build in checks that catch errors before they reach a client or vendor, with clear separation of duties and approval rules.
  • Continuous Improvement: Set baselines, track improvement, and report what changed each quarter.

2. Billing

  • Billing Cycle: Lead the monthly billing cycle for all clients we directly invoice, including Regional Centers and School Districts. Work directly with outsourced billing partners to drive prompt and accurate insurance client billing and collections.
  • Data Integrity: Partner with the appointment rendering and scheduling teams so the data used for billing is clean and complete before billing begins. Close the gaps that cause unrendered or unbilled sessions.
  • Client Billing: Convert documented sessions and session notes into invoices based on authorized hours, rates, and codes (e.g., regional center Purchase of Service agreements and school district contracts and IEPs).
  • Invoice Submission: Manage submissions according to each client's requirements, and resolve discrepancies or denials quickly.

3. Accounts Receivable and Collections

  • AR Management: Own the AR aging, follow up on overdue invoices, and drive down days sales outstanding (DSO), regardless of payer source or billing method.
  • Cash Application: Post incoming payments accurately in our Practice Management system and reconcile them to invoices.
  • Denials and Disputes: Track root causes of short pays, denials, and disputes, and fix the process upstream so they don't repeat.
  • Outsourced Billing Partners: Own the relationship to drive partnership, data integrity, clean claims, prompt payment and collections.
  • Self Pay / Patient Responsibility: Work with families in a professional, respectful manner to establish payment plans and otherwise collect on copays, coinsurance and other patient responsibility items.

4. Accounts Payable

  • Vendor Payments: Manage vendor setup, invoice intake, approvals, and payments on a predictable schedule, meeting vendor payment terms.
  • Approval Workflow: Enforce spending approval thresholds and documentation, and keep AP clean for audits.
  • Spend Visibility: Track recurring spend and subscriptions. Identify savings opportunities.

5. Finance Operations

  • Monthly Financial Rhythm: Define and run a monthly calendar for billing, collections, payment posting, AP, reconciliations, and close.

  • Cash Management: Monitor cash position weekly and keep leadership 60 days ahead of cash needs.
  • Audit and Compliance: Keep billing and payment records audit-ready and aligned with client contracts and expectations, and funder rules.

6. Analysis, Forecasting, and Reporting

  • KPI Reporting: Produce weekly and monthly finance scorecards: billed vs. authorized hours, unrendered sessions, collection rate, DSO, AR aging, AP aging, cash position, and margin by client and school district.
  • Forecasting: Build and maintain rolling revenue, cash flow, expense and net income forecasts. Update them as placements, rates, and staffing levels change.
  • Budgeting: Support the annual budget and forecasts, and track actual performance against it.
  • Business Analysis: Analyze profitability by client, district, and service line, model the impact of rate changes and new contracts, and support pricing and growth decisions.
  • Ad Hoc Analysis: Answer leadership's financial questions quickly with clear, data-centered analysis.

7. Team Leadership and Collaboration

  • Supervision: Lead billing and finance specialists, providing training, feedback, and clear workflows.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with clinical operations, scheduling, HR, and leadership so finance processes fit the realities of the business.

  • California Regional Center and School District Billing: Minimum of 3 years of experience billing California Regional Centers under the Department of Developmental Services (DDS) and 3 years of experience with school district billing. Demonstrated knowledge of authorization verification, unit-based billing, documentation requirements, reimbursement rules, and billing compliance. Experience with insurance billing and the Self-Determination Program (SDP) is preferred.

  • Systems and Technology: 3+ years experience with accounting, billing, payer portals and practice-management systems. Familiarity with Lumary and Rippling is preferred. Experience with Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies is a plus.

Job Description:

The Orthopedics Clinical Lead brings deep hands-on experience in outpatient orthopedics and musculoskeletal care delivery and practice operations to guide product development, implementation, and sales. This role serves as a clinical subject matter expert responsible for ensuring orthopedic, physical therapy, and occupational therapy workflows are clinically appropriate, operationally effective, and aligned with patient safety and regulatory expectations. The successful applicant will partner closely with product management, design, and development teams to ensure our healthcare IT solutions reflect real-world clinical musculoskeletal workflows, orthopedic device integrations, and operational realities. Furthermore, this individual will collaborate directly with implementation and sales teams to support client onboarding, product positioning, and clinical alignment during the commercial cycle.
  • Represent real-world outpatient musculoskeletal care delivery models, workflows, and operational practices within orthopedic surgery, sports medicine, physical therapy, and occupational therapy settings.
  • Engage orthopedic surgeons, sports medicine physicians, nurse practitioners, physicians assistants, physical therapists, occupational therapists, clinical assistants, and practice administrators through site visits, workshops, discovery sessions, and virtual engagements.
  • Serve as a trusted specialty advisor during product discovery, validation, and prioritization activities.
  • Provide practical insight into specialty-specific workflows including examination and evaluation, diagnostic imaging, injection and in-office procedure documentation, fracture care, surgery planning, post-operative rehabilitation pathways, physical & occupational therapy, etc.
  • Translate musculoskeletal regulatory, operational, and clinical requirements—for example 90-day surgical global period tracking, therapy cap limitations, and prior authorization rules—into clear, actionable guidance for product management, design, and engineering teams.
  • Support cross-functional alignment by clearly communicating orthopedics and rehabilitation therapy requirements to technical and non-technical audiences, including sales and implementation.
  • Lead musculoskeletal-focused discussions, addressing workflow, compliance, and operational considerations with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Travel to customer and partner sites as needed to support field engagement and product discovery.
  • Perform other duties that support the overall objective of the position.

Education Required:

  • Required: Clinical degree and active or prior clinical licensure/certification in a healthcare profession relevant to the specialty area (e.g., Advanced Practice Provider, RN, PharmD, LCSW, PsyD, PT, OT, or equivalent clinical credential).
  • Required: Clinical degree and active or prior clinical licensure/certification in a musculoskeletal or sports medicine profession (e.g., Doctor of Medicine [MD] or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine [DO] specializing in Orthopedics or Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation [PM&R] or related specialty, Physician Assistant [PA], or Advanced Practice Provider [NP/APRN], Physical Therapist [PT], Occupational Therapist [OT], or equivalent clinical credential.
  • Preferred: Advanced degree in healthcare, clinical informatics, healthcare administration, public health, business, or related field.

    Note: Or any combination of education and experience which would provide the required qualifications.

Experience Required

  • Minimum of 5 years of direct clinical, care delivery, or practice operations experience within an outpatient orthopedics, physical medicine, or sports medicine setting required.
  • Demonstrated deep understanding of the unique clinical workflows, documentation needs, and progress-tracking requirements across outpatient physical therapy (PT) and occupational therapy (OT) disciplines
  • Experience using ambulatory orthopedic or rehab therapy EHR systems in active clinical or operational workflows required.
  • Experience engaging directly with orthopedic providers, rehab therapists, cast technicians, and operational leaders in real-world practice environments, from front office through surgical leadership.
  • Experience collaborating with or advising product, design, or technology teams in a healthcare environment is preferred.

License/Certification Required

  • Active or previously active clinical licensure/certification in a musculoskeletal, orthopedic, or rehab therapy discipline (e.g., MD/DO, PA-C, NP, RN, PT, OT, or ATC).

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


Knowledge Of:

  • Specialty-specific orthopedic and rehab workflows, including physician-led surgical planning, joint-specific physical exams (e.g., ROM, special tests), therapist-led SOAP evaluations, and therapeutic exercise flowsheets.
  • In-office procedure workflows such as joint injections, fracture reduction, casting/splinting, and DMEPOS (Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics, and Supplies) dispensing.
  • Integration of imaging studies (e.g., X-ray, MRI, ultrasound reports) and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) (e.g., KOOS, HOOS, DASH, Oswestry Disability Index) within the patient chart.
  • Healthcare documentation standards, surgical and physical therapy regulatory reporting (including timed CPT codes, 8-minute rule, and GP/GO modifiers), and compliance requirements (e.g., MIPS, value-based care).

Skill In:

  • Communicating complex musculoskeletal clinical and operational concepts (such as global surgical billing and therapy compliance) to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Facilitating discussions, workshops, and feedback sessions with orthopedic surgeons, physical/occupational therapists, and practice managers.
  • Translating specialized musculoskeletal workflows (such as anatomical joint injection mapping, longitudinal ROM tracking, and therapist goal banks) into structured product design inputs.
  • Influencing product decisions through domain credibility, clinical expertise, and real-world musculoskeletal care insight.

Ability To:

  • Establish trust and credibility with orthopedic providers, rehabilitation therapists, and clinic administrators.
  • Engage and influence diverse stakeholder groups across various roles and environments.
  • Adapt communication style to clinical, operational, technical, mission-driven, and complex settings.
  • Work effectively in a cross-functional product environment.
  • Travel may be required up to 25%.

Humana is seeking a Lead Kubernetes Architect to lead the architecture, engineering standards, and lifecycle strategy for enterprise Kubernetes platforms, with a primary focus on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). The Lead Kubernetes Architect will partner across Cloud Engineering, Security, Network, Platform, SRE, DevOps, and application teams to define Kubernetes reference architectures, establish platform best practices, guide roadmap execution, and support Day 2 operational excellence. This is a hands-on architecture leadership role for someone who can operate strategically and tactically—shaping standards, solving complex technical issues, mentoring engineers, and driving Kubernetes platform adoption at enterprise scale.

Key Responsibilities


Kubernetes Platform Architecture


  • Lead the architecture, design, and implementation of enterprise Kubernetes platforms across AKS and GKE, from initial planning through production deployment and ongoing lifecycle management.
  • Define and maintain Kubernetes reference architectures, design standards, and reusable platform patterns for secure, scalable, and resilient container hosting.
  • Develop and execute a Kubernetes product maturity roadmap aligned to Humana’s Cloud Platform strategy and business priorities.
  • Design for multi-cluster, multi-region, and highly available deployment models, including failover and disaster recovery considerations where required.

Engineering and Delivery Leadership


  • Lead new Kubernetes platform capabilities from concept through design, build, validation, release, and operational support.
  • Drive adoption of Infrastructure as Code, GitOps, and CI/CD delivery models for Kubernetes platform provisioning and workload enablement.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to onboard applications and build platform capabilities that improve developer experience, security, and operational consistency.
  • Facilitate technical workshops, architecture reviews, roadmap sessions, whiteboarding sessions, and design reviews.

AI/ML, Automation, and Cost Optimization


  • Identify and implement AI and ML-driven enhancements to improve Kubernetes platform operations, accelerate incident detection and remediation, and drive measurable cost reduction and operational efficiencies.
  • Evaluate and apply intelligent automation for capacity forecasting, workload placement, anomaly detection, rightsizing recommendations, and platform performance tuning.
  • Partner with engineering and operations teams to incorporate data-driven insights into platform scaling, utilization management, and service reliability decisions.
  • Define strategies to improve platform efficiency through predictive analytics, automation, and continuous optimization of cluster and workload resources.

Kubernetes Resource Optimization and Capacity Management


  • Lead the optimization of Kubernetes resources, including CPU, memory, storage, node pools, autoscaling policies, and workload scheduling to maximize efficiency and platform performance.
  • Establish and manage capacity planning practices for Kubernetes clusters and supporting network dependencies to ensure adequate performance, scalability, and availability.
  • Monitor and improve cluster utilization, node health, and workload distribution to reduce waste, prevent resource contention, and maintain service stability.
  • Partner with network and platform teams to ensure network stability and reliability, including planning for ingress, egress, load balancing, DNS, traffic management, and cluster networking dependencies.
  • Define proactive thresholds, alerts, and remediation patterns to prevent capacity-related incidents and support reliable growth across AKS and GKE environments.

Security, Reliability, and Governance


  • Establish and enforce Kubernetes best practices across networking, ingress, load balancing, identity and access management, certificate management, pod security, policy controls, and observability.
  • Ensure platform designs align with Humana enterprise standards for cloud onboarding, security, automation, and operational readiness.
  • Drive platform resiliency through auto-scaling, upgrade planning, health monitoring, rollback strategies, and operational guardrails.

Operations and Lifecycle Management

  • Lead troubleshooting and resolution of complex platform issues in real time, including production-impacting incidents and cross-team escalations.
  • Improve platform observability, logging, alerting, and operational readiness using approved enterprise tooling.
  • Contribute to cost optimization strategies for Kubernetes environments, including cluster right-sizing, autoscaling, and non-production optimization practices.

Leadership and Collaboration


  • Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through technical leadership, coaching, and delegation.
  • Provide architectural guidance to application teams, product teams, and cloud engineers deploying containerized workloads.
  • Build strong partnerships with internal stakeholders, vendors, and engineering teams to drive platform adoption and long-term success.
  • Lead technical demonstrations and communicate architecture decisions clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.


Use your skills to make an impact


Required Qualifications


  • 5+ years of experience in software engineering, platform engineering, cloud engineering, or infrastructure engineering.
  • Demonstrated enterprise experience architecting, implementing, and supporting Kubernetes platforms, including AKS, GKE, and/or EKS.
  • Hands-on experience building and deploying cloud infrastructure through CI/CD and Infrastructure as Code in Azure, GCP, or AWS.
  • Experience developing and operationalizing a Kubernetes lifecycle support model, including upgrades, support, reliability, and Day 2 operations.
  • Strong experience with Kubernetes architecture fundamentals, including:Cluster design and provisioningNetworking and ingressLoad balancingRBAC and identity integrationPod security and policy enforcementCertificate and secret managementMonitoring, logging, and troubleshooting
  • Experience optimizing Kubernetes resource utilization, scaling strategies, and cluster capacity management in enterprise environments.

  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and stakeholder communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced hands-on experience with AKS and GKE in large-scale enterprise environments.
  • Experience supporting Day 2 operations for Kubernetes clusters in production.
  • Experience applying AI/ML, predictive analytics, or intelligent automation to cloud operations, cost optimization, observability, or capacity planning.

Description

TripleTen is an EdTech company that designs and runs tech career learning programs for the US and Latin American markets. We’ve been doing it for over five years, teaching complete beginners — people with no prior tech background — through cohort-based programs built on our own platform and curriculum, developed in partnership with Nebius AI. Our team is fully remote and globally distributed, and we serve a large, active student base across both regions.

As a Technical Owner you’ll own every technical decision behind our programs, from the first conversation with a course author to the bug that never reaches a learner. This is a technical partner role, not a coding job: you weigh each decision against cost, time to learner, and bugs shipped, and you lead one engineer who writes autotests. The role is fully remote and full-time, for candidates based outside the US.

What you will do

  • Own each program’s technical setup. Know its environments, services, providers, and autotests, and keep a written map of what each program depends on.
  • Shape new and updated programs. Collect requirements from authors and constraints from product, test the options, and land on a workable trade-off.
  • Replace what no longer fits. Find, cost, and run the switch when a tool, provider, or setup is outdated or too expensive.
  • Manage providers. Compare offers, negotiate terms, and own integrations with external providers.
  • Lead autotest coverage. Set coverage and priorities for the autotest engineer, and write or fix tests yourself when needed.
  • Be our customer to engineering. Write specs with acceptance criteria for automation, API, and platform needs, and chase each one to done.
  • Cut bugs reaching learners. Trace each bug to where it entered, close the gap with a test, check, or process change, and track the trend.

Requirements

Must have

  • End-to-end technical ownership. 3+ years in engineering, QA automation, or technical operations, including choosing a product’s setup and living with the trade-off after launch.
  • Solid mid-level coding. Python and TypeScript/JavaScript, Git, CI, containers, and REST APIs: enough to read unfamiliar code, fix bugs, and write autotests.
  • English for requirements work. Strong enough to run requirements sessions and write specs engineering teams accept without a round of questions.

Nice to have

  • Leading engineers. Leading or mentoring at least one engineer, ideally in test automation.
  • EdTech and content validation. LMS or autograded courses, QA or release work, or agents that check content for accuracy and freshness.
  • Automation and data stack. Claude Code, MCP, n8n or Make; SQL and dashboards.

What we can offer you

  • Ownership. Real decision-making power in your area: we trust your expertise and don’t micromanage.
  • Remote and flexible. Fully remote collaboration
  • Digital office. Slack, Notion, Miro, and Zoom, with every license you need.

excerpt: ESQlabs is an innovative, internationally active Contract Research Organization (CRO) and a global leader in the development and application of the Open Systems Pharmacology (OSP) Suite.
description:
ESQlabs is an innovative, internationally active Contract Research Organization (CRO) and a global leader in the development and application of the Open Systems Pharmacology (OSP) Suite. We combine mechanistic modeling, Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetics (PBPK) and Quantitative Systems Pharmacology (QSP), with software and training to support Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) and Next-Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) for pharmaceutical, chemical, and academic partners worldwide. Our mission is to empower life sciences: helping scientists understand mechanisms of disease and chemical toxicity to optimize individualized, safer, and more efficient treatment and testing strategies.

As a scientific consultancy serving regulated industries, the quality and traceability of our work are central to our value proposition. We are now extending that discipline from documents and reports to software: we are building an automated, AI agent-orchestrated platform for regulated modeling workflows, and we need it to be qualifiable from the first step, rather than validated retrospectively.

About the Role

You build the quality function for a platform that will be certified, not just validated. You own the quality management system, the validation approach for an agent-orchestrated scientific system, the test plan and test reports, and the traceability from requirement to design to test to record. You define the standards; the platform engineers implement them. You report to the CEO, and you start with an interim consultant already in place and a build team that has written its first requirements and glossary.

You Will

  • Own the quality management system and lead its certification (ISO 9001 first; information security and AI management standards follow), designed as one integrated system.

  • Own validation of the platform under GAMP 5 second edition and computer software assurance: requirements with stable identifiers, test plan, test reports, traceability, supplier assessment.

  • Define and govern the boundary for AI: where a language model may draft, where it may never execute, what evidence every automated step must leave behind, and when the system may run without a human in the loop.

  • Own the certification framework for our analyses: reference case sets, conformance testing, the certificate register and its lifecycle, hosting of independent audits.

  • Run internal audits and corrective actions, advise scientific teams on ICH M15 deliverables, and track AI regulation (EU AI Act, FDA and EMA guidance) into practical requirements.

What You Bring

  • A software background: you have shipped code and can read a repository, a test suite and a CI pipeline without translation. This is the single most important requirement.

  • Several years of quality management or computerized system validation in a regulated setting (CRO, pharma, biotech, medical software), with working knowledge of GAMP 5, ALCOA+, 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11.

  • Experience taking an organization through at least one certification audit (ISO 9001 or ISO/IEC 27001), from certification body selection to closure of findings.

  • A working understanding of how language model agents behave in practice (tool calling, non-determinism, prompt injection) and the ability to explain to an auditor how a system with deterministic and non-deterministic parts is qualified.

  • Fluent English, independent working in a remote cross-cultural team, and a pragmatic way with scientists. German and lead auditor or lead implementer training are a plus.

What's in store for you

The dynamic team behind ESQlabs unites people with different backgrounds, spanning disciplines like pharmaceutical sciences, physics, bioinformatics, mathematics, data science, and software engineering. Our trust in each other, our open-mindedness, and our constant quest for excellence and innovation unite us. We value flat hierarchies, where everyone can contribute ideas and expertise to develop the best product. We are passionate, always willing to broaden our horizons, and love our start-up culture.

You will also benefit from:

  • Flexible work hours and a home office policy that focuses on people and not on numbers

  • An attractive remuneration package

  • Regular in-person team gatherings at locations across Europe.

  • The opportunity to define what quality assurance means for agentic scientific software, at a point when the standard is still being set.

  • A dedicated budget for education programs and conferences you can attend

  • A working environment in which your contribution will make a difference, and that allows you to take ownership of projects and processes

  • Responsibility, autonomy, participation, and career perspective

About us

We collaborate with global corporations in the pharma and chemical industry, as well as start-ups in the life-science technology sector and academic and non-profit research institutions. We define new standards in pharmacometrics and systems pharmacology and toxicology areas. Our software and model platforms help scientists understand mechanisms of diseases and chemical toxicity to optimize individualized treatment of patients and protect the health of the animal and human life.

ESQlabs has attracted international players as sponsors for the OSP Software development. In addition, funding through national and EU-wide research grants allows us to develop our core technologies continuously.

For more information about our culture, values and benefits visit our Unique career opportunities - esqLABS GmbH.

ESQlabs is an equal-opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of background, and value the diversity of perspectives this brings to our team.

At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe.

Job Summary

The Insider Threat Investigator will contribute to the development, execution, and continuous improvement of Jabil’s global Insider Threat Program. The investigator will identify, assess, investigate, and help mitigate insider risks that could affect Jabil’s people, intellectual property, sensitive information, facilities, technology, operations, and reputation. This role requires a practical, prevention-focused approach that combines investigative skill, risk analysis, and sound business judgment. The investigator will work across a global manufacturing environment and collaborate with Security, Cybersecurity, Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, and business leaders while protecting confidentiality, employee privacy, and investigative integrity.


Job Description

The Insider Threat Investigator will receive and evaluate indicators of potential insider risk, conduct preliminary inquiries and assigned investigations, preserve evidence, and develop objective findings and recommendations. Matters may involve intellectual property or trade secret theft, unauthorized disclosure, fraud, misuse of systems or data, cybersecurity incidents, conflicts of interest, foreign influence or elicitation concerns, and other conduct that may create material risk to the company.

The investigator will gather and analyze information from authorized sources; review relevant security, human resources, compliance, and business records; conduct or support interviews; preserve evidence; identify information gaps; and maintain accurate and defensible case documentation. The investigator will work closely with cybersecurity and digital forensics analysts to obtain, interpret, and preserve technical evidence from SIEM and SOAR platforms, endpoint and network security tools, access-control systems, audit logs, authentication records, and other authorized sources.

The role will distinguish anomalous activity from legitimate business conduct by considering the employee’s role, access, relevant context, potential risk indicators, and corroborating information. The position will conduct and support risk assessments involving personnel, facilities, information systems, data, supply chains, third parties, and operations. The investigator will help determine scope and potential impact, develop proportionate mitigation options, monitor corrective actions, and prepare reports, case summaries, trend analyses, metrics, and briefings for program leadership and appropriate stakeholders.

The investigator will coordinate with relevant internal functions and may support engagement with law enforcement, government agencies, outside counsel, or other external partners when directed. All work must comply with applicable law, privacy requirements, records-handling standards, and strict need-to-know controls.

The role will also contribute to program development through research, policy and procedure updates, reporting pathways, awareness and training materials, case-management practices, exercises, audit and compliance responses, and lessons learned. Occasional domestic and international travel may be required for investigations, site reviews, training, audits, and stakeholder engagement.


Education/Experience Requirements

A bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, security management, intelligence studies, risk management, cybersecurity, business, law, or related field is preferred. The candidate should have relevant experience in corporate security, insider threat or insider risk, investigations, intelligence, national security, risk management, cybersecurity, law enforcement, compliance, audit, fraud, or a closely related discipline.

The successful candidate must demonstrate strong investigative, analytical, critical-thinking, interviewing, report-writing, and risk-assessment skills. Familiarity with both physical security and cybersecurity principles is required, along with the ability to collaborate with cybersecurity and digital forensics professionals and interpret technical evidence relevant to an investigation. The candidate must be highly organized, able to manage multiple sensitive matters, exercise discretion and sound judgment, and maintain complete, accurate, and secure case files.

Desired experience includes working with legal departments and law enforcement, participating in multidisciplinary investigative teams, responding to audit or compliance requirements, and handling confidential, proprietary, restricted, or classified information is preferred. Experience protecting intellectual property, trade secrets, engineering data, customer or employee information, manufacturing processes, or other high-value assets in a global manufacturing, technology, supply-chain, defense, or similarly complex environment is highly desirable. Relevant certifications or professional training in investigations, fraud, security, cybersecurity, intelligence, risk, compliance, or project management are valued.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

KIRA is building a AI Stockbroking Superapp for Southeast Asia across payments, remittance, insurance, wealth, and trading.

These products move real money. Reliability, regulatory requirements, and third-party financial rails are fundamental to the product - not considerations around the edges.

The Technical Product Manager owns a product vertical end-to-end, from strategy and outcomes through technical design, delivery, and launch.

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where AI genuinely improves an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted.

What You'll Own

  • Owning a product vertical end-to-end, including strategy, metrics, roadmap, priorities and delivery.

  • Shaping technical design with engineering across APIs, data flows, ledgering, reconciliation, failure handling, security and scalability.

  • Driving trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability, regulatory requirements and user experience.

  • Building regulatory requirements into the product across KYC, transaction monitoring, limits, privacy and licensing.

  • Applying AI where it improves outcomes, with clear evaluation, safeguards, human oversight and failure handling.

  • Shipping products around external dependencies, including regulatory approvals, financial rails and third-party partners.

  • Aligning Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance around clear product decisions and launch requirements.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of complex technical products from strategy through production.

  • Strong technical foundation across system architecture, APIs, databases, workflows, failure modes and distributed systems.

  • Experience working closely with engineers and ability to review, challenge and contribute to technical designs.

  • Experience in payments, banking, remittance, insurance, trading or another regulated, high-consequence product domain.

  • Strong product judgment and ability to make difficult trade-offs under technical, regulatory and operational constraints.

  • Experience building with LLMs or AI products, including evaluation, reliability and understanding when AI should not be used.

Nice to have

  • Engineering or highly technical product background.

  • Experience building zero-to-one fintech or consumer products.

  • Experience defining evaluation frameworks for ML or LLM-powered products.

Outcome

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

Partnering with Franchise, Commercial, Customer, RGM, Marketing, Finance, Supply Chain, Field Operations, and bottler leaders, the role brings fragmented capabilities into one execution architecture with clear decision rights, standards, routines, and accountability. What You'll Do for Us

  • Design the future-state operating model. Establish a future-ready vision and one-to-three-year plans for commercial execution excellence. Define and align decision rights, governance, roles, routines, escalation paths, and accountability across Franchise Operations, Commercial, Customer, RGM, Finance, Marketing, Supply Chain, Field Operations, and bottler leadership; remove disconnected handoffs.
  • Connect strategy to marketplace execution. Lead the commercial agenda across the total beverage portfolio, translating NAOU category, channel, customer, and geographic priorities into a connected process spanning commercialization, bottler plans, annual execution calendars, field standards, measurement, and corrective action. Translate objectives into transaction and volume plans across channels, geographies, customers, and the bottling system.

  • Experience translating enterprise strategy into connected commercial and field execution plans, incorporating customer requirements, bottler capability, and execution feasibility before deployment.

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The Role

We’re looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to help build and run the fundamental part of Nebius - the Network - the infrastructure everything else depends on. This is an engineering-first SRE role: you’ll set clear reliability targets, build the tooling and automation to meet them, and make the network safer to operate as we scale quickly.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Define and own reliability goals for network services and critical paths (SLIs/SLOs, availability targets, error budgets where it makes sense)
  • Drive reliability improvements across the whole network: not only services, but also site readiness, inter-site connectivity (DCI), and operational standards
  • Own incident response for your areas, lead investigations/postmortems, and turn failures into durable fixes (not repeated firefighting)
  • Build and evolve observability: actionable metrics/logs/traces, alerting, and faster debug loops during and after incidents
  • Design safer change workflows: automation, CI/CD, test/staging environments, canarying, rollbacks, and auditability for network changes
  • Work closely with network engineers and platform teams to embed operability into designs and keep operations practical and fast

We expect you to have:

  • Strong production Linux fundamentals and a structured approach to debugging complex systems
  • Solid understanding of networking basics and how real networks fail (control plane vs data plane, latency/loss, failure domains, etc.)
  • Hands-on experience operating high-availability systems and improving them over time (not just “keeping lights on”)
  • Ability to write and maintain software/automation (Go is common for us; Python is also welcome)
  • Experience with modern infrastructure tooling (e.g., IaC, CI/CD, container platforms) and comfort automating operational workflows

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience with high-throughput traffic processing: load balancers, tunneling/decap, NAT64, or similar datapath-heavy systems
  • Low-level networking performance/debug background (eBPF/XDP, DPDK, perf/ftrace, kernel networking internals)
  • Experience building network-safe delivery pipelines (testing labs, staged rollouts, automated verification, drift detection)
  • Background with large-scale network observability/telemetry (e.g., routing/flow telemetry, regression detection at scale)

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Who we are

Altimate AI provides an expert agentic data engineering harness to automate the work of data teams. These generate data pipelines, write data documentation/tests, and optimize data infrastructure autonomously. In particular they help to automatically reduce the total cost of ownership on Databricks and Snowflake.

Teams using Altimate.ai have seen 3x accelerated data development and up to 30% reduction in cloud data infrastructure costs. Altimate is used by hundreds of companies and thousands of weekly active users. Read more about us in this VentureBeat Article.

We are a Series A startup of 50+ people, distributed across India (mainly Bangalore) and the US. Working here means short deadlines, juggling several things at once, adapting quickly, and making calls without complete information. If you have done marketing at a startup, you will recognize this.

Role summary

Reporting directly to the head of marketing, you will run the execution engine of our marketing team: the systems, the channels, the publishing cadence, and the reporting that tells us what is working.

This is a hands-on role covering the full range of digital marketing mechanics: marketing automation, email, blog publishing, social, events, and reporting. Search/answer-engine visibility, and email outreach/deliverability are two immediate priorities, and we will increase the scope of the role over time based on the skills and interests of the successful candidate along with company priorities.

We are a small team, so we would rather shape the role around what you are good at than hold you to a fixed spec. If you bring depth in something we have not listed (paid acquisition, lifecycle, partner marketing, ABM) we will make room for it if it fits our strategy, and fill the gap elsewhere with contract help or other people on the team.

As an AI-native company, we expect you to work the way we build product: using agentic AI tools, skills, and scheduled automations to scale your own output, and not doing everything by hand.

What you'll own

Marketing systems and automation. HubSpot is our system of record: segments, properties, workflows, forms, campaign tracking, and integrations with the rest of our stack. You will be the primary system owner.

Search and answer-engine visibility (AEO/SEO). On-site and off-site work across and : technical SEO, on-page optimization, structured data, site architecture and internal linking, backlinks and listings, and optimization for AI answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews). Build the measurement that shows whether it is working.

Email and newsletter. Manage the subscription list and opt-in process. Build, schedule, and send a regular newsletter from material our engineering team and contract writer produce. Own hygiene, segmentation, and deliverability. Set KPIs and own the process for meeting them.

Blog publishing and distribution. Get engineering- and writer-authored articles live (Hashnode today, though we may change the publication flow), then build exposure for them: syndication, communities, newsletters, cross-posting.

Social channels. Own our channels day to day. Turn existing long-form content into posts, judge which channels are worth our effort, and grow reach. You are not writing the source material, but you need judgment about what will land where.

Analytics and reporting. Track numbers from GA4, PostHog, Google Search Console, HubSpot, OpenSEO and elsewhere and act on them.

Digital events. Webinars and online events end to end: platform, registration workflow, promotion, reminders, follow-up, reporting.

In-person event logistics. Coordinate our presence at conferences and meetups in North America and Europe — venue and vendor bookings, shipping, schedules, promotion, lead capture, follow-up. We also expect to run occasional events in India (meetups, recruiting events) that you would help promote.

Where this role goes long term

To start off, we are hiring an individual contributor. As the team scales, we expect this role to grow into leading a small team, and we are looking for someone with the ambition and judgment to step up when that happens. If your goal is to stay a pure IC indefinitely, this is not the right fit.

What this role is not

  • Not a content writing role. Our existing team produce the blog posts, newsletter articles, and SEO content. You help project manage and distribute that work; you do not author it.

  • Not a design role. Visual creative is handled elsewhere.

  • Not a product-technical role. You do not need to understand data engineering our product internals to do this job well, but a demonstrated familiarity with software development and data engineering would be a big plus.

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years in digital marketing, 6 preferred, with meaningful time in startups or small multi-channel marketing teams.

  • Hands-on ownership of a marketing automation tools: configuring it, not just working inside something someone else built.

  • Email marketing infrastructure experience: selecting or implementing an ESP, migrating a contact database, building a compliant opt-in flow, and diagnosing genuine deliverability problems. Just sending campaigns inside an already-healthy system is not the same thing.

  • Technical SEO you have done yourself: schema, site architecture, crawl and index health — plus a current, practical point of view on AEO.

  • Self-sufficiency in the tools: GA4, Google Search Console, HubSpot, Ahrefs/Semrush/OpenSEO or equivalent.

  • Practical fluency with agentic AI tools: specific workflows and automations you have built and run, not general familiarity.

  • Operational reliability. A large part of this job is recurring work that has to happen on schedule and correctly.

Nice to have

  • Paid acquisition experience (Google, LinkedIn, retargeting). We may bring it into scope if you have it

  • Experience marketing to technical or developer audiences, or in the data ecosystem

  • Comfort with a git-based publishing flow (markdown, pull requests)

  • Light editing of technical content written by others

  • Experience briefing and managing external agencies or contractors

Logistics
